description:
Surfaced during the funding-chip work (PRs #1091, #1105). Results-explorer
e2e tests intermittently fail with `No result found for "<real-id>"` (or a
heading like `TPC-H Results` / `TPC-H - DuckDB` never becoming visible) on a
result id that genuinely exists in the corpus.

Root cause (verified, NOT an id-churn / fixture bug):
  - The id is present. Regenerating the corpus with
    `npm run test:e2e:fixtures` and querying the snapshot shows the row in
    both `bench.results` and `bench.result_detail_metrics`.
  - `queryRows` (results-explorer/src/db.ts) does NOT swallow errors, so this
    is a genuine ZERO-ROW read, not a masked exception, and the snapshot HTTP
    fetch is 200 OK (confirmed from the CI Playwright trace's network log).
  - `getResultDetailMetrics` / the index queries run `WHERE result_id = ?`
    against a cold, partially-fetched HTTP-backed `results.duckdb`. The
    readiness probe `waitForSnapshotRows` / `validateAttachedSnapshot`
    (src/db.ts) only does `SELECT <col> FROM <view> LIMIT 1` per required
    view, which a cold snapshot can satisfy while a keyed lookup on the same
    view still returns nothing.
  - A zero-row detail result is then rendered as a TERMINAL "No result found"
    with no retry (ResultDetail.tsx: `if (data === null) setError(...)`).

Where it bites: the FIRST page load after a fresh build (local ~40s cold vs
~9s warm; warm re-runs 3/3 clean). CI is always cold, so CI is where it shows
— especially the WebKit `@smoke` lane (slowest engine, smoke-only, so its
first test always eats the cold start) and the first snapshot-hitting spec in
the Chromium full suite. Re-running the identical commit passes. A real user
deep-linking a detail URL against a cold CDN cache can hit the same thing.

Key files:
  - results-explorer/src/db.ts — waitForSnapshotRows / SNAPSHOT_READY_SCANS
    (probe is existence-only, not keyed); queryRows (retry wrapper, only
    retries isTransientDuckDbSnapshotError, not a cold zero-row read).
  - results-explorer/src/lib/duckdbQueries.ts — getResultDetailMetrics,
    getPlatformIndexRows (the keyed lookups that come back empty).
  - results-explorer/src/pages/ResultDetail.tsx — renders null as a terminal
    "No result found" with no retry.

Related project memory: project_explorer_cold_snapshot_race. Same
develop-red-from-flakes churn family as the auto-revert misattribution note.
title: Fix results-explorer cold-snapshot zero-row race (keyed lookups return empty on a cold HTTP-backed DuckDB snapshot)

work.evidence: Reproduced deterministically two ways. (a) Unit: fake connections in src/__tests__/snapshotReadiness.test.ts model the exact shapes — unkeyed LIMIT 1 scans answer while keyed WHERE result_id=? returns [], and COUNT(*) reports the true total while the column materializes fewer rows. (b) e2e: with #1340's re-navigation mitigation reduced to a single attempt, the Chromium suite fails reproducibly on Compare/responsive/external-corpus routes — the harness-independent signal
work.notes:
Add a focused test (or a throttled-fetch harness) that attaches a cold
HTTP-backed snapshot and shows `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` on a required view
succeeding while `WHERE result_id = ?` on the same view returns 0 rows in
the same window. This pins the defect independently of wall-clock timing.
work.summary: Reproduce deterministically: force a cold snapshot and assert the keyed-lookup zero-row window

work.evidence: Readiness gating alone is INSUFFICIENT — measured, not assumed. Three progressively stricter gates were each defeated: (1) keyed probe on the last result_id -> Compare still failed on short_ids; (2) completeness (COUNT(*) vs materialized) on results/result_detail_metrics/short_ids -> Compare still failed on the per-query evidence tables; (3) completeness across ALL 8 snapshot tables -> still 3 failures on other routes. Readability is not monotonic per query, so the fix must live at the read: queryRows now re-issues an EMPTY result within a 15s post-attach window (bounded by QUERY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS). Both the strengthened readiness gate and the read-layer retry are kept
work.notes:
Two candidate fixes (pick one, document why in the PR):
(a) Strengthen waitForSnapshotRows to do a keyed probe (or a COUNT that
    cannot be satisfied from metadata) so the DB instance is not exposed
    until keyed lookups resolve; or
(b) Treat a cold zero-row keyed read as transient in getDetailResult /
    getResultDetailMetrics and retry a bounded number of times before
    concluding null, so a real id is never rendered as "No result found"
    during the cold window.
Do NOT weaken the genuine not-found path — an id that truly is absent must
still surface "No result found" promptly.
work.summary: Make the readiness gate keyed, or make a cold zero-row read retryable

work.evidence: Regression coverage: 14 tests in snapshotReadiness.test.ts (keyed-probe, completeness, and shouldRetryColdEmptyRead boundary/attempt/never-attached cases); verified 5 of them fail against pre-fix code. Suite: 844 vitest, 26061 fast lane, typecheck clean. Decisive proof: 3 consecutive Chromium runs fully green with the e2e re-navigation mitigation disabled (single 26s attempt) — the first time that has ever passed. Perf improved: cold init P50 437ms vs 564ms baseline. WebKit/Firefox graduation NOT recommended yet: only Chromium was exercised locally and there is no post-fix CI flake data
work.notes:
Add the w1 repro as a standing regression test. Once green, this unblocks
(or de-risks) graduate-browser-smoke-to-blocking-gates, whose 10-green
criterion this flake was defeating on the WebKit lane.
work.summary: Regression coverage + reassess graduating WebKit/Firefox smoke to blocking

banner above the chart area.

Warning text should explain the implication, not just state the fact.
"Execution mode differs: sql vs dataframe" is insufficient - add

description:
The strategy doc (§ Trust, Visibility, and Ranking) lists the dimensions
on which two results are comparability-breaking. Phase 1 enforces
hard-blocks on benchmark and scale factor mismatch. Execution mode and
tuning mode are also comparability-breaking - a SQL vs DataFrame
comparison or a tuned vs notuning comparison can look like a platform
performance difference when it is actually a configuration difference.

Phase 1 couldn't enforce these because execution_mode and tuning_mode
weren't in the manifest. Once explorer-extend-manifest-and-pipeline
lands, the Compare view can inspect them and warn.

This TODO adds visible warnings (not hard-blocks) when:
  - The two results differ on execution_mode (SQL vs DataFrame)
  - The two results differ on tuning_mode (tuned vs notuning)
  - The two results use different query subsets (full vs partial)

Warnings are prominent (banner at top of compare view) but not blocking -
intentional cross-tuning comparisons are valuable.
preserves: Compare view still renders when warnings are present
Cross-tuning and cross-mode comparisons are allowed (not blocked) - warning is advisory, not preventive
Existing hard-block on benchmark mismatch and scale-factor mismatch - these remain blocking

presenting charts. A benchmark user comparing two or more result bundles needs
an immediate conclusion such as "Polars is faster on 22/22 queries and 3.65x
faster by geomean" plus clear warnings when the selected runs are not directly
comparable. This builds on the existing sticky compare bar and compare route.

Existing `/results/compare?ids=...` URLs continue to load.
The sticky compare bar remains available from benchmark and platform pages.
Warnings do not prevent users from inspecting mismatched selections; they prevent unsupported winner claims.

description:
The current Compare URL format is
`/results/compare?ids=<full_result_id>,<full_result_id>,...`.

Full result IDs average ~40 characters (e.g.,
`tpch-duckdb-sf0.01-20260403-7fe93365`). With 4+ selections plus the
base URL, encoded commas, and any future additional query params, the
URL approaches 2KB. Chrome handles this, but proxies, older browsers,
and CDN caches have been observed to truncate or reject URLs above
1024 bytes. Once the matrix leaderboard ships and users can
one-click-compare 6-8 platforms, this becomes a real failure mode.

This TODO introduces a short-ID scheme: a stable 8-character prefix
of a deterministic hash of the full result_id. The pipeline emits a
lookup table `short_ids.json` mapping short → full; the frontend
resolves both directions.

Collision handling: if two short IDs collide in the active corpus,
the pipeline extends the colliding pair to 10 chars (and so on). This
is logged at build time. At current corpus scale (12 bundles) and
foreseeable scale (hundreds), 8 chars is effectively collision-free,
but the extend-on-collision rule is required for robustness.
preserves: Direct links to /results/r/<full_result_id> remain unchanged - this TODO only affects Compare query params
Existing long-form Compare URLs continue to work - backward compatible
Pipeline remains a single pass - short-ID generation piggybacks on the existing bundle-id enumeration

description:
Source: results-explorer/publication remediation re-review (2026-07-06),
Defect #5 (de-escalated to cosmetic).

results-explorer/index.html:15 sets the CSP via `<meta http-equiv=
"Content-Security-Policy">`, and its content includes `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
Per the CSP spec, `frame-ancestors` is IGNORED when the policy is delivered in
a <meta> element — it is only honoured as an HTTP response header. So that
directive provides no clickjacking protection today; it reads as a control
that does not exist.

This is cosmetic, NOT a security hole: the load-bearing directive
`connect-src 'self'` (which confines all network egress and closes the
duckdb-wasm remote-fetch/exfil channel) DOES work in a meta CSP, and it is
present. The only issue is the misleading inert `frame-ancestors` line.

Fix: drop the inert directive and replace it with a comment stating that
framing/clickjacking protection must be applied as an HTTP response header
(`X-Frame-Options: DENY` or a header-delivered `frame-ancestors`) at the
hosting/CDN layer (GitHub Pages), because meta CSP cannot express it.
preserves: The duckdb-wasm-compatible directives (script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval', worker-src blob:) — removing these would break the explorer.
connect-src 'self' — the load-bearing egress confinement; must not change.

prior_art.concept: _project/DONE/main/planning/remediate-explorer-csp-hardening.yaml — the item that added the CSP; SUPERSEDE its noted 'frame-ancestors inert in meta' caveat by actually removing the directive.
results-explorer/index.html:6-15 — the existing CSP meta + head comment; EDIT in place, preserve all non-frame-ancestors directives.

description:
A fresh-clone or returning developer runs `cd results-explorer && npm run
dev` and is met with a full-screen error wall:

  DuckDB snapshot 'bench.results' is missing required columns: ...
  Regenerate the snapshot via 'benchbox explorer build' or check the
  deployed results.duckdb file.

Root cause is not a code bug — it is an architectural papercut:
  - `*.duckdb` is gitignored, so the snapshot is never tracked.
  - CI rebuilds it on every docs deploy
    (`.github/workflows/docs.yml:103`); local devs never do unless they
    know to.
  - `npm run dev` has no predev step that detects staleness.
  - The runtime guard in `results-explorer/src/db.ts:184-199` correctly
    refuses to render against a snapshot whose schema doesn't match the
    frontend's required-column set — so the user sees a 9-column-diff
    wall the first time the read-model contract bumps.

Because the read-model contract is changing actively (PRs #344, #354,
#380 added eligibility columns in the last 30 days), this wall recurs
every few weeks for every developer.

This TODO closes the recurring DX wall. It is separable from the CLI
surface relocation (TODO `explorer-cli-surface-migration`) and the
schema versioning work (TODO `explorer-read-model-schema-versioning`).

Three solution shapes to evaluate:

  (i)  **`predev` npm script** in `results-explorer/package.json` that
       checks whether `public/data/results.duckdb` is older than the
       most-recent file under `results-data/bundles/`, and rebuilds via
       the canonical entry point if so. Pros: zero new files; works with
       the existing build step. Cons: every `npm run dev` runs an mtime
       check; spawns the Python entry point when rebuilding (3-5s on
       the 528-bundle corpus).

  (ii) **Tiny in-tree dev snapshot** under
       `results-explorer/dev-data/results.duckdb` (5-10 cohorts,
       deterministic), NOT gitignored, that the explorer falls back to
       when `public/data/results.duckdb` is missing. Pros: `git clone
       && npm run dev` works instantly with no Python. Cons: adds a
       tracked binary (~500KB-2MB depending on corpus) that needs
       periodic refresh — but only when the schema bumps, not the data.

  (iii) **`make explorer-dev` wrapper target** that runs rebuild then
       vite. Pros: explicit, documented in Makefile. Cons: requires
       developer to know about and use the make target; doesn't help
       someone who runs `npm run dev` from inside `results-explorer/`.

The right choice depends on how often the schema bumps vs. how often
the data bumps; (ii) optimizes for "schema-stable, data-shifting" and
(i) optimizes for "schema-shifting, data-stable". (iii) is the most
conservative and explicit but doesn't fix the default `npm run dev`
path.
preserves: Browser-fixture generation (`generate-browser-fixtures.mjs`) is unaffected — it has its own snapshot regen.
Production builds (CI docs deploy) continue to use the full corpus, not the dev snapshot or fallback.
`results-explorer/public/data/results.duckdb` semantics are unchanged when present.

description:
The strategy review (2026-04-15) identified that the explorer's current
data model - manifest.json (aggregate only) + details/{id}.json (one file
per result) - cannot support a ClickBench-style Platform × Query matrix
leaderboard without N parallel detail fetches assembled client-side. That
approach is slow, fragile, and silently breaks when platforms run
heterogeneous query subsets.

This TODO introduces a third derived artifact shape emitted by the
explorer pipeline:

    results-explorer/public/data/benchmarks/{benchmark}_sf{sf}_{phase}.json

One file per (benchmark, scale_factor, phase) tuple, containing the full
cross-platform query matrix pre-computed from already-loaded bundles (no
extra I/O - the pipeline already has everything in memory during its
single pass).

Key schema decisions driven by the adversarial review:

1. Key includes **phase** (not just benchmark/scale). The proposal that
   keyed on (benchmark, scale) alone silently collapses power vs
   throughput vs maintenance phases. Making phase part of the filename
   makes the scope of each matrix explicit and URL-addressable.

2. Tuning_mode is a per-platform-row field, not an artifact-level filter.
   Two DuckDB rows with different tuning modes occupy different matrix
   rows; the UI labels them as such.

3. Each row carries `power_score` (for TPC-H/TPC-DS), `geomean_ms`, and
   `cost_usd` so the UI can choose ranking metric per benchmark family
   without a second fetch.

4. Sparse matrices: platforms that ran a subset of queries produce
   `null` in the missing cells, never crash the build.

5. Artifacts are gzipped on write (`*.json.gz`). TPC-DS SF100 with 30
   platforms × 99 queries × throughput streams can reach 200-500KB raw;
   gzip cuts that ~5×. Loader handles both for local dev convenience.
preserves: Existing details/{id}.json per-result pages - detail page consumers must continue to work
Existing manifest.json schema - new artifact is additive; do not remove or reshape manifest fields
ExplorerPipeline.run() remains a single pass over bundles - no extra bundle loads introduced

description:
The 2026-04-15 review identified that `Compare.tsx` fetches N detail
JSON files and recomputes everything per render: per-query speedups
(line 388-393), diverging deltas (DivergingBarChart.tsx:49), normalized
speedups (NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:57), summary-card metrics
(Compare.tsx:219-290), and the breakdown table (Compare.tsx:364-429).

This is the architectural root cause of the parity problem: when the
CLI and explorer compute independently, drift is inevitable. The
parity test infrastructure (`explorer-establish-cli-explorer-parity-tests`)
proves equivalence today but does not eliminate the duplication.

The fix is to push computation into the pipeline. The pipeline already
emits per-`(benchmark, sf, phase)` `BenchmarkSummary` artifacts via
`transformer.py` → `pipeline.py`. Add a parallel `ComparisonArtifact`
emitted per ordered set of result_ids: it carries display_timings,
per-query speedup matrix (one row per (queryId, baselineIdx)),
diverging delta matrix, and pre-disambiguated platform display labels.

Compare.tsx becomes a pure renderer that fetches one artifact and
iterates. The chart components stop computing - they receive
pre-computed numeric arrays.

This work also ports the platform-label disambiguation from
`result_plotter.py:68-149` (driver version, execution mode, scale
factor suffixes) into the artifact, so the explorer no longer renders
ambiguous "DuckDB / DuckDB" rows when two results share a platform name.

Existing `BenchmarkSummary` artifact format and emission - this work adds a parallel artifact, does not modify the summary
Existing `ComparabilityBanner` UI - only the warning generation moves server-side; the component contract is unchanged
Existing `DetailResult` model and per-detail JSON file emission - Compare must still work via the fallback path during rollout

description:
The 2026-04-15 visualization review identified that the Python CLI
(`benchbox/core/visualization/`) and the Preact explorer
(`results-explorer/src/components/`) reimplement the same
visualization math in two languages with **zero shared computation
and zero contract tests**.

Concrete drift surfaces today:
  - Heatmap color: `colorForCell` (QueryHeatmap.tsx:39-45) duplicates
    `textcharts.heatmap` log10-ratio→hue logic.
  - Per-baseline speedup: `NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:57` duplicates
    `textcharts.normalized_speedup` (`baseline / this`).
  - Diverging delta: `DivergingBarChart.tsx:49` duplicates the
    `textcharts.diverging_bar` `(this - baseline) / baseline * 100`
    formula, plus an independent magnitude sort at line 63-67.
  - Per-query "fastest" highlight: Compare.tsx:388-411 inlines its own
    ranking that has no CLI counterpart and disagrees with Compare's
    summary-card definition (see explorer-unify-visualization-foundations
    for the dual-definition bug).

The user requirement is explicit: **"there should be only ONE place
where visualization values are composed, when that is not possible
we must have test infrastructure that ENSURES the parallel
implementations match."** This item builds that test infrastructure.
Centralizing computation server-side is tracked separately
(explorer-emit-comparison-artifact-from-pipeline).

Strategy: Python emits canonical fixtures (input data + expected

description:
The adversarial review (2026-04-15) identified two critical invariants
that must hold before any matrix leaderboard can be meaningful:

**Invariant 1 - Platform identity is separate from provenance/visibility.**
The current pipeline writes whatever string appears in the bundle's
platform.name field directly to manifest.json and details/. In practice
this produces distinct rows for "DuckDB-trust-ci", "DuckDB-trust-community",
"DuckDB-trust-local", etc., even though they are the same engine variant and
the trust information is already captured in the separate trust_label field.
Any cross-platform matrix built on this read model is misleading because the
platform axis is polluted with provenance variants.

Fix: extract a canonical `platform_id` (e.g., "duckdb") alongside the raw
platform name, and define explicit ranking-eligibility rules that gate which
rows may appear in ranked tables.

**Invariant 2 - One canonical display value per logical query.**
The transformer preserves every measurement row (iter, stream) for provenance.
`_geomean_ms()` therefore averages *all* execution samples, including
throughput streams. Meanwhile, Compare.tsx calls `find()` on the queries
array and takes the first row - currently returning 16ms for a query whose
samples are [16, 11, 11, 11] (cold-cache outlier, not representative).

Neither approach is wrong for its stated purpose, but neither is appropriate
as the display value in a comparison matrix. The fix is a canonical reduction:
median of successful measurement runs for each distinct logical query_id,
exposed as `display_ms` per query and `display_geomean_ms` at the result
level. The raw `geomean_ms` is preserved as an audit/detail field.

This TODO does **not** implement the matrix UI or the cohort artifact - it
only fixes the data contracts that every downstream feature depends on.
It replaces the dangling `explorer-extend-manifest-and-pipeline` dependency
that previously blocked `explorer-emit-benchmark-summary-artifact`.

work.notes:
Signature:
  `_query_display_ms(timings: list[QueryTiming], query_id: str) -> float | None`

Algorithm:
  1. Filter to timings where `timing.query_id == query_id`
     AND `timing.status == "pass"`.
  2. From passing timings, select `run_type == "measurement"` rows;
     if none have explicit run_type, accept all.
  3. Compute median of `duration_ms` across the filtered set.
  4. Return None if the filtered set is empty (all failed or query
     not present).

Median is chosen over mean because a single cold-cache outlier
(common in power-test runs that include one warmup iteration before
measurement) should not dominate the display value.

work.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:278 - aria-label uses ms.toFixed(1) (e.g. "10.0 ms")
while the visible cell text uses fmtMs() which emits toFixed(0)
("10 ms").  Screen readers announce a value that differs from what
is displayed.

Fix: use fmtMs(ms) in the aria-label string for consistency.

Also: for the fastest cell (ratio=1.0), the label reads "10 ms, 1.0×
fastest in column" which is grammatically awkward - the cell IS the
fastest, not a comparison to it.  Special-case as "10 ms, fastest in
column" when ratio rounds to 1.0.
work.summary: Align aria-label text with visible cell text for timing values
Replace manual violation-split in axe-helper with configureAxe

work.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:122-149 - handleCellKey handles ArrowLeft/Right/
Up/Down but not Home/End.  The WAI-ARIA 1.2 grid pattern recommends
(not requires) Home to jump to first cell in row and End to last cell
in row, Ctrl+Home to first cell in grid.

Low priority: not a WCAG requirement for read-only data grids.
Worth adding if AT user feedback surfaces the gap.
work.summary: Add Home/End key support to keyboard grid navigation

work.notes:
QueryHeatmap.test.tsx currently renders with no onSelectionChange, so
the checkbox column header (hasSelection=false) is never in the axe
DOM.  The Required fix (w3 in the main TODO) added aria-label to the
empty <th>, but there is no regression test that exercises the
selection path through axe.

Fix: add one axe test case in QueryHeatmap.test.tsx that passes
selectedIds={new Set()} and onSelectionChange={() => {}} so axe runs
against the full grid including the checkbox column header.
work.summary: Add axe test for QueryHeatmap with selection enabled

description:
Redesign the Results Explorer front door and shell so it feels like part of
the BenchBox product rather than a separate light dashboard. The user clarified
that the primary audience is benchmark users choosing a database, while the
leaderboard browser must remain attention-grabbing because it feeds the
submission flywheel. The target frame is therefore:

"BenchBox Database Leaderboards: reproducible rankings for choosing OLAP
platforms by workload, scale, deployment, and normalized cost."

This item covers identity, first impression, first-viewport density, and the
shared BenchBox narrative. It should preserve the existing home
MetaLeaderboard work, but make it the first meaningful content rather than
burying it below generic hero/stat chrome.

The existing `/results/`, `/results/{benchmark}/`, `/results/p/{platform_id}/`, `/results/r/{result_id}`, `/results/compare`, and `/results/query` routes remain stable.

work.notes:
Compare.tsx:196-198 - grouped bar chart uses `?? 0` for null display_ms
values (queries where all runs failed).  Zero-height bars correctly
disappear visually, but the intent is non-obvious: a reader might wonder
if 0 misrepresents failed queries as "fastest."

Fix: add a one-line comment before the `?? 0`:
  // Null means all runs failed; render as 0 so bar disappears rather than
  // crashing the chart formatter.
work.summary: Add comment explaining ?? 0 fallback in Compare.tsx grouped chart

work.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:74 - filter `v > 0` silently excludes timing=0ms
(physically impossible but could occur with rounding artifacts).

Fix: add a comment:
  // Exclude zero/null cells; sub-ms values round to 0 in some runners.
work.summary: Document zero-timing filter intent in QueryHeatmap.tsx

work.notes:
manifest.ts:79-80 - HTML detection uses `contentType.includes("text/html")`.
If a real 5xx error page uses `application/json` content-type, the gzip
DecompressionStream would throw with a cryptic "DecompressionStream error"
rather than a meaningful HTTP error.

Fix: check `!res.ok` first:
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status} fetching ${url}`);
Then proceed to content-type check for Vite SPA fallback detection.
work.summary: Improve getBenchmarkSummary to also check !res.ok before content-type

work.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:272 - lightnessForCell is called unconditionally even
when suppressHeat=true (single-platform view).  The result is immediately
discarded.  This is a negligible waste but could confuse a reader.

  const lightness = suppressHeat ? null : lightnessForCell(ms, minInCol);
work.summary: Suppress lightnessForCell call when suppressHeat is true

anti_patterns.why: linear compresses sub-2x gaps when a 80x outlier is present

approach:
The heatmap is a single component with no internal state beyond
selection. All data comes from the summary prop. Filter controls
live in BenchmarkIndex and drive the (sf, phase) → artifact URL
selection + client-side filtering of rows by tuning/trust.

For coloring: write a pure function colorForCell(ms, minInCol,
maxInCol) → CSSValue. Unit-test it directly with known inputs before
wiring it to the component. The color math is where a proposal most
easily goes wrong; keep it isolated and snapshot-tested.

For the log-ratio color: clamp the ratio at 10x so a 100x-slower
outlier doesn't compress everything else. Values above the clamp
still render red but don't stretch the scale further.
description:
The strategy review (2026-04-15) concluded that the explorer's primary
surface per benchmark must be a Platform × Query matrix leaderboard,
modelled on ClickBench but adapted to BenchBox's multi-dimensional data
(trust tiers, tuning modes, phases). The current BenchmarkIndex.tsx
renders a sorted list - this TODO replaces it with the matrix.

The matrix is the product definition: arriving at /results/tpch/ should
immediately answer "which engine wins, and by how much, on each query?"
without navigating further.

Layout:

  [Scale ▾] [Tuning ▾] [Phase ▾] [Trust ▾]  [View: Matrix | List]

  Platform      Trust    Power/Geomean  Cost   Q1    Q2   ... Q22
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  DuckDB        maintainer   3184.9 / 11.5ms  $0    18ms  4ms  ... 6ms
  Polars        maintainer   --     / 8.2ms   $0    12ms  3ms  ... 4ms
  DataFusion    community    2847.1 / 13.7ms  $0    22ms  6ms  ... 9ms

Heat coloring rules (corrected from the original proposal):

- Per-column normalization (each query independently).
- **Log scale**, not linear - SQLite at 892ms vs DuckDB at 11ms would
  collapse the DuckDB/Polars/DataFusion gradation under linear.
- Scale is **ratio-to-fastest-in-column** (ClickBench-style),
  not min-max.
- Null cells render "-" in muted gray with `aria-label="no data"`.

Row selection: checkboxes on each row feed the existing Compare page
via URL-encoded IDs. See explorer-compare-url-short-ids for the ID
encoding concern.
preserves: BenchmarkIndex list view remains available via a toggle for mobile users
Compare page contract - selection emits URLs the Compare page already understands
Existing /results/:benchmark/ route - do not change URL pattern, only the rendered content
Existing manifest.json consumers - this TODO adds a new loader, does not remove the existing one
title: Build ClickBench-style matrix leaderboard as primary benchmark landing view

work.notes:
The current Compare.tsx calls find() to get the first QueryTiming
row for each query (Compare.tsx:107, :350). This returns the
cold-cache outlier when multiple measurement iterations exist (e.g.,
[16, 11, 11, 11] → 16ms displayed).

Fix: read `display_timings` (list[QueryDisplayTiming]) from the
detail JSON instead of scanning the raw `queries` array. The
`display_ms` value per query_id is the median of successful runs,
computed by the pipeline (see explorer-fix-read-model-contract).

Add a helper in src/lib/queryReduction.ts:
  `getDisplayMs(detail: DetailResult, queryId: string): number | null`
It reads `detail.display_timings.find(t => t.query_id === queryId)?.display_ms ?? null`.
Replace both find() call-sites in Compare.tsx with this helper.

This makes the matrix and the Compare page agree on what a query's
performance is - they will now both use the same canonical reduced
value from the pipeline.
work.summary: Fix Compare.tsx to use display_ms from DetailResult instead of first-row raw duration_ms

description:
Make the Results Explorer usable below 768px without simply stacking all
filters before all data. The audit found that the mobile first viewport can
show hero/stat/submission chrome before the leaderboard, benchmark heatmaps can
clip horizontally, and Query Workbench filters can dominate the screen before
users see any rows. The mobile design should preserve the leaderboard-first
identity while adapting dense tables into scrollable, card, or tabular
patterns with explicit affordances.
preserves: Desktop density does not regress: at 1440px, MetaLeaderboard renders at least 8 rows above the fold (asserted by w8 Playwright check).
FacetDrawer prop API and the underlying facet model from `explorer-selection-facets-coverage-at-scale` w6 are not modified by this work.
Horizontal scroll, where used, is explicit and keeps row/header context visible (sticky first column + visible scroll-hint element).
Keyboard navigation and accessible labels remain available for tables, drawers, and charts.
URL state remains the source of active filters across responsive layouts (no mobile-only state shadow).
title: Explorer: mobile-responsive dense leaderboard, filters, and charts

chartMath.parity.test.ts:43-45 - FIXTURES_DIR resolves via a
four-level `../../../../` relative path from __dirname:
  path.resolve(__dirname, "../../../../tests/parity/fixtures")

This silently breaks if either directory moves.  Options:
  (a) Use an environment variable (PARITY_FIXTURES_DIR) set in
      vitest.config.ts so the path is defined in one place.
  (b) Use `path.resolve(process.cwd(), "tests/parity/fixtures")`

  (c) Expose the fixtures path via a vite define constant.

Option (b) is simplest and matches how the Makefile already

error message to say "Run `make parity-fixtures` to regenerate."

  1. If the Python function changed intentionally → regenerate

description:
The frontend at `results-explorer/src/db.ts:53-106` hard-codes 51 required
column names against `bench.results` and validates the snapshot by
computing a set difference. Any backend rename/add/remove silently
invalidates every existing snapshot — dev's local copy, downloaded
production copies, CI fixture caches — until they regenerate. The error
shape is a 9-name diff dump, which is hard to act on and embeds no
upgrade hint.

There is already an `EXPLORER_BUILD_CONTRACT` mechanism (see
`benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/contract.py` and
`results-explorer/scripts/explorer-build-contract.mjs`), but it versions
the *output file shape*, not the *read-model column set*. The frontend
guard does not consult any version field.

Goal: replace the column-set diff with a real schema version. The
frontend error becomes "snapshot read-model v6; UI requires v7. Please
rebuild or update." Backend PRs that bump the read-model column set are
required to bump `read_model_version`.

This TODO is independent of CLI relocation (`explorer-cli-surface-
migration`) and dev-DX (`explorer-dev-snapshot-dx`), but lands cleaner
after the CLI relocation because the verification commands and
contract emitter point at the new entry.
preserves: Browser-fixture generator continues to work — only the column-list guard goes away; readiness scans for individual tables stay.
Existing snapshots produced before this TODO continue to fail informatively (as 'v0 missing or stale').
Production CI rebuild does not change behavior — the new version is emitted by the same publish entry point.
The build contract continues to validate via `EXPLORER_BUILD_CONTRACT`; this TODO extends it, does not replace it.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/contract.py — existing `EXPLORER_BUILD_CONTRACT` versioning the output shape; EXTEND with a `read_model_version` field rather than introducing a parallel mechanism.
benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/duckdb_builder.py — writes the duckdb snapshot; the place to emit a `schema_version` scalar/table.
results-explorer/scripts/explorer-build-contract.mjs:7 (REQUIRED_OUTPUTS) and the contract-fetching helper — established pattern for the Node side reading contract values; reuse.
results-explorer/src/components/__tests__/ — vitest convention for the frontend version-mismatch test.

description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review of the #1343 receipt ingestion and #1331 consumer sweep.

E4 (adversarial-input, merge-gated): the .applied.json receipt is unbounded end-to-end. Bundle validation checks companion filename/symlink/hash only (benchbox/validation/bundle.py:660-680); the explorer pipeline re-serializes receipt verbatim into results.applied_receipt (_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/transformer.py:303-332); RunReceipt.tsx:345 maps every entry into the DOM. A community submission with a valid bundle plus a 500k-entry receipt (matching companion_hashes digest) passes validation, bloats every snapshot consumer, and janks/OOMs viewers.

F9 (discovery inconsistencies): the pipeline's bundle discovery guards path.is_file() (pipeline.py:429) but the other two copies do not - benchbox/validation/bundle.py:728-739 and scripts/generate_corpus_inventory.py:54-63 - so a directory named x.json in a community submission tree raises IsADirectoryError (unhandled traceback in a workflow that runs on contributor-controlled trees, scripts/validate_submission.py:84). Companion-suffix matching is case-sensitive everywhere (a hand-renamed foo.APPLIED.json becomes a bundle candidate and fails loudly downstream - confusing error, not corruption).

RR1 (label accuracy): RunReceipt.tsx:342 renders 'Statement receipt ({entries.length})' but post-#1331 entries are per-INTENT - a dual-key ClickHouse CREATE TABLE emits two entries with duplicated statement text, so the count over-states statements.

X1 (hash seam, smell): ComparabilityReceipt.tsx:283-301 folds applied_ledger_hash into the compared Tuning value; pre- vs post-#1331 runs of the SAME logical ClickHouse tuning show 'Tuning ... differs' warnings with no seam explanation (policy_generation.py:38 unbumped; its scope is policy seams, this is a hash seam). Decide: annotate the warning when requested_config_hash matches but applied hash differs, or document the seam in the receipt UI help text.

XSS explicitly disproven during review: all receipt fields render as JSX text children; no innerHTML in results-explorer/src. Do not add sanitization theater.
preserves: Bundle discovery keeps rejecting companions as result bundles (the #1343 fix) across all three copies.
Rendering stays JSX-text-only for receipt fields; no innerHTML introduced.
Valid receipts of realistic size ingest byte-identical (verbatim contract) - caps must sit far above any legitimate run's entry count.
applied_ledger_hash remains display/warning-only - never a match, dedup, or facet key.
title: Bound the verbatim applied receipt end-to-end; harden bundle discovery edge cases; fix receipt label and hash-seam presentation

description:
Phase A of the Results Explorer strategy revision (plans/purring-jingling-petal-ultraplan).

`ResultDetail.tsx` is the only surface that currently violates the
"median at high level, samples on drill-down" contract: it renders the
raw per-sample `DetailResult.queries[]` array (every iter/stream) as
the default query table, while every other page (BenchmarkIndex,
PlatformIndex, Compare, Home) already reads the canonical median from
`DetailResult.display_timings[]`.

This item fixes that drift. The raw samples do not disappear - they
move behind an "Individual samples" expander so audit is still

description:
Reframe the explorer from "pick a benchmark and browse rows" toward
"which platform should I pick for this workload at this scale and deployment
shape" while preserving the leaderboard browser. The public corpus is expected
to grow to hundreds or thousands of result bundles, so the current filters and
tables need scalable faceting, coverage disclosure, and URL-persistent state.

Missing benchmark coverage must not penalize cross-benchmark ranking, per
product direction, but missing coverage must be visually obvious. A platform's
aggregate should therefore be "average rank over covered cohorts" with
coverage badges and missing cells, not a zero/last-place penalty.

description:
The original strategy proposal suggested defaulting the leaderboard to
`trust: maintainer-run` and hiding community results unless explicitly
opted in. The 2026-04-15 adversarial review rejected this: hiding
community results by default **defeats the entire value of BenchBox's
trust model**. The right pattern is to show everything and render the
trust tier as a visible per-row badge, with trust as an optional filter.

This TODO:

1. Adds a Trust column to QueryHeatmap rows and the list-view fallback,
   rendered as a small colored badge (maintainer = green, community =
   blue, unknown/CI/local = neutral gray).

2. Adds a trust filter control to BenchmarkIndex that defaults to "All"
   (shows every tier) with chips for each tier a user can deselect.

3. Sorts rows by primary metric within the default "All" view, not by
   trust tier - the trust model is informational, not a sort key.

4. Propagates trust_label through to the Compare page header so trust
   disparities in a comparison are also visible there.

Explicitly rejected: defaulting to "maintainer-run only" or visually
de-emphasizing community results via reduced opacity. BenchBox's
differentiator is the explicit trust model - make it pop.
preserves: Default view shows all trust tiers - never hide community results by default
Existing trust_label values in manifest.json - do not reshape the vocabulary
Trust tier does not affect row ordering within the leaderboard - ranking stays metric-based

description:
PR #277 added the `explorer-tokens` PR-time job in
`.github/workflows/pr.yml`. It is gated on
`needs.ci-paths.outputs.needs-code-ci == 'true'`, which is true for any
code-CI path (`benchbox/**`, `tests/**`, `scripts/**`, …), so the job
boots a runner on every Python-only PR before its inner
`Detect results-explorer/src changes` step short-circuits the scan.

Add an `explorer-paths-needed` boolean output to
`scripts/path_filter_decision.py` (mirror the existing
`content-guard-needed` pattern) and switch the job's `if:` to use it.
The inner detection step can then be removed.

The classifier already has the matching pattern infrastructure;
`results-explorer/**` is in `.github/path-filters.yml` `code-ci`. Add
a new top-level rule key `explorer-tokens` (sibling of `safe-content`,
`content-guard`, `code-ci`) matching exactly `results-explorer/src/**`.
The classifier emits `explorer-paths-needed` (boolean) when any
changed path matches that key; the PR-time job's `if:` switches from
`needs.ci-paths.outputs.needs-code-ci` to
`needs.ci-paths.outputs.explorer-paths-needed`. The inner
`Detect results-explorer/src changes` step is then redundant and is
removed in the same change.
preserves: Existing ci-paths outputs (safe-content-only, needs-code-ci, content-guard-needed) and their semantics.
ci-required-result aggregator behavior — explorer-tokens skipped path still counts as success.
title: Expose explorer-paths-needed from path_filter_decision so the explorer-tokens job stops booting on Python-only PRs

description:

(plans/purring-jingling-petal-ultraplan).

description:
The 2026-04-15 review identified a cluster of foundational issues in
the results explorer that share the same root cause: visualization
primitives are defined inline per component instead of shared. These
bugs produce inconsistent UX today and block clean follow-on work
(chart-coverage expansion, parity tests, comparison artifacts).

Five distinct problems, fixable as one coordinated change:

**Issue 1 - Dual definition of "speedup" on the Compare page.**
Summary cards (Compare.tsx:225) compute `slowest_primary / primary`
(a "vs slowest" spread). Per-query breakdown table (Compare.tsx:392)
computes `slowest / fastest` (within-query spread). Speedup chart
(NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:57) computes `baseline / this`
(per-baseline ratio). All three render with the same "x" label.
Users see contradictory numbers on the same page.

**Issue 2 - Color/style constants duplicated across 4 files.**
`COMPARE_COLORS` / `CHART_COLORS` (`["#3b82f6","#10b981","#f59e0b","#ef4444"]`)
defined in Compare.tsx:17, NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:22,
DivergingBarChart.tsx:11, QueryTimingChart.tsx:18. Plus magic numbers
`LOG2_MIN/MAX`, `MAX_DELTA_PCT=300`, `GRID_STOPS=[0.25,0.5,1,2,4]`
scattered without a single source.

**Issue 3 - "Failed to Decode Data" error is opaque and misleading.**
When a benchmark artifact is missing, Vite serves the SPA HTML
fallback (HTTP 200), `DecompressionStream` then throws
"Failed to Decode Data" (manifest.ts:81-87). Users see this on the
TPC-H Results page (the user's screenshot of 2026-04-15) when the
page loads before the manifest filter has resolved the phase.
Three sub-problems: (a) BenchmarkIndex.tsx:84 useEffect fires before
`phases` resolves; (b) error message gives no clue what happened;
(c) Vite SPA fallback is detected as "decode error" rather than 404.

**Issue 4 - SVG charts have hardcoded viewBox dimensions.**
NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:69 (`viewBox="0 0 600 …"`),
DivergingBarChart.tsx:91 (`viewBox="0 0 600 …"`),
QueryTimingChart.tsx:58 (`viewBox="0 0 800 …"`),
GroupedQueryChart (`viewBox="0 0 900 …"`). All use
`preserveAspectRatio="none"` so on wide screens text squishes and
bar widths look wrong. This is a primary visual contributor to the
user's "sub-par visualizations" complaint.

**Issue 5 - Compare uses `geomean_ms` ignoring per-benchmark primary metric.**
Compare.tsx:151-156 hardcodes `getPrimary(r) = r.geomean_ms`. For
benchmarks where `power_score` is the primary metric (defined in
RANKING_METRIC_BY_FAMILY), the speedup math runs on the wrong axis.
Already exposed via BenchmarkSummary.ranking.primary_metric for the
heatmap (QueryHeatmap.tsx:102-107) - Compare needs to consume the
same registry.
preserves: ComparabilityBanner UI and `buildComparabilityWarnings` API - only consumers change, not the warning generation
Compare URL format `?ids=id1,id2,...` - short-id resolution behavior unchanged
Existing 36 Vitest tests + Python fast suite - all must still pass
QueryHeatmap row selection / Compare URL building - touched only to read from chartTheme, not behavior change
QueryHeatmap visual output - colorForCell/lightnessForCell return values must not change

description:
Phase E of the Results Explorer strategy revision
(plans/purring-jingling-petal-ultraplan).

The master leaderboard (Phase B) and the query workbench (Phase C)
both want shareable URLs that round-trip filter state. Existing
BenchmarkIndex/PlatformIndex filter selects use local `useState`,
which makes cohort/SF/phase choices invisible to navigation and
bookmarks.

Introduce a tiny `useUrlState<T>(key, initial, serde)` hook using
`history.replaceState` + `popstate`. Migrate existing filter
`useState` call sites directly - no API surface invention, just a
swap.
preserves: Existing BenchmarkIndex/PlatformIndex filter behavior is identical - URL sync is additive
No new dependencies - hook uses only built-in history/popstate APIs
vite-ssg build continues to succeed (hook must be SSR-safe)

description:
Blind-spot `2026-05-04-113747` surfaced two recurring weaknesses in the
/blog critique rubric for vendor-announcement response posts:

1. Currency drift between outline write date and present-day shipped
   state -- "honest deferrals" cited in an outline can become shipped
   surface within days; the rubric has no Technical-lane check that
   re-validates such claims against `git log` and `_project/TODO`/
   `_project/DONE`.
2. Partisan-reader response to framing -- vendor-response posts have a
   guaranteed adversarial reader on the source-vendor's team; framings
   that contrast (boring/novel, surface/hidden) carry the same
   substance with less bridge-burning if rephrased into technical
   specificity.

The current rubric's Risk axis mentions "stale, partisan" generically
but does not enforce a vendor-response-specific check. Adding three
cheap axis additions closes the gap.

description:
Six blind-spot findings between 2026-05-03 and 2026-05-05 each flagged a
class of review the current five-axis rubric (Correctness, Readability,
Architecture, Security, Performance) does not catch:

- Matrix/audit docs whose deliverable is tables of numbers
  (`2026-05-03-085238`).
- Mixed tooling+data PRs where reversibility differs by component
  (`2026-05-03-090105`).
- Repo-shape ADRs (branch-shape, CI moves, cross-branch vendoring) that
  need a day-1 executability dry-run (`2026-05-03-092657`).
- Multi-work-unit specs whose vertical slicing is unreachable in
  practice (`2026-05-04-120000`).
- Defect-follow-up reviews that miss stale artifact reuse in
  orchestration code (`2026-05-05-090216`).
- Verification-only commits that cite transient evidence in commit
  messages with no committed artifact (`2026-05-04-083819`).

The fix is concentrated: extend
`.claude/skills/code/references/five-axis-review.md` with six branches,
each gated by the kind of change under review. The rubric stays
five-axis-shaped; the branches add review-targeted prompts.
preserves: Existing 'What's Done Well' rule and change-sizing guidance remain.
Severity classification table (Critical/Required/Nit/Consider) is unchanged.
The five top-level axes (Correctness, Readability & Simplicity, Architecture, Security, Performance) remain the primary frame; new content is review-shape-specific branches, not new top-level axes.
title: Extend the five-axis code review rubric with six missing branches

description:
Maintainer testing of the Phase 2 submission flow proves the technology
works. A first external contributor walking through the docs unaided
proves the *experience* works - different bar, different bugs. We need
one human who has not seen the code to attempt a real submission and
report back where they got stuck.

This item recruits one trusted external user (not a maintainer, not a
current Claude Code agent), watches them perform the full submission,
captures friction points, and converts the friction list into actionable
follow-up TODOs. Done before broader public promotion.

Update 2026-04-28: an agent-proxy dry-run was performed via Claude
Cowork as a doc-hardening pre-pass. It surfaced 11 friction items and
produced 6 follow-up TODOs (`dry-run-followup-*.yaml` in this
directory). See
`_project/handoffs/external-dry-run-retrospective-2026-04-28.md` for
the retrospective. The agent run does NOT close this TODO -- the
human dry-run (w1-w5) is still required because Cowork structurally
cannot exercise auth, push, PR open, CI validate, maintainer review,
trust-label apply, or explorer redeploy. The agent run reduces the
friction the eventual human contributor will hit.

Update 2026-04-29: a SECOND agent-proxy dry-run was performed via
Codex against PyPI `benchbox 0.2.1` on a clone of `published-results`.
Each surface friction item the 2026-04-28 PR cluster (PRs #43-#46)
pre-fixed was either not hit by Codex or hit-and-resolved-cleanly,
validating the doc-hardening pre-pass. Critically, Codex reached one
layer deeper than Cowork could and surfaced a release-blocker: the
`published-results` validator's hash algorithm (per-directory) does
not match `develop`'s writer (per-file), so any submission produced
by current `benchbox submit` will fail CI on the documented PR target
branch. Filed as
`dry-run-followup-validator-hash-contract-mismatch.yaml` (Critical).
Plus 7 polish items consolidated as
`dry-run-followup-cli-ux-and-doc-polish-2026-04-29.yaml` (Medium).
See `_project/handoffs/external-dry-run-retrospective-2026-04-29.md`
for the retrospective + maintainer forensic.

This TODO still does NOT close. The human dry-run remains required:
(a) the Critical hash-contract fix must land + ship before recruiting
a human, (b) only a human can validate the post-CI maintainer review
and explorer redeploy (Step 5), and (c) public promotion timing
depends on a frictionless human run.
preserves: Phase 2's trust-label distinction - community submissions retain `community-submission`, never silently promoted.
Production review rigor - if the submission has defects, it is asked to be fixed, not silently merged.
The contributor's autonomy - no real-time hand-holding during the dry-run.

approach:
Three-phase extraction strategy with clear gates between phases.

Phase A - Internal API Separation (in-tree, no new package):
1. Expand ascii/__init__.py to export all data models and factory functions (w1)
2. Decouple the single `format_scale_factor` import via optional Callable on
   ASCIIChartOptions - the only benchbox import inside ascii/ (w18)
3. Create ascii_api.py facade module as single import point for external callers (w16)
4. Migrate all external callers (CLI, MCP, exporters, post_run_summary,
   chart_generator) to import from ascii_api only (w16)
5. Enforce import boundary with automated gate check (w17)
6. Create golden-output snapshot tests for all 15 chart types BEFORE extraction (w19)
Gate: zero direct ascii submodule imports outside visualization package.

Phase B - Standalone Package Extraction:
7. Scaffold textcharts package in packages/textcharts/ with src layout (w3)
8. Define public API: drop ASCII prefix, add ChartOptions alias (w13)
9. Copy code, rewrite internal imports, add custom palette support (w4-w6)
10. Replace BenchBox ascii/ with compatibility shim re-exporting from textcharts (w7)
11. Add textcharts as BenchBox path dependency (w8)
12. Verify golden-output parity - must be byte-identical (w9-w10)
Gate: full test suite passes, zero benchbox imports in textcharts.

Phase C - Packaging and Release:
13. Complete packaging MVP with README, chart gallery, py.typed (w15)
14. Publish to PyPI and switch BenchBox to versioned dependency (w11)
15. Deprecate compatibility shims after one stable release cycle (w12)

description:
BenchBox currently owns a mature ASCII charting implementation (15 chart types,
595-line base module, zero external dependencies) under
`benchbox/core/visualization/ascii/` plus runtime dispatch and adapters in
CLI/MCP/export paths. We want to extract this into a reusable standalone Python
library called `textcharts` (PyPI: `textcharts`, import: `textcharts`) without
breaking existing BenchBox workflows.

Key architecture decisions:
- Library name: `textcharts` - generic, memorable, no BenchBox branding
- Dispatch layer (`ascii_runtime.py`): stays in BenchBox - it contains
  domain-specific NormalizedResult→chart data conversion
- Naming: standalone drops `ASCII` prefix (e.g. `BarChart` not `ASCIIBarChart`);
  BenchBox shims re-export with `ASCII*` aliases for compatibility
- Only ONE coupling point to sever: `base.py:481` imports `format_scale_factor`

The correct migration path is staged:
1) Define and freeze charting API contracts first
2) Decouple the single `format_scale_factor` import via optional Callable
3) Complete BenchBox-internal API separation before extraction starts
4) Extract charting primitives + renderers behind a compatibility shim
5) Keep BenchBox-specific normalization/adaptation in BenchBox
6) Validate text-output parity via golden snapshot tests before cutover
7) Externalize packaging/release only after in-repo adoption is stable

This TODO captures the full execution DAG required to minimize risk and avoid
regressions in CLI output, MCP responses, and tests.

description:
Integrate Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse SQL Analytics Endpoint as a read-only SQL
query platform for benchmarking pre-loaded Delta Lake tables.

**Critical Architectural Constraint**:
The Lakehouse SQL Analytics Endpoint is READ-ONLY. This is a fundamental Fabric
design choice, not a BenchBox limitation:
- NO DDL: Cannot CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, ALTER TABLE
- NO DML: Cannot INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE
- QUERY ONLY: SELECT statements only

**Data Loading Requirement**:
Data MUST be loaded via Microsoft Fabric Spark Notebooks (see related TODO:
fabric-spark-notebooks-platform.yaml). The workflow is:
1. Use Fabric Spark to load data into Lakehouse Delta tables
2. Use this adapter to benchmark query performance via SQL endpoint

This is a valid benchmarking pattern for:
- Measuring query-only performance (common for BI/reporting workloads)
- Comparing Lakehouse SQL endpoint vs Fabric Warehouse performance
- Testing Delta Lake query optimization (V-Order, Z-Order effects)

The adapter will explicitly validate the read-only constraint and fail fast
with helpful error messages if users attempt write operations.

Technical characteristics:
- T-SQL dialect (subset compatible with Synapse/SQL Server)
- TDS protocol via pyodbc (same as Fabric Warehouse)
- Entra ID authentication only
- Automatic Delta Lake to SQL type mapping
- OneLake-backed storage (transparent to queries)

Reference: fabric_warehouse.py:14-30 documents this limitation explicitly:
"Lakehouse: SQL Analytics Endpoint is READ-ONLY (not supported)"
This adapter provides READ-ONLY support as a deliberate feature.
title: Add Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse SQL Analytics Endpoint support

Integrate Microsoft Fabric Spark Notebooks as a supported BenchBox platform for
managed Spark-based benchmarking in the Fabric ecosystem.

Microsoft Fabric Spark is fundamentally different from Fabric Warehouse:
- **Fabric Warehouse** (existing): T-SQL based, uses COPY INTO for data loading
- **Fabric Spark** (this TODO): PySpark-based, uses Livy API for job submission

This fills a critical gap: the existing FabricWarehouseAdapter explicitly notes
that Lakehouse data loading requires Spark, which is currently unsupported.
This adapter would enable:
- Full Lakehouse benchmarking with read/write capabilities
- V-Order optimization (Spark-only feature in Fabric)
- Delta Lake native operations
- OneLake integration via Spark paths

Key technical characteristics:
- Spark 3.4+ runtime with Fabric-specific configurations
- Livy REST API for remote job submission (notebooks execute remotely)
- Entra ID authentication (consistent with Fabric ecosystem)
- OneLake paths: abfss://{workspace}@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/...
- Delta Lake as default table format

Reference: fabric_warehouse.py:14-30 documents the Warehouse vs Lakehouse distinction
and explicitly states Lakehouse requires Spark for data loading.

description:
WS1 of _project/planning/ci-failure-reduction-plan.md. fast_test_lane_policy.json is the 2nd most-touched file in the repo (10 PRs since 2026-06-20; 8 ceiling bumps in the week of 07-16..07-22; ~30 documented bumps in _ceiling_note including two multi-PR 'composed byte-identical bump' episodes). Root causes: (a) bumps use minimal headroom (+5..+33) so the next test-adding PR retrips; (b) the justification log is one JSON string so any two bumps conflict textually; (c) the check is absolute, not base-relative, so two independently-green PRs compose over the ceiling after both merge (strict checks are off).

Phased fix: (1) move _ceiling_note to an append-only _project/config/fast_lane_ceiling_log.md with merge=union in .gitattributes; (2) bump quantum +500 with resulting headroom >= 250, plus a WARNING from timing_policy_check.py when headroom < 100 so the bump lands before the violation; (3) persist develop's fast-lane collected count from develop-post-merge (it already runs ci-lint and prints the count) and enforce a base-relative delta (start: +150) in the PR lint lane, demoting the absolute ceiling to a post-merge/nightly backstop; (4) auto-ratchet: scheduled job opens a mechanical chore PR bumping +500 with a generated log entry when headroom < 100. End state: feature PRs never edit the policy file.
preserves: An absolute lane-size backstop remains enforced somewhere (post-merge/nightly) at every phase - never delta-only
develop-post-merge safety net stays active (see dev-loop-step-6-queue-decision-gate must-preserve)
forbidden_marker_expressions and forbidden_path_substrings enforcement in timing_policy_check.py is unchanged

_project/blind-spots/2026-07-18-190500-evidence-tree-sha-provenance-mismatch.md is UNTRACKED in git (it exists only in the primary clone's working tree, not in any commit). Phase 6 deletes the tracked _project/blind-spots/*.md records, so a git-based deletion will not necessarily remove this one -- it can silently survive demolition, leaving exactly the kind of stray in-tree findings record the whole domain exists to eliminate (R4).

Its finding IS already landed in production (disposition=open, awaiting triage) and was verified lossless at the time, BUT its related_paths and suggested_sweep were hand-mapped into 3 finding_evidence rows -- the anti-pattern that findings-schema-legacy-frontmatter-mapping-20260724 forbids. Now that v4 has real columns for both, the record should be re-synced from source so its representation matches the pipeline, then the file removed.

Ordering matters and is not obvious: because the source file declares no `evidence:` key, a plain re-sync will NOT clear those 3 rows (parse_draft records evidence_declared, and reconcile only runs when the draft asserts the key -- deliberate, so a legacy record's curated rows are never destroyed). Clearing them is therefore an explicit step, not a side effect of re-syncing.

description:
Three surfaces shipped during the findings-domain v4/phase-5 work are documented nowhere an agent or operator would look:

description:
The root cause of the whole silent-loss class: validate_blind_spot.py accepts one field set (ALLOWED_FIELDS = 5 required + 8 optional) and _split_body parses EVERY '## ' section, but parse_draft (_project/scripts/todo_findings.py) reads a strictly narrower set -- 5 frontmatter keys plus evidence, and only 4 of the parsed sections. The two sets are never compared by any test, so a validator-accepted field silently vanishes and 'todo finding sync' still prints 'synced 1' with no error and no warning. Measured over the live corpus 2026-07-29: 65 of 65 files lose content this way.

The fix is a fail-closed contract, not a one-off patch: declare the parser's field and section homes machine-readably in todo_findings.py (for example FIELD_HOMES and SECTION_HOMES mappings), and test that every name in validate_blind_spot.ALLOWED_FIELDS and every known body heading has a declared home. Fields not yet given a real column carry an explicit, named pending set so the contract is still total -- adding a NEW validator field without a home fails the test immediately, and findings-schema-v4-lossless-legacy-fields empties the pending set rather than editing the assertion.

This is the guard that stops the class recurring; it is deliberately independent of the v4 migration so it can land first and make the v4 work verifiable.

description:
Implement the SCHEMA_VERSION 3 -> 4 migration that gives every validator-accepted legacy field and every '## ' body section a field-level home, so the phase-5 parity gate can promise field-level preservation. Measured exposure over the live 65-file corpus (2026-07-29): today's parse_draft silently drops related_paths (65 files, 170 path entries), suggested_sweep (65 files, 11,559 chars), todo_id (36 files, 19 unique targets, NO column exists), and 8 unknown '## ' sections totalling 5,779 chars -- including seven 'Why the review missed it' meta-analysis sections, which are the L2 lesson the corpus exists for. sync reports 'synced 1' with no error or warning. This item is why findings-phase5-migration is blocked: phase 5 pushes all 65 files through this parser and phase 6 then deletes the tracked originals.

Shape decided by the owner 2026-07-29: explicit columns plus a sections table. ALTER TABLE findings ADD COLUMN related_paths TEXT (JSON array); ADD COLUMN suggested_sweep TEXT; CREATE TABLE finding_sections (id, finding_id REFERENCES findings ON DELETE CASCADE, position, heading, text) for any '## ' section outside the four known headings -- the sections table subsumes the whole problem class rather than enumerating today's four stray headings.

todo_id link mapping (pre-flight run 2026-07-29 against the live tracker): ZERO dangling targets -- all 19 unique todo_id values resolve to live items, so the spec's dangling-link policy (target_item NULL plus a note) covers a case that does not occur; keep the counter in the parity report but expect zero. The 36 files split by status: 32 are 'merged-to-todo' + todo_id and map to kind 'promoted-to' (consistent with disposition 'promoted'); 4 are 'actioned' + todo_id and must map to kind 'resolved-by', because a 'promoted-to' edge on an 'actioned' finding both misstates the history and breaks the promote invariant that 'promoted-to' implies disposition 'promoted'. Both kinds are already in the baked-in CHECK, so no finding_links table rebuild is needed.

Composed with findings-link-fk-delete-safety-20260724 by owner decision 2026-07-29: both changes require SCHEMA_VERSION 3 -> 4, and production must migrate ONCE. The FK delete-safety change (finding_links.target_item is a real FK, so a hosted --replace reload can fail or leave stale links) lands in this same migration and PR. The project todo wrapper has no 'update' subcommand (standalone-only), so that item's scope could not be folded into it in place; it is completed alongside this one against the same landed migration.

Operational coupling: the CLI refuses to run against a DB whose schema_version is below the CLI's SCHEMA_VERSION and migrations never auto-apply, so the moment v4 code is on develop every collaborator's CLI is inert against the live v3 DB until someone runs 'todo migrate'. Land the code and run the hosted migrate together.

description:
BenchBox currently treats ClickHouse as one base platform with mixed local/server
behavior, while ClickHouse Cloud is already a separate first-class platform. That
design leaves the public contract and the implementation boundary out of sync:

- `clickhouse` defaults to chDB local execution, but multiple registry/install
  surfaces still present it as the `clickhouse-driver` platform
- local and server execution use materially different client contracts, yet they
  are forced through one adapter boundary
- result, dependency, and CLI surfaces partially collapse `clickhouse` and `chdb`
  while other code already treats `chdb` as a distinct label
- the real ClickHouse Docker path exists, but its tests only validate connectivity
  and trivial query execution rather than benchmark-level schema/load/query behavior

The new public naming contract must be three first-class platform identifiers:

- `clickhouse-local` - chDB embedded/in-process ClickHouse
- `clickhouse-server` - Docker-backed or self-hosted remote ClickHouse via `clickhouse-driver`
- `clickhouse-cloud` - managed ClickHouse Cloud via `clickhouse-connect`

Under this contract, bare `clickhouse` is no longer the canonical server-facing
name. If it remains temporarily accepted, it must be a compatibility alias with
explicit deprecation behavior rather than the primary documented selector.

This work turns the naming split into a real architectural split. It should create
clear platform registration, dependency, packaging, testing, and documentation
boundaries while preserving shared ClickHouse SQL/tuning/workload logic underneath.

This TODO builds on the compatibility groundwork from
`standardize-clickhouse-deployment-mode-contract`, but it supersedes that item's
remaining docs/help/test cleanup. The end-state is not "keep
`clickhouse:local/server` but make it cleaner"; the end-state is explicit
first-class platform names with legacy selectors handled only as migration
compatibility inputs.
preserves: Existing chDB persistence behavior and `.chdb` database naming continue to work for the local embedded path under `clickhouse-local`

The Docker testing harness for ClickHouse continues to use the existing compose stack and Makefile entrypoints rather than inventing a parallel ad-hoc test path

The deployment normalization and legacy-read compatibility introduced by `standardize-clickhouse-deployment-mode-contract` remain reusable during the platform-name migration rather than being reimplemented from scratch
`clickhouse-cloud` remains a separate first-class managed-service platform and must not be folded back into a mixed base ClickHouse selector

description:
Recent no-color/greyscale ASCII chart behavior is still suboptimal in real outputs,
especially for head-to-head comparisons. User-reported regressions show that structural
differentiation and readability goals are not consistently met across chart types.

Confirmed issues from live output and code review:

1. **Box plot series labels are over-truncated and include a low-value marker prefix**
   (e.g., "■ DataFusion (.."), making series names harder to read.

2. **Grouped histogram outlier semantics are incorrect**: outlier detection is tracked by
   `query_id` only, so when one platform is an outlier for a query, all platform bars for
   that query are rendered as outliers.

3. **Grouped histogram legend markers do not match plotted glyphs** in no-color mode:
   legend uses marker set (■/◆/...) while bars use fill patterns (█/▓/...), causing
   unnecessary cognitive load.

4. **Heatmap no-color output is visually sparse and hard to scan**: values are centered
   instead of right-aligned and column delineation is weak, producing mostly-empty columns
   and poor comparability.

state at that point. Trial click does not actuate the handler.

description:
Follow-up work is required after adversarial review of the DataFrame parameter
substitution parity implementation (commit e6d83095). Three concrete issues were
identified:

1. Override lifecycle bug (P1): module-level parameter overrides can leak across
   runs because setup happens before query discovery and cleanup is not guaranteed
   for early returns or unexpected exceptions.
2. Stream parity gap (P1): TPC-DS override extraction currently ignores stream_id,
   but DataFrame execution iterates stream IDs across warmup/measurement iterations.
   This breaks SQL/DataFrame substitution parity for stream-varying runs.
3. Extractor coverage gap (P2): TPC-DS extraction supports only a narrow set of
   parameter families, leaving many query parameters stuck on static defaults.
   This prevents robust parity claims for broad TPC-DS coverage.

This TODO closes all three issues with minimal surface-area change, explicit
guardrails, and verification targeted at correctness, parity, and regression safety.

description:
DataFusion runs for `write_primitives` and `read_primitives` are not behaviorally
equivalent to the SQL baseline due to three concrete defects:

1. Write-primitives setup checks call `connection.execute(...)` directly in
   `WritePrimitivesBenchmark._table_exists()` and related setup probes, but
   DataFusion SQL execution uses `SessionContext.sql(...).collect()`.
   This causes false negatives for required TPC-H source table existence and
   aborts most operations before execution.

2. Read-primitives MAP queries (`map_construction`, `map_access`, `map_keys_values`)
   currently use SQL forms that fail on DataFusion parser/planner. These queries
   are still scheduled for DataFusion without a working dialect variant, so
   runs fail despite equivalent intent being possible.

3. Concurrent DataFusion runs targeting the same working directory can race on
   directory removal, producing intermittent `Could not remove existing database`
   failures. This also undermines reliable database reuse decisions.

Goal: restore platform parity so the same benchmark command (SQL mode) performs
the equivalent action on DataFusion, while preserving existing adapter architecture,
shared validation/reuse flow, and avoiding one-off duplicated logic.

Read-primitives catalog variant and skip_on semantics in `benchbox/core/read_primitives/catalog/loader.py` and `benchbox/core/read_primitives/queries.py` remain backward compatible

description:
On 2026-01-28, a local git config entry `user.name=user.email` was written
to .git/config, setting the commit author name to the literal string "user.email"
instead of "Joe Harris". This was discovered and fixed on 2026-04-14 (the config
entry has been removed). However, all commits between 80e17e9 (2026-01-28 09:21)
and 2cfdcfd (2026-04-14 20:16) were made with the bad author name - a total of
2,286 commits on main and 1,850 commits on published-results (overlapping with main).

git-filter-repo is available at /Users/joe/.local/bin/git-filter-repo and will
be used to rewrite the author name across all affected commits.

Refs affected:
- main: 2,286 commits with author "user.email" (first: 80e17e9, last: 2cfdcfd)
- published-results: 1,850 commits affected (shares history with main)
- Tags v0.1.0-v0.2.0: point to correct-author commits, but their SHAs shift
  during rewrite - tags must be force-pushed after rewrite
- private/claude/seed-corpus-infra: 3 remote-only commits on top of old main;
  these are NOT rewritten by filter-repo and must be cherry-picked onto new main
- claude/condescending-mcnulty: local branch, 0 commits ahead of main - safe to
  reset to new main HEAD after rewrite

description:
After converting TPC-H data to Delta format, every subsequent run triggers
"⚠️ Manifest validation failed; regenerating benchmark data" even when nothing
has changed. Data regeneration is unnecessary but takes ~10s at SF=1.

ROOT CAUSE: Directory-based formats (Delta, Iceberg, DuckLake, partitioned Parquet)
store a single directory path in the manifest entry (e.g., "lineitem/") with
size_bytes computed as a recursive file sum via rglob("*"). But validation calls
fp.stat().st_size on that directory path, which returns the inode size (~96 bytes
on macOS/Linux) - never matching the stored recursive sum.

This was masked when vortex (a regular file format) was at format_preference[0].
The format_preference ordering fix (commit d643ccaca) moved delta to position 0,
exposing the latent inconsistency.

DESIGN ANALYSIS - Should we store individual files instead of directories?
No. Delta/Iceberg/DuckLake tables are loaded as directories (e.g.,
`deltatable('path/to/lineitem/')`), not by listing individual parquet files.
The directory path IS the correct entry for downstream loaders. Storing individual
files would break the loading contract and require changes to 6+ callers of
get_table_files() plus all platform-specific data loading code.

FIX STRATEGY: Make validation directory-aware. When a manifest entry path resolves
to a directory, compute recursive file size (matching write-time calculation) instead
of calling stat().st_size directly. Additionally, add an `is_directory` boolean to
manifest entries so validation doesn't need to probe the filesystem to determine
entry type. This future-proofs for any new directory-based formats.

AFFECTED VALIDATION SITES (confirmed by code reading):
1. runner.py:1175-1177 - _validate_manifest_if_present()
2. data_validation.py:498 - table expectation validation
3. data_validation.py:530 - unknown benchmark file validation

AFFECTED FORMATS: delta, iceberg, ducklake, partitioned parquet - all use
rglob("*") for size at write time but get stat().st_size at read time.
preserves: ConversionResult.output_files continues to accept both file and directory Path objects
File-based format validation (parquet, vortex, tbl) continues to use exact stat().st_size comparison
ManifestV2 serialization remains backward-compatible (is_directory defaults to False)
_validate_manifest_if_present() returns the same 3-tuple contract: (is_valid, manifest_dict_or_none, manifest_found)
data_validation.py size checks for regular files remain exact (not relaxed)
get_table_files() API and return format unchanged - all 6 callers unaffected

description:
The MCP server emits non-protocol output to stdout during result export,
which breaks stdio MCP clients like the codex CLI. For stdio MCP servers,
stdout must contain exclusively JSON-RPC messages. When ResultExporter
prints status lines to stdout, it corrupts the JSON-RPC stream, causing
strict clients to close the transport with "Transport closed" errors.

self.console.print() at multiple points (lines 167, 171, 175, 247, 255)
to output status messages. When MCP tools create ResultExporter without
a quiet console, these messages leak to stdout.

The fix uses the existing quiet-mode infrastructure in benchbox/utils/printing.py
which already provides get_quiet_console() and set_quiet() utilities.

description:
In any TPC throughput run with >= 2 streams (and in combined mode), every query
is captured (EXPLAINed, cost paid, counted) but ZERO plans are attached to result
rows.

Root cause: the inline chokepoint sets `_plan_capture_key` on the recorded dict,
but the TPC row converters rebuild rows WITHOUT it:
  - benchbox/core/tpch/platform_power.py:25  (_power_query_result)
  - benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py:315-325, 409-419  (throughput converters)
Attachment then falls back to the public query_id, and `_attach_captured_plans`
(benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py:1311-1314) maps an id to None whenever it has
>= 2 captured variants. Throughput streams are seed-varied by spec
(`stream_seed = seed + stream_id*1000 + position`, benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py:221),
so every query is multi-variant with >= 2 streams -> all dropped. In combined mode
this also strips the power-phase plan for any id that later runs in throughput.

This is currently documented as a limitation (docs/features/query-plan-analysis.md:157)
and asserted-as-intended in a test (tests/integration/test_plan_capture_combined_divergence.py:213),
but seed variation is the NORMAL multi-stream configuration, not an edge case, and
the sibling test `test_standard_path_exact_key_attaches_each_variant` proves the
converters COULD carry the key and get per-variant fidelity.

Secondary reporting defect: the console summary (benchbox/platforms/base/result_capture.py:1744)
prints `self.query_plans_captured` (the per-variant counter) e.g. "Query plans: 88/88
captured", while the bundle's row-derived count (compute_plan_capture_stats,
benchbox/core/results/schema.py:940) is 0 and build_plans_payload writes no
.plans.json. The console claims success the artifact contradicts.

Related serialization defect: build_plans_payload (benchbox/core/results/schema.py:1028,1050)
keys plans_by_query by public query_id, so even when attachment succeeds, multiple
stream rows for one id collapse to a single last-writer-wins entry - contradicting
capture_query_plan's "one plan per (query_id, stream_id)" docstring.
preserves: Per-variant fidelity for rows that already carry an exact _plan_capture_key (test_standard_path_exact_key_attaches_each_variant must stay green).
The isolated post-measurement capture contract: no EXPLAIN in the timed loop or a concurrent stream; writes never re-executed.
query_plans_captured and the bundle plans_captured must agree after the fix.
title: Attach captured plans to multi-stream throughput/combined rows (and reconcile the console count)

read/consume side is non-functional on real exported bundles. Two layered

1. `.phases` does not exist. `BenchmarkResults` (benchbox/core/results/models.py:312)

     - benchbox/cli/commands/compare_plans.py:76,128  (crash)
     - benchbox/core/query_plans/comparison.py:758    (crash; compare-plans --summary)
     - benchbox/cli/commands/compare.py:1227          (crash; `compare --include-plans`, the recommended path)

description:
The manifest's format_preference field (persisted by previous --table-format
conversion runs) takes priority over platform default preferences. This means
if a user previously ran --table-format delta, ALL subsequent runs silently
use delta format even without --table-format.

Concrete failure: TPC-H SF1 on DuckDB fails because the existing manifest has
format_preference: ["delta", "parquet", "iceberg", "tbl"] from a prior
conversion. Delta entries are directories (is_directory: True), which the shard
loader can't handle via the generic file path. Same root cause for
read_primitives, write_primitives, and transaction_primitives (all share
TPC-H SF1 data).

Principle: BenchBox users should NEVER be surprised by the data format used
for loading. Platform preferences should always drive default format selection.
PLATFORM_FORMAT_PREFERENCES is already correctly configured (tbl first for
SQL platforms, delta first for lakehouse platforms) - it's just not being used
as the default.

Two orthogonal changes:
1. Always prefer platform defaults in native mode (one-line change)
2. Thread explicit --table-format to DataSourceResolver so explicit user
   requests still override platform defaults for that run

description:
The current Write Primitives DataFrame implementation for PySpark is fundamentally broken.
The "DDL operations" are just SQL string builders wrapped in Python methods - this is NOT
DataFrame testing, it's SQL execution with extra steps.

Current (WRONG) implementation:
```python
def execute_ddl(self, ddl_statement: str, spark_session: Any = None):
    spark_session.sql(ddl_statement)  # Just executes raw SQL
```

Correct PySpark DataFrame write operations should use the actual DataFrame API:
- INSERT: df.write.mode("append").parquet(path)
- BULK_LOAD: spark.read.parquet(src).write.parquet(tgt)
- UPDATE: DeltaTable.forPath(spark, path).update(condition, set)
- DELETE: DeltaTable.forPath(spark, path).delete(condition)
- MERGE: DeltaTable.alias("t").merge(source, cond).whenMatchedUpdate().execute()
- DDL: Should be REMOVED - DDL is SQL by definition, not DataFrame

Key design decisions (confirmed):
1. Row-level ops (UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE): Only support with Delta Lake/Iceberg
   - Plain Parquet gets INSERT/BULK_LOAD only
2. SparkSession: Require explicit session parameter (consistent with PySparkDataFrameAdapter)
title: Fix PySpark DataFrame Write Operations
