description:
The TPC-Havoc cross-dialect equivalence oracle already samples two engines: the
DuckDB SQL gate (PR #770, the hard blocker, KNOWN_DIVERGENCES empty) and a bounded
PostgreSQL sample (PR #803, POSTGRES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES empty, 203/203 executable
variants equivalent). That two-engine signal said the dialect-translation seam was
faithful - but on engines whose gaps are SIMILAR (both PostgreSQL-family). The
`deferred` item of tpchavoc-cross-dialect-equivalence-sampling asked whether that
fidelity is systematic or Postgres-specific.

This TODO is that sequenced follow-on: a THIRD engine with a DIFFERENT gap profile.
A variant is written once and run, after dialect translation, on ~20 platforms;
"equivalent on DuckDB" does not imply "equivalent everywhere" (translation can shift
NULL ordering, integer-vs-float division, DISTINCT/window/QUALIFY/aggregate-FILTER
semantics, implicit casts, date arithmetic). A third engine whose limitations differ
from Postgres tests whether the zero-divergence result generalizes.

Engine choice: DataFusion. It (a) has an existing BenchBox adapter, (b) is in-process
(no service container - the cheapest possible CI cost), and (c) has a DIFFERENT gap
profile from Postgres: its limitations are in PHYSICAL PLANNING of correlated
EXISTS/IN/scalar sub-queries (plus a missing LIST aggregate and an empty-tuple parser
gap), whereas Postgres's are select-list-alias-in-HAVING/WHERE and aggregate-in-window.
This is still a SAMPLE, not a 20-engine matrix; the DuckDB gate stays the hard blocker.

description:
TPC-Havoc's premise is that the 10 SQL (and DataFrame) variants of each
TPC-H query are structurally diverse but SEMANTICALLY EQUIVALENT to the
canonical TPC-H query. Nothing in the default run or in CI enforces that
equivalence: `benchbox run --benchmark tpchavoc` reports execution success
("Success rate: 100%") while never comparing any variant to the canonical
answer, and the develop correctness gate validates TPC-H, not TPC-Havoc
variants. A fast-but-wrong variant therefore makes a platform look good for
executing the WRONG query, silently corrupting the performance comparison the
benchmark exists to produce.

benchbox already ships the comparison primitive:
`TPCHavocBenchmark.validate_variant_equivalence(...)`
(benchbox/core/tpchavoc/benchmark.py:242) delegates to
`ResultValidator.validate_results_exact` / `validate_results_checksum` /
`validate_query1_results`. But it is invoked only from unit tests with
synthetic inputs - no run path executes the canonical TPC-H query and feeds
`original_results` for a real variant. `--validate-results` is an opt-in flag
(default off) that routes through `ValidationConfig` without driving
per-variant equivalence for tpchavoc.

The cost of this gap is concrete and already realized. PR #756 fixed three
correlated-subquery self-binding defects (q2_v8, q11_v1, q17_v8) that were
silent for exactly this reason, and the same PR's verification surfaced a
fourth, different-class divergence: q2_v10 zeroes negative `s_acctbal` via a
CASE-wrapped projection (38 of 460 rows differ from canonical Q2 at SF=1). A
result-equivalence gate would have caught all four.

This TODO wires the EXISTING validator into a bounded, CI-affordable gate,
enumerates every current divergence, and (via the companion burndown TODO)
drives them to zero so the gate lands green. It is complementary to
`testing-approach-correctness-gates` (that gate checks TPC-H answers; this
one checks TPC-Havoc cross-variant equivalence) and should mirror its
bounded single-cell shape.
preserves: DuckDB tpchavoc stays 100% execution-green at SF 0.01 / 0.1 / 1.0.
ResultValidator tolerance and checksum semantics are unchanged.
benchbox run --benchmark tpchavoc default (execution-only) behavior stays available; the gate is additive.

description:
In the course of fixing clickhouse-local stress-test failures
(PR fix/clickhouse-local-stress, commits 4b6598786 / 6e344bdec /
451d228fc) we landed two correct-but-papering-over workarounds in the
platform layer:

1. `benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py` -- the DDL pipeline asks
   each benchmark for `dialect="duckdb"` and rewrites known DuckDB-only
   syntax in `_optimize_table_definition` (`Nullable() NOT NULL` strip,
   `FLOAT[N]` -> `Array(Float32)`, `DOUBLE[N]` -> `Array(Float64)`,
   ENGINE/ORDER BY injection). The cleaner shape would be for each
   benchmark schema to honour a real `dialect="clickhouse"` and emit
   ClickHouse-native DDL directly. We didn't do that because
   `transaction_primitives` and `write_primitives` drop their inline
   PRIMARY KEY when `dialect="clickhouse"` (per their pk_capability
   rule) and that PK string is what `_extract_primary_key_columns`
   reads to derive ORDER BY -- a global dialect swap would silently
   regress those tables to `ORDER BY tuple()`.

2. `benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/client.py` -- `ClickHouseLocalClient.execute()`
   uses `format="ArrowStream"` + pyarrow IPC decode instead of chDB's
   built-in `format="DataFrame"`, because the latter SIGABRTs
   (uncatchable) when the result contains a Tuple-typed column (e.g.
   `read_primitives.array_of_struct` returns `Array(Tuple(...))`). The
   SIGABRT also corrupts the on-disk `.chdb` directory (`recursive_mutex
   lock failed`), so subsequent benchmarks fail at session init with
   Code 722 / Code 36 BAD_ARGUMENTS. A `TODO(chdb-tuple-dataframe)`
   marker is in `_arrow_to_dataframe`.

Both workarounds are correct, but the underlying issues need upstream
fixes. Without explicit tracking, these workarounds will silently
linger after the upstream issues are resolved -- continuing to pay the
perf/clarity cost long after we could have reverted.

This TODO exists to:
- File the chdb DataFrame/Tuple SIGABRT upstream and link the issue
  from the `TODO(chdb-tuple-dataframe)` comment.
- Decide on a long-term plan for the DuckDB-as-ClickHouse-DDL hack
  (either fix the PK extraction to read schema metadata directly, or
  audit each schema for a real `dialect="clickhouse"` path).
- Keep a single index of every "papered over" platform workaround so
  future maintainers can sweep them when upstream catches up.
preserves: All benchmarks that currently land their inline PRIMARY KEY in the emitted DDL string (transaction_primitives, write_primitives) keep producing the same ORDER BY clause
ClickHouseLocalClient.execute() continues to handle SELECT, DDL, INSERT-no-params, and empty results correctly
Stress test (./scripts/local_stress_test.sh --scale 1 --platform clickhouse-local) still passes after any workaround replacement

Follow-up captured from the statistics-as-a-phase work (track2-joinorder-stats-phase,
landed via PR #980). That work delivered the first-class statistics phase
(load -> statistics -> query): the StatisticsGatheringPhase dataclass
(benchbox/core/results/models.py:131), the per-engine ANALYZE knob
(benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py:384 gather_statistics / :405
run_statistics_phase, with the Redshift auto-on-load override), phases.statistics
serialization, and the per-benchmark supports_statistics_phase opt-in.

It resolved exactly ONE of the four "Open design questions" in
_project/design/track2-joinorder-stats-as-phase.md (detect-and-disable vs
document auto-analyze -> "document", via stats_mode: auto-on-load). The
other three were NOT implemented and were not recorded as deferred on the
now-DONE seed, so this seed logs them:

  1. (REQUIRED for Track 2) Cold-stats vs warm-stats reset/persist control.
     The design doc states Track 2 needs BOTH fresh-stats and
     stale-stats-after-additional-load modes to study statistics maintenance,
     "so the phase must support an explicit reset/persist control". PR #980's
     phase only runs ANALYZE once after load; there is no way to reset stats,
     or to load more data and re-measure with deliberately stale stats. Without
     this, the replicated/sampled scale-stress work cannot exercise the
     stale-statistics axis at all.
  2. (OPTIONAL) Per-table stats-build breakdown. PR #980 reports an aggregate
     phase duration_ms plus a tables_analyzed count; the design doc's lean was

  3. (SANITY CHECK) Idempotence. Re-running ANALYZE on already-analyzed data
     should produce the same plan -- the check that the phase measures stats
     build, not incidental cache warmth. No such assertion exists.

deps.needs and must_preserve treat track2-joinorder-stats-phase (now DONE) as
"the statistics-phase requirement satisfied". That is only true for the phase
mechanics; the reset/persist control the stale-stats study depends on lives in

item so the stats-axis-ready signal is honest.

approach: Do not narrow the window - close it. Options, roughly in order of preference. (a) Add a maintenance/read-only mode to the tracker so writes are refused for the duration of a cutover; this is the only option that makes the guarantee structural rather than social, and it is reusable for future migrations. (b) Quiesce every other session out of band, then verify quiescence by taking two exports a few minutes apart and asserting the event count is unchanged - cheap, needs no code, but relies on nobody starting up mid-cutover. (c) Snapshot and restore back to back, then reconcile by diffing the live DB against the snapshot and replaying the delta; the audit chain makes replay awkward and this is the most error-prone. Whichever is chosen, the migration item's precondition should be replaced with an event-count-stability check rather than a claim check, because that is what actually detects concurrent writers.
description: migrate-hosted-tracker-db-to-todo-db-0-3-schema gates its destructive step on 'no other actor holds a live claim'. That is the wrong test and it has now been falsified with evidence. restore-legacy --replace rebuilds every table from a snapshot, so any write landing between snapshot and restore is destroyed silently - no error, and the resulting audit chain verifies cleanly because it is rehashed from the snapshot. Measured on 2026-07-31: a snapshot staged at 1718 items / 4419 events was already behind a live DB at 1720 items / 4424 events. The two extra items (agent-write-preflight-blocks-ephemeral-clones, standalone-todo-db-renew-verb) were created by actor root@vm - another Claude session - which held NO claim at any point while creating them. So the claim check read clear while writes were landing. Claims cover claim/start/done/complete on existing items; they do not cover create, defer, promote, block or config writes. work.evidence: DECISION: maintenance mode (leased write freeze), with verified quiescence demoted to a corroborating probe. Rationale: quiescence alone is unsound - it samples the past and cannot bind the future, and the cutover window is minutes. Evidence this session: three reads 5min apart were identical (events count=4440 last_seq=4440 latest=2026-07-31T16:38:10Z), yet the DB had still moved 1720->1726 items and 4424->4440 events earlier the same day, and joe@joe-mac-mini.local holds a live claim. 'Quiet now' is not 'quiet during the restore'. Reconcile-after was rejected: restore-legacy --replace destroys interleaved writes silently and the rebuilt chain re-hashes clean from the snapshot, so there is no post-hoc signal to reconcile against. Implemented as a leased freeze (todo freeze / --status / --release) gating every mutating command in main(); TTL-expiry satisfies the no-stuck-lock must-preserve, and a no-freeze DB is unaffected. Also added stats['events'] write-activity fingerprint - the quiescence probe was previously unimplementable (see w2 note). 32 new tests in tests/unit/scripts/test_todo_db_freeze.py; full suite 1233 passed.

approach: Narrow the except to the failures that genuinely mean 'cannot classify' - FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, UnicodeDecodeError, the CompressionError already imported - and let anything else propagate. Decide deliberately what an unreadable file should mean: returning False is a guess, and raising is probably right for a data file the caller is about to parse anyway. description: benchbox/utils/file_format.py::_check_first_nonempty_line wraps its whole body in 'except Exception: return False'. Any failure reading the probe file - permissions, truncation, a decode failure, a broken compressed stream - is silently reported as 'this file has no trailing delimiter' rather than surfacing. That is not a neutral default: for a file that DOES carry a trailing delimiter, the caller then omits the synthetic column and PyArrow fails downstream with a column-count mismatch that names neither the real cause nor the file. Ten callers depend on this classification: duckdb.py:408, datafusion.py:903 and :1425, polars_platform.py:544, and the pandas/dask/pyspark/cudf/modin/datafusion dataframe adapters. Found while working crlf-framing-coverage-and-text-mode-invariant (PR #1355); that item pinned the CRLF text-mode invariant and deliberately did not widen into error handling, so this was left unlogged until an end-of-effort audit. Note the interaction: the blanket except is exactly what would convert a future binary-read change into a silent misclassification, which is why #1355's docstring calls it out.

Narrowing still swallows; the question 'does this file have a trailing delimiter' has no answer when the file cannot be read, and every one of the eleven call sites passes a path it is about to load, so surfacing the original error is strictly more useful than guessing. Only one False remains and it means 'answered': a file with no non-empty line genuinely has no framing. ADDITIONAL finding beyond the pinned evidence (confirmed empirically,
not just by inspection - a real `--tuning tuned` duckdb run produced
`platform.tuning: null`, not merely hash-absent): `tuning_enabled` and
`unified_tuning_configuration` never reached the adapter's `__init__`
AT ALL for the CLI's non-interactive/direct run path (`_run_direct`,
dry-run, load-only) - `db_manager.create_config()` only folds
overrides into `DatabaseConfig.options` (nested), while
`PlatformAdapter.__init__` reads them as top-level kwargs via
`from_config()`. This meant `effective_tuning_config` was always None
and no tuning was ever physically applied for these paths (confirmed
for duckdb and postgresql; only questdb's from_config already forwarded
both keys correctly). This is a genuinely separate, more severe,
pre-existing defect from what this TODO's evidence anticipated - fixing
it was a hard prerequisite for verifying w1-w4 end-to-end (otherwise
`effective_tuning_config` is always None and there is nothing to attach
provenance to). Fixed narrowly: run.py now promotes tuning_enabled/

DatabaseConfig: it is a pydantic model, and model_dump() (used
downstream to build platform_config) recursively serializes
dataclass-valued extra fields to plain dicts, which would hand the
adapter a dict instead of a UnifiedTuningConfiguration instance. Fixed
adapter.py to read the config object from the existing, already-

always passes it through as a live object reference).
A companion systemic gap - the SAME tuning_enabled/

description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review of the tuning subsystem (executable proofs, not speculation).

Defect 1 (C1, false applied_verified): corroborate() iterates ledger.executed_statements only (benchbox/core/tuning/introspection.py:481), so a STATEMENT_FAILED entry neither blocks the upgrade nor appears in the receipt. Reachable sequence: Snowflake run tuning two tables; table A's ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY executes and corroborates, table B's fails and is swallowed with a warning (benchbox/platforms/snowflake.py:1743-1744); overall_status derives applied_unverified; _corroborate_applied_ledger (benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py:1129-1130) upgrades to applied_verified while the same .applied.json carries B's failed entry. Reproduced with a constructed ledger: corroborated=True.

Defect 2 (R1): corroborate() never reads ledger.dropped, so a capability-filtered intent (record_dropped) leaves no receipt entry and a sibling corroborated statement mints applied_verified for a run whose requested tuning was knowingly not applied.

Defect 3 (R3): overall_status (benchbox/core/tuning/applied_ledger.py:228-232) returns applied_unverified when ANY statement executed, including PHASE_SESSION cache hygiene (e.g. Snowflake ALTER SESSION SET USE_CACHED_RESULT, recorded at base/adapter.py:916). A tuned run whose every ddl/post_load statement failed still reports applied_unverified instead of failed. Reproduced.

The trust rule (docs/development/tuning-introspection-receipts.md:17-33) is silent on failed statements and dropped intents; nothing authorizes ignoring them, and the review invariant is 'record LESS, never over-certify'. Semantics to implement: (a) a failed ddl/post_load statement blocks the upgrade and appears in the receipt with a blocking verdict; (b) any dropped intent blocks the upgrade and is surfaced in the receipt payload; (c) session-phase failures stay non-blocking for the upgrade (transient class) but see (d): overall_status returns failed when ddl/post_load statements were attempted and ALL failed, regardless of session-phase successes; a session-SET-only ledger keeps today's applied_unverified semantics.
preserves: Capture never breaks a run: every record/derive/corroborate path stays non-raising and degrades to debug logs.
Existing receipt payload fields keep their names and shapes; additions only (explorer ingests the receipt verbatim).
Session SET/PRAGMA statements remain transient: they neither earn nor block verification, and a session-only ledger still derives applied_unverified.
applied_ledger_hash stays a hash over ordered EXECUTED statements only (ADR-001 physical identity) - failed statements must NOT enter the hash.
applied_verified remains reachable ONLY via corroborate() from applied_unverified; overall_status never returns it.
title: Corroboration gate must refuse applied_verified when the ledger holds failed ddl/post_load statements or dropped intents; all-physical-failed runs must not report applied_unverified

approach: For each nit: first write the pinning test that documents today's behavior, then either fix minimally or record the wontfix rationale next to the pin. N1's minimal fix is stripping quoted strings and comments before regex classification (shared helper, applied in _classify and _statement_table). N2 is a two-line guard in _match_object. N3 replaces the substring check with the same clause-shape regex the classifier uses. N5 is a design note decision (qualify table identity through the Introspector contract) - likely wontfix-with-pin at this priority.
description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review: fail-closed-in-practice smells worth guarding so they cannot silently become defects. Land after tuning-corroboration-gate-failed-and-dropped-20260801 (same files). Each may individually be closed as wontfix with a recorded rationale + pinning test; the deliverable is that none of these behaviors is LATENT anymore.

N1: _classify's key-clause regexes (_ORDER_BY_RE etc., introspection.py:239-253) match text inside string literals/comments - probe: CREATE TABLE t (c String DEFAULT 'order by (l_shipdate)') ... ORDER BY (real_col) parses the LITERAL as the sort clause (first match wins) and never sees the real clause. Direction today is fail-closed (catalog reflects the real clause -> mismatch), unreachable from shipped generators - but it is a correctness landmine for any future schema carrying such text.

N2: _match_object corroborates an empty-columns intent against an empty-columns fact (probe: ORDER BY () vs a fact with columns=()). Unreachable today - all three shipped introspectors skip empty keys - but a future introspector emitting an empty-columns fact would create trivial corroboration. Guard: intents/facts with no columns never corroborate.

N3: _record_tuned_sort_key_op early-returns on the substring check '"ORDER BY" in original_statement.upper()' (clickhouse/workload.py:223): a partition-only tuned table whose SOURCE DDL contains that substring anywhere (literal, comment) is applied but never recorded - under-recording that lets sibling tables carry the run to verified without this table's partition being corroborated. Not constructible from shipped schemas.

N5: introspector fact matching is bare-table-name only (all three introspectors filter/emit unqualified names; _match_object compares normalized names) - a cross-schema shadow object with the same name and columns can supply the corroborating fact. No realistic false-verified constructed (an executed statement implies the real table's catalog fact), but schema-qualified matching would remove the ambiguity class.
preserves: Classification stays platform-agnostic generic-SQL-shape; no per-platform parsing enters _classify.
Every change keeps or strengthens fail-closed direction; nothing widens what can corroborate.
Shipped-generator behavior is bit-identical: these guards must not change any current verdict for statements the generators emit (pin with regression vectors).
The gate semantics from tuning-corroboration-gate-failed-and-dropped-20260801 are untouched.
title: Corroboration hardening nits: string-literal clause matching, empty-columns trivial corroboration, ORDER BY substring recording guard, bare-name table matching

description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review doc-vs-code sweep. Fix after (and consistent with) tuning-corroboration-gate-failed-and-dropped-20260801, which changes the trust rule these docs describe.

A1 (Required, doc contradicts code): docs/development/tuning-introspection-receipts.md:89-105 says DuckDB's CTAS 'drops that index... a sorting-only run honestly stays applied_unverified' and calls the fix out of scope - but benchbox/platforms/duckdb.py:961-1020 now re-creates idx_<table>_sort post-CTAS (_recreate_sort_index_after_ctas) and records it precisely so the run can verify. Stale at birth (both shipped in 30dcc8a).

A2 (vocabulary): _VERIFIABLE_VERDICTS includes UNVERIFIABLE (introspection.py:64), so summary.verifiable_total (introspection.py:190) counts no-rule/blocked statements the doc defines as NOT verifiable (receipts doc:27-29,52). Gate outcome unaffected. Decide: rename the summary key (it has zero production consumers - verified in the review) or redefine it in the doc; either way make code and doc agree.

A4: ADR-001:120-124 says the ledger is populated only via the recording proxy; the direct ClickHouse record-at-execute (workload.py:76) and the deferred _applied_layout_operations fold (adapter.py:1181-1206 - reconstructed position, not observed) are undocumented there.

A5: receipts doc:44 'order- and case-normal' is ambiguous; comparison is order-sensitive for every kind (introspection.py:441-444). Say 'in order' on all four rows.

A6: transient/maintenance prefix sets are wider than the doc table - RESET/USE transient, VACUUM/ANALYZE/COMPACT maintenance (introspection.py:264-265) - i.e. statements the doc routes to the blocking 'anything else' row are silently non-blocking. Document (or narrow) deliberately.

A7: receipts doc:129 stale '~line 984' wiring pointer (now adapter.py:1017-1033/1097).

A3: ADR-001:130-142 sample statement record shows 'mechanism': null fields the hashed to_dict() omits (applied_ledger.py:138-150) - the documented shape is not the hashed shape.

A9: ADR-003 context is stale with no addendum: OLAP pack condition inverted (clickhouse/tuning.py:91 applies when tuning_enabled), generators now render in execution (workload.py per ADR-3 single renderer), generate_tuning_clause dead-code note obsolete.

R6: document the Snowflake key-vs-physical-clustering semantics asymmetry if not already landed by snowflake-clustering-precheck-and-schema-filter-20260801.
preserves: ADR decision history stays intact - addenda only, no rewriting of recorded decisions.

If verifiable_total is renamed, receipt summary changes are additive/renamed-with-tests only; the upgrade gate logic is untouched.

description:
From the 2026-07-12 tuning review, finding R5 (evidence pinned to commit acfb8992).

- BENCHBOX_TUNING_ENABLED sets config key tuning.enabled which NOTHING at
  runtime reads (only reader is a test); yet docs/usage/configuration.md:91-94
  and docs/reference/cli/configuration.md:93 claim it activates tuned runs in CI.
- examples/tunings/README.md is wholesale stale: documents a --tuning-config
  flag that does not exist, example scripts that do not exist, stale flat
  filenames, an env-var recipe that cannot work, and an unqualified "2-10x"
  performance promise.
- The actual precedence order (flag default notuning -> keyword/path -> yaml
  default_config_file [BENCHBOX_TUNING_CONFIG] -> BENCHBOX_TUNING_PATH ->
  cwd-relative examples/ -> cwd -> fallback) is documented nowhere.
- --tuning auto on SQL platforms prints "using smart defaults based on system
  profile" but delivers a default-constructed config (run.py:1021-1024);
  real smart defaults exist only for DataFrame mode (tuning_runtime.py:49-92).
- docs/reference/cli/tuning.md: wrong --output default, three subcommands
  (list/show/platforms) undocumented.
preserves: BENCHBOX_TUNING_CONFIG and BENCHBOX_TUNING_PATH behavior exactly as implemented

description:
The last leg of the ADR-001 trust story (docs/development/
tuning-adr-001-trust-and-hash-semantics.md names introspection receipts as
the design direction; the applied-ledger work deliberately left
applied_verified unclaimable). After tuning application and data load,
introspect the live schema (SHOW CREATE TABLE / information_schema /
duckdb_constraints) per platform, compare against the ledger's executed DDL
intents, and emit a receipt into the .tuning.json companion. For tuned
ClickHouse runs the applied ledger also records session SETs, not just DDL
(benchbox/core/tuning/applied_ledger.py); introspection must corroborate
every ledgered entry of every kind, DDL and session-setting readback alike,
before validation_status upgrades to applied_verified. A run whose schema
matches while a session setting was ignored or reset must not receive
applied_verified. Mismatches (of either kind) downgrade with a diff list.
Introspection failure is non-fatal and leaves applied_unverified (never
blocks a run).
preserves: Introspection never fails or slows a run materially (bounded queries, non-fatal)
applied_verified is claimable ONLY via corroboration - never derived from the ledger alone

description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review of benchbox/core/tuning/metadata.py (982 lines) and platforms/base/validation.py. Four defects with concrete failing sequences, all of the form 'reused DB accepted although its physical tuning differs from what the run's bundle claims':

M1 (extra tunings pass): metadata.py:805-812 - missing tables are errors but extra tables only add_warning; is_valid stays True and connection_lifecycle.py:246-258 reuses on is_valid. Sequence: run 1 tunes lineitem+orders (metadata saved for both); run 2's config tunes only orders -> extra 'lineitem' = warning -> DB reused; the bundle's requested_config_hash and tunings_applied describe an orders-only tuning while lineitem's physical layout persists; drift_check reports is_valid:true.

M2 (PK/FK drift invisible): constraint enablement is neither persisted (column rows metadata.py:466-488; section markers cover only unique/check + platform optimizations, metadata.py:226-259) nor compared (_compare_tuning_configurations metadata.py:785-821 compares tables only; rebuilt existing side gets dataclass defaults at metadata.py:683). Sequence: run 1 with primary_keys.enabled=true; run 2 reuses with enabled=false, identical table tunings -> clean pass; a 'no-PK' labeled run executes against a PK-constrained database.

M3 (sort attribute drift invisible): persistence keeps only (table, tuning_type, name, order) (metadata.py:477-488, rebuilt with type=UNKNOWN at 716-722); comparison reduces to (name, order) tuples (metadata.py:840-843). ASC re-requested as DESC (different physical layout on platforms honoring direction) passes clean. Same for nulls_position/compression.

M4 (notuning reuse unchecked): platforms/base/validation.py:118-139 - both branches require adapter.tuning_enabled; with tuning disabled neither the drift comparison nor even the 'database contains tuning metadata' warning runs. A physically tuned DB is reused and published as a notuning baseline.

Compounding smells to address opportunistically: B5 marker-write failures are silent (metadata.py:280-282) and missing markers are warnings (319-326), so section drift detection can be silently absent; B6 any load exception maps to None (657-660) then reported as 'No tuning metadata found' (767-768), misattributing connectivity failures; B7 _METADATA_SCHEMA_VERSION is written but never read (169-174); TuningMetadataManager queries go through platform_config, not the connection_config under validation (186-188 vs 300,617,647).
preserves: Existing DBs with pre-change metadata get a deterministic, explained outcome via the schema version read path - not spurious drift errors.
Fail-closed direction on validation errors: unreadable/ambiguous metadata leads to recreate-or-refuse, never silent reuse.
Metadata persistence failure stays non-fatal to the run (tuning_metadata_saved flag semantics unchanged).
drift_check remains descriptive in the .applied.json companion and can never be a source of applied_verified (ADR-001 addendum).

description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review of benchbox/core/tuning/metadata.py (982 lines) and platforms/base/validation.py. Four defects with concrete failing sequences, all of the form 'reused DB accepted although its physical tuning differs from what the run's bundle claims':

M1 (extra tunings pass): metadata.py:805-812 - missing tables are errors but extra tables only add_warning; is_valid stays True and connection_lifecycle.py:246-258 reuses on is_valid. Sequence: run 1 tunes lineitem+orders (metadata saved for both); run 2's config tunes only orders -> extra 'lineitem' = warning -> DB reused; the bundle's requested_config_hash and tunings_applied describe an orders-only tuning while lineitem's physical layout persists; drift_check reports is_valid:true.

M2 (PK/FK drift invisible): constraint enablement is neither persisted (column rows metadata.py:466-488; section markers cover only unique/check + platform optimizations, metadata.py:226-259) nor compared (_compare_tuning_configurations metadata.py:785-821 compares tables only; rebuilt existing side gets dataclass defaults at metadata.py:683). Sequence: run 1 with primary_keys.enabled=true; run 2 reuses with enabled=false, identical table tunings -> clean pass; a 'no-PK' labeled run executes against a PK-constrained database.

M3 (sort attribute drift invisible): persistence keeps only (table, tuning_type, name, order) (metadata.py:477-488, rebuilt with type=UNKNOWN at 716-722); comparison reduces to (name, order) tuples (metadata.py:840-843). ASC re-requested as DESC (different physical layout on platforms honoring direction) passes clean. Same for nulls_position/compression.

M4 (notuning reuse unchecked): platforms/base/validation.py:118-139 - both branches require adapter.tuning_enabled; with tuning disabled neither the drift comparison nor even the 'database contains tuning metadata' warning runs. A physically tuned DB is reused and published as a notuning baseline.

Compounding smells to address opportunistically: B5 marker-write failures are silent (metadata.py:280-282) and missing markers are warnings (319-326), so section drift detection can be silently absent; B6 any load exception maps to None (657-660) then reported as 'No tuning metadata found' (767-768), misattributing connectivity failures; B7 _METADATA_SCHEMA_VERSION is written but never read (169-174); TuningMetadataManager queries go through platform_config, not the connection_config under validation (186-188 vs 300,617,647).
preserves: Existing DBs with pre-change metadata get a deterministic, explained outcome via the schema version read path - not spurious drift errors.
Fail-closed direction on validation errors: unreadable/ambiguous metadata leads to recreate-or-refuse, never silent reuse.
Metadata persistence failure stays non-fatal to the run (tuning_metadata_saved flag semantics unchanged).
drift_check remains descriptive in the .applied.json companion and can never be a source of applied_verified (ADR-001 addendum).
title: Drift validation for reused databases passes when it should fail: extra table tunings, PK/FK enablement, sort attributes, and notuning-reuse are all invisible

description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review (doc-vs-code sweep).

Defect (A8/D2): benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:359 records tuning_mode=None for an explicit --tuning notuning run. ADR-002 (docs/development/tuning-adr-002-mode-vocabulary-fallback-facets.md, section 2, lines 55-66) requires absent-vs-notuning to stay distinct ('never coerced'); the None coercion makes explicit baseline runs land in the NOT_RECORDED facet downstream and stop exact-matching other notuning runs in comparison surfaces.

Residue: benchbox/core/schemas.py:497 still carries the exact pre-decision comment ADR-002 quotes as the bug ('# "tuned", "notuning", "auto", or path'), documenting the outlawed vocabulary as current; schemas.py:550-551 replays tuning_mode verbatim as a --tuning argument (legitimate for path replay, but the comment must describe the pinned vocabulary from benchbox/core/tuning/modes.py).

Verified consistent while reviewing (do not churn): the vocabulary pin itself (modes.py), fallback labeling (tuning_resolver.py:152), and the --official refusal (run.py:138-158).
preserves: Absent (never specified) stays distinct from explicit notuning in every recorded artifact - the fix must not reverse-coerce absent into notuning.
ExecutionContext replay (schemas.py:550-551) keeps round-tripping path-based --tuning values byte-for-byte.
The --official gate behavior (run.py:138-158) is unchanged.
The pinned mode vocabulary in benchbox/core/tuning/modes.py is the single source of truth; no new mode strings are invented.

description:
From the 2026-07-12 tuning review, finding R1 (evidence pinned to commit acfb8992).

benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py:714 calls
`validate_for_platform(self.platform_name)` with the human display string
("ClickHouse (Local)", "StarRocks"). TuningType.is_compatible_with_platform
(benchbox/core/tuning/interface.py:79-164) lowercases it and looks it up in a
map keyed by canonical types ("clickhouse"), so multi-word display names match
nothing and every enabled tuning type errors -> ValueError after data
generation. Verified empirically: a default-constructed config (constraints
default enabled=True) yields 4 errors on StarRocks / "ClickHouse (Local)" /
Doris / Trino; even the key "clickhouse" fails on default-enabled
foreign_keys/check_constraints. TuningMetadataManager also persists the display
name into the metadata table (benchbox/core/tuning/metadata.py:207).

Fix: introduce a canonical platform-type accessor on adapters (the CLI key,
e.g. database_config.type) and route every tuning-capability lookup and
metadata persistence through it. Also decide-in-code the unknown-platform
behavior explicitly (warn + treat as no-capability, never a crash keyed on
string formatting).

description:
Confirmed during PR #1198's implementation and its Opus review (2026-07-17).
A repo-wide search finds ZERO production call sites for any adapter's
generate_tuning_clause (singular) mixin — every hit is in tests. Production
rendering flows through the DDL generators' generate_tuning_clauses
(plural; core/dryrun.py, duckdb.py) or #1180's registry-driven paths.

Yet five pre-existing #1180-era registry entries claim physical DDL
rendering via that dead mixin (rendered_via="ddl",
mechanism "adapter_mixin:<Platform>Adapter.generate_tuning_clause"):
postgresql, snowflake, redshift, bigquery, mysql. For postgresql it is
affirmatively false (PostgreSQLAdapter.generate_tuning_clause
unconditionally returns "" - postgresql.py:898-903 - and
apply_table_tunings is a no-op). The others follow the same pattern and
need individual verification. An evaluator consulting the registry (or
`benchbox tuning platforms`, now generated from it) would believe tuned
runs on these platforms physically render tuning DDL when they may not.

Fix: verify each of the five against its real execution path; correct each
entry to honest rendered_via (likely "none" with per-platform notes, or
"ddl" only where a generator is actually consumed at execution); extend
the capability-source drift test so a mechanism claim naming a dead
code path fails (e.g. assert claimed adapter_mixin symbols have
production call sites, or retire the adapter_mixin mechanism vocabulary
entirely in favor of generator-backed mechanisms).
preserves: PR #1198's 9 rendered_via=none entries and the emptied allowlist
validate_for_platform behavior for platforms with real tuned rendering (duckdb, clickhouse per #1180)

Added an opt-in exclude_internal keyword to sanitize_platform_options()
(default False, preserving existing call sites' behavior). When True it
drops underscore-prefixed keys and _INTERNAL_OPTION_KEYS, matching
_iter_public_options semantics, and propagates recursively through
nested Mapping values. Set exclude_internal=True at every export-facing
call site: runtime_metadata.py:105 (platform_raw_config, the leak site
named in the finding), runtime_metadata.py:450 (_raw_platform_metadata,

work.notes:
_sanitize_option_value no longer falls back to str(value)/repr() for
any caller. If the value exposes a callable to_dict(), that result is
used (recursively sanitized, including secret redaction and, when
requested, internal-key filtering); if to_dict() raises, or the value
has no to_dict, the key's value becomes the marker string
"<unserializable:TypeName>" (key itself is preserved per the
anti_patterns note - only the opaque value is replaced). This applies
unconditionally (not just when exclude_internal=True) since there is no
legitimate reason to publish a raw Python repr from any call site.
Wrapped the to_dict() call in try/except so a broken to_dict()
implementation can't raise out of bundle emission.
work.summary: Replace the str() fallback for non-JSON-able values on exported paths: use to_dict() when available, else drop the key with a captured warning marker

(2) Apply clustering POST-LOAD via ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY, mirroring snowflake.py, since Snowpark writes plain tables via save_as_table/COPY INTO. (3) Native Snowflake first. Step 1 landed as PR #1371 (snowflake-cluster-key-corroboration-20260730): the shared classifier now understands ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY and a SnowflakeTuningIntrospector corroborates it against INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CLUSTERING_KEY. This item is now a FEATURE task, not a capture task: make Snowpark apply a post-load clustering key, after which capture and corroboration are inherited. Still blocked pending that implementation; unblock when someone picks it up.

description:
Test-strategy review of the UAT harness (`tests/uat/`) found four
independent ways the accounting can overstate corpus coverage or hide
failures - none of them are individually catastrophic, but together they
mean the "total_defined" denominator and the report exit code cannot be
trusted at face value:

(a) `tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py:94-95` - `enumerate_cells_with_pruning`
    iterates `benchmark_list` and does `info = benchmarks.get(benchmark);
    if info is None: continue` for benchmarks named in the config that
    are absent from the registry. This is a silent drop: no
    `CompatibilityPrunedCell` row, no log line, no accounting entry at
    all - the benchmark simply vanishes from both `cells` and
    `compatibility_pruned`, and downstream `total_defined_count`
    (report.py:165, `attempted + skipped + unreachable`) never knew it
    was supposed to exist. A typo'd benchmark name in a sweep config
    fails this way with zero signal.

(b) `tests/uat/matrix.py:302-319` (`filter_scales_by_registry`) drops
    requested scales that fall outside a benchmark's declared
    `scale_options` ("ladder pruning"). Confirmed via
    `tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py:108-111`: the filtered-out scales are
    just absent from `filtered` - there is no equivalent of
    `compatibility_pruned` for registry/ladder-based drops. Only
    compatibility-RULE prunes (platform/benchmark incompatibility) get an
    accounting row; ladder prunes (scale outside registry bounds) get
    none. `tests/uat/phases/report.py` has no ladder-pruned counter
    field/parameter at all, so this class of denominator shrinkage cannot
    even be reported if a caller wanted to.

(c) Regenerating a report from a `cells.jsonl` whose sidecar
    `cells.jsonl.accounting.json` is missing silently reports
    `unreachable=0` and drops the `release_gate_attention` flag. This
    is DELIBERATE and already pinned by
    `tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py:116-143`
    (`test_report_cli_without_sidecar_defaults_unreachable_zero`,
    docstring: "Older artifacts predate the sidecar; the report must
    still regenerate.") - flagged here as a real gap worth revisiting,
    not a bug to fix outright: silently defaulting to 0 for OLDER
    artifacts trades one risk (crashing on legitimate legacy re-runs)
    for another (a report that looks clean when unreachable-ness was
    simply never computed). Decide in w1 whether the harness should
    instead surface a visible "sidecar missing, unreachable count
    unknown" marker distinct from "sidecar present, unreachable=0" for
    genuinely clean runs.

(d) `tests/uat/phases/report.py:54-57` -
    `ReportSummary.exit_code()` returns `2` if aborted, else `1` only
    if `cross_scale_floor_breached` (an OPT-IN check - `cross_scale_floor`
    defaults to `None` at report.py:51/142 and is only enforced when a
    caller explicitly passes it), else `0`. This means a report full of
    `fail`/`timeout`/`unreachable` cells still exits `0` unless the
    caller happens to have opted into the cross-scale floor check - CI
    or a human eyeballing an exit code alone would see "success" for a
    corpus that mostly failed.

uat-clickhouse-server-ddl-compatibility,

uat-clickhouse-server-query-compatibility, uat-docker-stack-recovery) are
all about specific run evidence, platform defects, or re-run ordering -
none touch the enumerate/matrix/report accounting code itself, so there
is no overlap. Blind-spots
`_project/blind-spots/2026-05-03-081920/081921/081922-*.md` are related
in spirit (all about UAT reporting overstating what was actually
exercised/validated) but cover different axes - cross-scale checklist
enforcement, validator-clean-rate tracking, and submission terminal-state
ambiguity, respectively - not the enumerate/ladder/sidecar/exit-code
issues here. No true duplicate found.

work.notes:
Two options, pick one and document the decision inline in
report.py's module docstring:
  1. Change `ReportSummary.exit_code()` default behavior so any
     `fail_count > 0 or timeout_count > 0 or unreachable_count > 0`
     returns non-zero (e.g. `1`), independent of the opt-in
     cross_scale_floor check. This makes "report exit code == 0"
     mean "everything attempted actually passed."
  2. Keep today's lenient default (exit 0 unless cross-scale floor
     breached) but add an explicit `--strict` CLI flag to the report
     phase that opts into failing on any fail/timeout/unreachable
     count, for callers (e.g. release-gate automation) that want a
     hard gate.
Recommendation: prefer option 2 (additive `--strict` flag) if any
existing caller currently depends on today's lenient default (check
`tests/uat/cli.py` and any Makefile targets that call `uat report`
before deciding) - otherwise option 1 is the more honest default.
This decision blocks w4 (exit_code implementation/tests).

DECISION (2026-07-04): Option 1 (default-strict), no --strict flag.
Evidence gathered before deciding:
  - The UAT CLI file is actually `tests/uat/_cli.py` (the YAML's
    `tests/uat/cli.py` does not exist - naming drift; `_cli.py` is the
    argparse entry point `make uat-report` calls via
    `python -m tests.uat._cli report`). Its `_handle_report` prints
    the report's exit code straight through (`return summary.exit_code()`)
    with no branching, `|| true`, or exit-code interpretation.
  - `Makefile`'s `uat-report` target (~line 1983) just shells out to
    `python -m tests.uat._cli report ...`; it does not inspect or
    branch on the resulting exit code either.
  - Grepped `.github/workflows/` for `uat-report`/`uat report`/`_cli
    report`: no matches. No CI workflow parses or gates on this exit
    code today.
  - The UAT orchestrator (`tests/uat/orchestrator.py`, out of scope)
    already folds the report phase's `exit_code()` into
    `SweepResult.exit_code()` via `max(phase_exit_codes.values())`; no
    orchestrator or e2e test (`test_orchestrator.py`,
    `test_e2e_integration.py`) asserts `exit_code() == 0` for a run
    containing an actual fail/timeout/unreachable cell outside of the
    aborted/cross-scale-floor-breached cases that already return
    nonzero.
  - The only place that DID rely on the old lenient default was this
    TODO's own test suite: `tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py`'s
    `test_report_cli_reconciles_skipped_and_unreachable_fixture`
    (fixture has a failed + an unreachable cell) and
    `test_report_cli_reads_skipped_unreachable_sidecar` (sidecar
    reports 3 unreachable) both asserted `exit_code == 0` - updated to
    `exit_code == 1` as part of w4, per the anti-pattern's own carve-out
    for updating tests, not because anything outside the test suite
    depended on the leniency.
Conclusion: no real caller depends on "exit 0 despite failures," so
option 1 (the more honest default) was chosen over the additive
`--strict` flag. Full reasoning is duplicated in
`tests/uat/phases/report.py`'s module docstring.
work.summary: Decide (d) exit-code policy: non-zero exit on failures by default, or an explicit --strict flag

description:
The 2026-05-28/29 native + docker UAT runs could not be approved partly
because the *evidence* was incomplete, not only because cells failed. An
adversarial review of these run dirs found the process blockers below
(paths under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/):

- uat_complete_native_20260528_20260528: aborted on the /tmp disk floor
  in the execute phase. Only resume.json survived; no matrix_summary.tsv,
  no validator_rollup.tsv, no report footer. validate/package/
  explorer_smoke/report never ran.
- uat_complete_native_remaining_non_oltp_20260528_20260529 (dataframe):
  no manifests at all (no resume.json, cells.jsonl, uat_lifecycle.log,
  matrix_summary.tsv). Pass/fail was only reconstructable from per-cell
  result JSONs.
- NO_JSON failures (e.g. duckdb write_primitives/ai_primitives, all
  modin-df cells) captured ZERO error text: the per-cell log held only
  the command header (run with --quiet), and the tee log
  /tmp/uat-logs/native_non_oltp_20260528.log was 0 bytes.
- No git commit SHA is recorded in any artifact; result JSONs carry only
  driver versions (e.g. duckdb 1.3.2), so runs cannot be pinned to source.

This item makes the framework emit a complete, source-traceable artifact
for EVERY sweep, including aborted ones, so a reviewer can always prove
source SHA, command, phase status, terminal state, and failure cause.

Implementation correction from current code reading: the cited
tests/uat/phases/execute.py:708 line is Docker command detail handling,
not CellResult stderr storage. Per-cell subprocess output is already
written to each durable cell log by tests/uat/runner.py; the remediation
reads a bounded tail from that log and stamps the tail/classification into
cells.jsonl while appending a UAT_FAILURE_TAIL block for failed or
missing-result cells. This avoids adding output text to CellResult or
re-capturing subprocess streams per cell.

Original evidence pin: the stale line references above were from commit
da6a33c14. This implementation re-confirmed the drift on current develop
before relying on the code path.
preserves: No new always-on subprocess cost on the hot per-cell path beyond writing already-captured text.
Successful (non-aborted) sweeps emit byte-identical artifacts to today apart from the new SHA fields and richer status column.

description:
Once the framework and defect fixes land, a clean release-gate sweep must
be run — and its ordering and approval criteria must be explicit, because
the 2026-05-28/29 evidence had two structural problems beyond cell
failures:

- Ordering: the docker non-OLTP run started 2026-05-28 23:14, but a
  native-execution dataframe sweep ran afterwards (2026-05-29 01:17-07:50).
  A Docker stack began before all native/dataframe platforms had completed,
  so cross-run release-gate value is compromised.
- Completeness: no run reached validate/package/explorer_smoke/report; no
  matrix_summary.tsv or validator_rollup.tsv exists for any run.

Release-gate re-run contract:
  1. native SQL platforms first
  2. dataframe (native-execution) platforms second
  3. Docker non-OLTP stacks third
  4. Docker OLTP stacks last
Run sequentially, one platform at a time; lifecycle logs must prove native
completion before any Docker stack starts. Use a FRESH run root (not the
failed 2026-05-28 dirs), BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs,
a recorded seed, non-OLTP scales 0.01/0.1/1, OLTP scale 0.01.

APPROVAL GATE — APPROVE only if every non-blocked locally-testable platform
reaches the report phase and all required, non-pruned cells pass. HOLD if
ANY of: missing manifests, missing commit SHA, DuckDB reference failures,
a Docker zero-cell run, a hung platform, or a NO_JSON without error text.

assessment, 2026-07-16). That item's Bucket A (empty numeric/date source
values) cannot land its DDL/loader work (w2, success_metrics) until this

correctness expectation.

The question: for an empty numeric/date value in the source data, should the
ClickHouse-server loader emit/preserve `Nullable(T)` DDL for that column, or
coerce the empty to a type default under a non-Nullable column?

therefore query answers), so it must be ratified against the benchmark
schema's own nullability semantics rather than chosen for loader
convenience. The parent already records a recommended default (see
recommended_resolution); this item exists to make that call explicit,
ratify it against TPC schema nullability, and record the rejected path as
deferred so the parent's w2 is unambiguous.

description:
2026-07-21 adversarial UAT review finding (P0): the remediation that made ClickHouse vector_search and datavault SF=0.01 pass live exists ONLY as unmerged local commit 5f266e76f on branch fix/uat-clickhouse-loader-nullability-dialect (no remote, no PR). origin/develop@9f69c53c6 still loses all nullability: _optimize_table_definition (benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py:70-154) never adds Nullable(...), so bare DuckDB types from schema_primitives.py:52-56 reach ClickHouse as NOT NULL while the value converter correctly emits None (data_loading.py:2148-2203) -> live failures 'NoneType has no attribute year/tzinfo' (TPC-DS date/DataVault load_end_dts) and integer None rejection.

The stranded commit is NOT mergeable as-is; four defects found by review:
1. Wraps Nullable onto tuning-key columns: 9 tuned TPC-DS tables (STORE_SALES SS_SOLD_DATE_SK partition + SS_CUSTOMER_SK/SS_STORE_SK/SS_PROMO_SK sorting, STORE_RETURNS, CATALOG_SALES, CATALOG_RETURNS, WEB_SALES, WEB_RETURNS, DATE_DIM, ITEM, CUSTOMER per tpcds_tuned.yaml) get Nullable columns in MergeTree ORDER BY/PARTITION BY; allow_nullable_key appears nowhere in benchbox/ -> schema-creation crash replaces the load crash.
2. Greedy regex \([^;\n]*\) corrupts compact single-line DDL when a paren-typed nullable column is not last (b Nullable(DECIMAL(10,2), c VARCHAR(5))); its own test only covers last position.
3. Nullable(X) NOT NULL can be emitted if get_schema() nullability disagrees with rendered DDL (strip runs before wrap).
4. A nullable FLOAT[N] would become Nullable(Array(...)), which ClickHouse rejects (latent).

Same review, dialect side (P1, fully live on develop): resolve_csv_dialect's manifest branch is all-or-nothing (data_loading.py:189-197) -- partial metadata (vector_search writes only csv_has_header, generator.py:206) falls back to comma for .csv, discarding the benchmark's _csv_delimiter='|' (benchmark.py:94-95) -> embedding fields split on commas. 15+ platforms share the resolver. Correct fix is BOTH generator-side (self-describing manifest) and resolver-side (field-by-field fallback per the documented a->b->c precedence). 5f266e76f only fixes the resolver.

Also falsify/close during live verification: chdb/clickhouse-local file() path may silently coerce empty nullable fields to 0/epoch/'' via input_format_csv_empty_as_default (data_loading.py:2041-2059) -- corruption, not crash.

This item is the remaining implementation chunk of [[uat-clickhouse-server-loader-type-coverage]]; that umbrella's live TPC-DS closure is checkpoint w6/v4 here.

Tuned TPC-DS CREATE TABLE succeeds for all 24 tables (the 9 key-affected tables are the regression surface).

description:
After PR #738 fixed the clickhouse-server provisioning/auth/database/load
path, the 2026-06-01 corpus rerun no longer showed the original 57/57
platform wipeout. The largest remaining failure cluster is server-mode
client-side INSERT type conversion during load, not generic ClickHouse
compatibility.

PR #738 introduced this path because Docker-backed ClickHouse server cannot
read arbitrary host files through server-side `file()`. The path is
BenchBox-side and gated to server deployment mode; clickhouse-local keeps the
faster `file()` load path. The review of the corpus found no silent
corruption: empty strings into String columns are preserved as empty strings,
and every observed type gap fails loudly during load.

Corpus evidence:
  - Matrix: `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/matrix_summary.tsv`
  - Cells: `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/cells.jsonl`

Representative failures:
  - `clickhouse-server_tpcds_0.01_20260601_120433.log`: `Code: 53. Type mismatch in VALUES section... Column c_current_cdemo_sk: required argument is not an integer`; TPC-DS then reports many empty tables.
  - `clickhouse-server_clickbench_1.0_20260601_122208.log`: `ClickHouse file loading failed: 'str' object has no attribute 'tzinfo'`.
  - `clickhouse-server_vector_search_0.01_20260601_133631.log`: `ClickHouse file loading failed: could not convert string to float: '[0.0206561,...]'`.
  - `clickhouse-server_datavault_0.01_20260601_133545.log`: `ClickHouse file loading failed: argument of type 'Table' is not iterable`.

Observed impact from the corpus classifier: roughly 22 of the 42 non-passing
cells are loader type coverage. Bucket A is nullable numeric/date handling
for empty fields into non-Nullable ClickHouse columns (TPC-DS, NYC Taxi,
FlightData, plus downstream TPC-DS OBT). Bucket B is DATETIME/TIMESTAMP
conversion, currently falling through as strings and producing the `tzinfo`
error (ClickBench, H2O DB, TSBS). Bucket C is array/vector parsing for
Vector Search. Bucket D is Arrow/Table-valued schema introspection for
DataVault. These are not platform lifecycle failures: Docker up/down
succeeded and the corpus executed all 57 cells.
preserves: Do not make clickhouse-local depend on clickhouse-driver server-only conversion behavior.
Do not silently coerce invalid data to zero or empty strings; nullability and parse failures must stay visible.
Empty strings into String columns must remain empty strings; do not turn them into NULL.
Keep the PR #738 server-mode contract: Docker-host data files load through client-side batches, not server-side `file()` paths.
The 15 passing corpus cells must keep passing: TPCH, SSB, AMPLab, AI primitives, and TPCH skew at all three scales.

The 2026-06-01 clickhouse-server corpus rerun exposed cells where schema/load
finished and BenchBox produced result JSON with partial query failures, but
UAT still classified the terminal state as `no_json_nonzero` because the
process exited nonzero. These are not RC-1 platform wipeouts; they are query
dialect failures plus a UAT result-capture fidelity gap.

  - Matrix: `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/matrix_summary.tsv`

  - metadata_primitives: 150 passed, 3 failed; first error references unknown `admin_option` in `system.role_grants`.

The UAT harness should preserve the discovered result path even when the
child command exits with code 1 after recording query-level failures. That
makes future corpus triage direct instead of requiring manual stdout/log
inspection.

description:
RC-1 is the clickhouse-server UAT wipeout: the 2026-05-31 retry artifacts
show 57/57 clickhouse-server cells failed with `terminal_state=no_json_nonzero`
and empty `failure_tail`, so the original run did not expose the actionable
error.

Re-run on 2026-06-01 after the stderr-visible diagnostic fix confirmed the
real failure for the smallest cell:

  BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs \
    LOG_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/clickhouse-server-rc1-repro-20260601 \
    TIMEOUT_S=90 make uat-cell PLATFORM=clickhouse-server BENCHMARK=tpch SCALE=0.01

Result: failed in 33.96s, log
`~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/clickhouse-server-rc1-repro-20260601/clickhouse-server_tpch_0.01_20260601_103610.log`
captured `Code: 210. Connection refused (localhost:9000)`. `nc -vz
localhost 9000` and `localhost 8123` also returned connection refused.

The missing-extra hypothesis was checked and is not the observed failure in
this worktree: `clickhouse-driver` is installed and the diagnostic reached
the driver connection path. The UAT argv is still hardened separately so
clickhouse-server uses its canonical uv extra instead of relying on whatever
the current environment has installed.

Follow-up live repro on 2026-06-01 found three additional server-specific
blockers after Docker was healthy: the local compose stack required an
explicit host-accessible password, the adapter selected `database=default`
before creating it, and ClickHouse server mode attempted to load Docker-host
paths through server-side `file()`, which is limited to
`/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files`. After those fixes plus removal of
session-resetting unsupported `SET` statements, the smallest live cell passed:

  CLICKHOUSE_HOST_PORT=19000 CLICKHOUSE_HTTP_HOST_PORT=18123 \
    BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs \
    LOG_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/clickhouse-server-rc1-repro-20260601 \
    TIMEOUT_S=600 make uat-cell PLATFORM=clickhouse-server BENCHMARK=tpch SCALE=0.01

Result: passed in 10.24s with `submit_terminal_state=submittable`, log
`~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/clickhouse-server-rc1-repro-20260601/clickhouse-server_tpch_0.01_20260601_114205.log`,
and result
`~/Developer/benchmark_runs/results/tpch_sf001_clickhouse_server_sql_20260601_114215_e1a77de5.json`.

Post-fix corpus verification on 2026-06-01 ran the original 57-cell
clickhouse-server non-OLTP surface under UAT-managed Docker lifecycle:

  CLICKHOUSE_HOST_PORT=19000 CLICKHOUSE_HTTP_HOST_PORT=18123 \
    BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs \
    make uat-sweep CONFIG=/tmp/uat-clickhouse-server-rc1-corpus-20260601.yaml

  `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/matrix_summary.tsv`
  `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/cells.jsonl`

The corpus executed all 57 candidate cells with no compatibility or
early-stop pruning. Summary footer: `passed=15 failed=40 timed_out=2`,
`run_status=COMPLETED`, `source_dirty=false`. Docker lifecycle recorded

description:
DECISION (user, 2026-07-11): the supported engine is mocker (Apple
Containerization Docker-CLI shim) on macOS and docker elsewhere.

Current state, verified on develop @ fc31f3604:

1. HARDCODED BINARY: UAT's managed lifecycle, preflight probes, and
   recovery cleanup all hardcode the `docker` binary
   (tests/uat/docker_assets.py:361, phases/preflight.py:85/:100,
   docker_cleanup.py:181-184). BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI (honored by
   _project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py:879-883) is ignored by UAT;
   CONTAINER_ENGINE is honored only by the Makefile test-docker-*
   targets (Makefile:452-463). The engine used to produce historical
   gate evidence is recorded nowhere.

2. MOCKER VOLUME LEAK: mocker 0.5.4's `compose down -v` does not remove
   named volumes; the workaround exists only in the Makefile
   compose_down_fresh macro (Makefile:463), so UAT-managed teardown leaks
   named volumes on every platform switch under mocker.

3. APPLE-CONTAINER CLEANUP DEFECTS (make uat-docker-cleanup
   ENGINE=container):
   - PREFIX= silently ignored: reclaim_container_usage(project_prefix=..)
     never threads it; classifiers hardcode DEFAULT_UAT_PROJECT_PREFIX
     (container_cleanup.py:344, :379-380, :407). ENGINE=container
     PREFIX=custom APPLY=1 reports the custom prefix but deletes by the
     default one. No test covers the passthrough.
   - networks never inventoried in any mode (_inventory_resources lists
     only images/containers/volumes, container_cleanup.py:324-329).
   - ownership overreach: image-name prefix matching (`benchbox-`) can
     classify a non-UAT dev container as owned even in `owned` mode
     (container_cleanup.py:56, :244-248).

4. DOCKER-ENGINE GAP: images pulled (not built) by compose carry no
   compose label and are never reclaimed by any automated path --
   multi-GB platform images accumulate forever (docker_cleanup.py:294-321
   reports them as non-UAT; compose down --rmi local skips registry
   images, docker_assets.py:392-393).

End state: one engine-resolution function (env override
BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI > platform default: mocker-if-present on darwin,
docker otherwise; hard error if the resolved binary is missing) used by
docker_assets, preflight, uat_bring_up, and docker_cleanup; the resolved
engine name+version recorded in uat_lifecycle.log and the accounting
sidecar; mocker teardown gains the named-volume sweep; the three
Apple-container cleanup defects fixed.
preserves: Default behavior on a docker-only Linux host is byte-identical (docker resolved, no mocker probing beyond a which() check on darwin).
Forbidden-command guard (docker_assets.py:431-459 refuses global prunes) applies to every engine.
docker_cleanup label-scoped ownership for the Docker engine (never mutate non-UAT labeled resources).
make uat-docker-cleanup remains report-only without APPLY=1.

work.notes: mocker 0.5.4 confirmed installed (`mocker --version` -> 0.5.4). Scratch compose project (`benchbox-uat-w0test`, alpine + a named volume) via `mocker compose up -d` then `down -v`: containers were removed but the named volume (`benchbox-uat-w0test-scratchvol`) survived `down -v` and required a manual `mocker volume rm` -- confirms the leak evidence dates from 0.5.4 still hold on this install. `mocker network --help` and `container network --help` both exist and produce structured `--format json` output (`container network ls --format json` verified working; `mocker network ls` verified working, plain text). Also discovered (not previously documented) during w0/live-smoke re-runs: `mocker container ls`/`image ls --format json` echo the literal string "json" instead of producing JSON (fully broken, not just incomplete); `mocker volume inspect` takes exactly one name (not docker's variadic form) and returns a lowercase, non-Docker-shaped schema; `container volume ls` (the native Apple CLI) is EMPTY for mocker-managed named volumes -- mocker tracks its own volumes in a separate store invisible to the native `container` CLI. These findings drove w1/w3's docker_cleanup.py mocker-fallback design and the AGENTS.md/docs notes on ENGINE=docker vs ENGINE=container coverage. Scratch project fully torn down and cleaned after testing.

description:
The 2026-05-29 dataframe sweep
(uat_complete_native_remaining_non_oltp_20260528_20260529) exposed several
failures with IDENTICAL signatures across independent engines
(pandas-df, polars-df, pyspark-df, dask-df, and datafusion). Identical
failures across unrelated engines point to BenchBox defects in the shared
DataFrame loader/translation path, not to per-engine limitations. Evidence
(errors[] from the per-cell result JSONs):

1. datavault load_end_dts unresolvable on polars/pandas/pyspark (q66/66,
   all scales). polars: 'unable to find column "load_end_dts"; valid
   columns: ["92cec9d0fb7ef6a..."]'; pyspark suggests columns like
   [``, `0.02`, `1996-02-12`] -> the datavault loader is binding header
   rows / column names wrong.
2. pandas date-as-string typing: tpch q39/66, flightdata q60/60,
   read_primitives q90/456 all fail with
   "'<=' / '>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and
   'datetime.date'" -> date columns load as strings in the pandas path.
3. write_primitives bulk_load_append_mode: pandas/polars/pyspark all fail
   ~q195-204/399 with "Operation bulk_load_append_mode failed: IO Error:
   No files found that..." -> shared write_primitives file-discovery bug.
4. datafusion positional column names: nyctaxi/flightdata/tsbs_devops fail
   with "Schema error: No field named pickup_datetime. Valid fields are
   trips.f0" -> table registration drops real column names, exposing
   f0/f1/f2.
5. pandas tpcds every query fails (q309/309) with KeyError 'd_date_sk'.
6. UnifiedExpr clickbench: polars "cannot create expression literal for
   value of type UnifiedExpr"; pyspark "'UnifiedExpr' object has no
   attribute '_get_object_id'" -> literal/expression translation bug.

Note: polars|tpcdi correctly self-reports "TPC-DI DataFrame ETL requires
transactional maintenance capabilities" — that is a genuine limitation and
belongs in uat-native-dataframe-compatibility-rules, NOT here.
preserves: Engines that already pass these benchmarks (per the run: polars/pandas/pyspark passing cells) must not regress.
Genuine limitations (polars tpcdi transactional ETL) stay failures/prunes, not forced green.

description:
In the 2026-05-29 dataframe sweep, dask-df produced only 5 per-cell logs
(tpch 0.01/0.1/1.0, tpcds 0.01/0.1) before the run stopped — it was the
last platform by wall-clock and the sweep ended there with no resume.json
and no abort_reason. The dask tpcds 0.1 log ends with:
"distributed.scheduler - ERROR - Task ('_groupby_apply_funcs-...', 0)
marked as failed because 4 workers died while trying to run it".

Two problems: (a) tpcds on local Dask kills workers (likely memory
pressure during groupby/concat), and (b) a Dask cluster death did not
cleanly record FAIL and advance — it left the sweep truncated. A worker
death must terminate the cell as FAIL (with the captured scheduler error)
and the sweep must move on, never hang or silently stop.

NOTE: the plan draft cited "KeyError('ca_county')" for Dask; that is NOT
in the evidence. The verified Dask signature is the "4 workers died"
scheduler error on tpcds; "KeyError 'd_date_sk'" was the pandas-df tpcds
failure (tracked in uat-cross-engine-dataframe-defects). Use the verified
signatures.
preserves: Sequential platform execution and per-cell timeout semantics are unchanged.
dask-df cells that pass (tpch 0.01/0.1/1.0) must not regress.

description:
The #693 disk-headroom gate is trivially bypassable, verified on develop
@ fc31f3604:

1. PHASE-LIST KEYING: every mid-run free-space check is keyed on
   `"preflight" in config.phases` -- orchestrator.py:295
   (free_space_checks_enabled), :299 (watch_disk_floor), _cli.py:419.
   An execute-only config (a legitimate composition the schema allows)
   runs with ZERO disk gating. Omitting a phase named "preflight" should
   skip the preflight REPORT, not disable a safety interlock.

2. SILENT DEGRADE: `except Exception` at tests/uat/phases/preflight.py:217

   a warning; budget_gate stays None and the stronger budget-aware gate

   feeds with only a stderr line.

3. EXPLICIT-ZERO SEMANTICS: free_space_min_gib <= 0 disables all checks

Desired end state: the free-space floor and per-cell disk watch are
active for every execute-bearing run regardless of the phases list;
`free_space_min_gib: 0` remains the documented opt-out but logs a loud
one-line warning; an estimator failure is a hard preflight error (the
operator fixes the budget table or sets the flat floor explicitly),
not a silent downgrade.

approach:
Treat this as a UAT harness lifecycle problem, not an adapter problem. The
execute phase is the only layer that knows when the full set of cells for one
platform has finished and the next platform is about to start. That boundary
is late enough to preserve same-platform database reuse and early enough to
release Docker volumes before the next engine consumes storage.

Implement the change in two layers: a pure-ish Docker asset module that owns
compose mapping and command construction, then a narrow execute-phase hook
that calls the helper at platform start/end under a `try/finally`. Keep the
cleanup safe and targeted: UAT-owned compose project only, volumes removed
only for that project, no global Docker pruning. Prevent no-op configs by
rejecting non-`off` teardown unless UAT-managed startup is enabled. Audit
fixed `container_name` compose files before assuming compose project names
are sufficient isolation. Add explicit config validation and fast tests
before any live Docker smoke.

description:
Storage-constrained UAT sweeps can exhaust disk even after the existing
reuse-aware cleanup prunes `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/databases/`: Docker
containers, networks, and named volumes live outside the BenchBox output root
and are not cleared by the UAT framework today.

The right integration point is the platform boundary in
`tests/uat/phases/execute.py::run_execute`: after the final cell for one
platform completes, and before the next platform starts. That keeps
same-platform benchmark/database reuse intact while preventing Docker-backed
platforms from leaving volume state behind for the rest of a multi-platform
sweep.

Implement targeted, UAT-owned Docker cleanup only. Do not add blanket
`docker system prune`, do not delete unrelated developer stacks, and do not
move lifecycle management into adapters. The cleanup policy must be expressed
in real UAT config fields with readers/tests so it does not repeat the
existing orphan-YAML-field problem around `cleanup.*`.

The implementation must not be a safe-looking no-op. A non-`off` Docker
platform-switch cleanup policy is only valid when UAT owns the Docker stack
lifecycle for that platform (starts it with a UAT-owned compose project and
tears down that same project). If operators choose externally managed Docker
services, UAT should keep current skip/probe behavior and must report Docker
cleanup as disabled rather than pretending to clear assets it does not own.
preserves: Benchmark cell elapsed time remains the `benchbox run` subprocess duration; Docker startup/teardown is UAT overhead, not query timing.
Docker cleanup targets only UAT-owned compose projects by default; user-managed developer stacks are not stopped or pruned.
Existing TPC-H/TPC-DS source-consumer database reuse remains intact; Docker teardown happens at platform boundaries, not per cell.
Externally managed Docker stacks keep current probe/skip behavior unless a separate explicitly approved external cleanup mode is designed.
Generated datagen under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/datagen/` remains preserved unless a separate explicit cleanup policy is approved.
Non-Docker and DataFrame platform UAT behavior stays unchanged except for shared free-space guardrails.
Sequential platform execution remains mandatory; do not add parallel platform execution or async Docker lifecycle behavior.

work.notes:
Add a concrete config contract under `cleanup:` and document its defaults. The contract must distinguish four questions:
  1. Should UAT manage Docker stacks for Docker-backed platforms, or only probe externally managed stacks?
  2. What teardown depth is allowed at a platform switch for UAT-managed stacks?
  3. Which destructive operations are forbidden even when cleanup is enabled?
  4. How does the config avoid a no-op when teardown is requested but UAT does not own the stack?

Recommended shape:
  - `cleanup.docker_manage_platforms: false|true` deciding whether UAT may run `docker compose up -d --wait` before a Docker platform.
      - `false` preserves current externally managed behavior: TCP probes may skip unreachable platforms, and Docker cleanup must be reported as disabled.
      - `true` is the storage-saving UAT-owned lifecycle mode: start a UAT-owned project before the platform, then tear down that same project at the platform boundary.
  - `cleanup.docker_platform_switch: "off"|"containers"|"volumes"|"images"`:
      - `off`: no Docker teardown. Required when `docker_manage_platforms: false` unless a future explicit external-cleanup mode is added.
      - `containers`: `docker compose down --remove-orphans` for the UAT-owned project only.
      - `volumes`: `docker compose down -v --remove-orphans` for the UAT-owned project only. This is the recommended storage-saving setting for UAT-managed Docker sweeps.
      - `images`: `docker compose down -v --remove-orphans --rmi local` for the UAT-owned project only; never remove pulled/base images by default.
  - `cleanup.docker_project_prefix: "benchbox-uat"` to make ownership visible and avoid colliding with Makefile test stacks.
  - `cleanup.docker_start_timeout_s` for compose startup wait failures if UAT-managed startup is enabled.
  - `cleanup.docker_fixed_container_name_policy: "fail"|"override"|"allow"` if w1 finds fixed names that need a first-class decision.

Validation requirements:
  - Reject invalid enum values at config-load time.
  - Reject `docker_manage_platforms: false` combined with `docker_platform_switch` of `containers`, `volumes`, or `images`; otherwise the requested cleanup would silently do nothing.
  - Reject UAT-managed startup for a platform whose w1 decision says fixed `container_name` makes managed mode unsafe.
  - Ensure both `make uat-sweep` and `make uat-execute` read the same cleanup policy.
  - If `uat-framework-review-followups` has already landed typed UAT config dataclasses, extend those dataclasses. If it has not landed, still add real validation/readers/tests for these fields in the current config shape; do not add raw-only fields that are silently ignored.
work.summary: Define the Docker cleanup contract and config schema before adding behavior

work.notes:
Add a focused helper module, preferably `tests/uat/docker_assets.py`, rather than embedding subprocess command construction in `execute.py`.
The helper should expose small, testable pieces:
  - A `DockerPlatformSpec` dataclass with platform ID, compose file path(s), optional service names, fixed-container-name policy, managed-start eligibility, expected TCP probe label, and notes for special cases like Velox.
  - `is_docker_platform(platform: str) -> bool` backed by the mapping from w1.
  - `compose_project_name(config_name, platform, prefix) -> str` that sanitizes names and stays deterministic within a sweep.
  - `compose_up_command(spec, project_name) -> list[str]` for UAT-managed startup.
  - `compose_down_command(spec, project_name, cleanup_mode) -> list[str]` for `containers` / `volumes` / `images` modes.
  - `validate_managed_start_allowed(spec, config) -> None` so fixed `container_name` and external-only decisions fail early with clear text.
  - A subprocess runner that captures stdout/stderr, timeout, return code, and command string for logging.
Safety requirements:
  - Always include `docker compose -p <uat-owned-project> -f <compose-file> ...` for automated cleanup.
  - Never generate `docker system prune`, `docker volume prune`, `docker image prune`, or unqualified `docker compose down`.
  - Never call `down -v` against compose projects that UAT did not start or cannot identify as UAT-owned unless a future explicit user-approved external-cleanup mode is added.
  - Make dry-run return/log the commands without executing them.
  - Treat Docker unavailable as an environment/setup outcome, not as a Python traceback.
  - For fixed `container_name` platforms, either generate/use the approved override from w1 or refuse managed startup before any Docker command is run.
work.summary: Implement a Docker asset helper with safe, inspectable command generation

work.notes:
Integrate at `tests/uat/phases/execute.py::run_execute`, not in `runner.py` and not in any platform adapter.
Required control flow:
  - Group cells by `(platform, benchmark)` as today, preserving the topological reorder for source/consumer reuse.
  - Detect the start of each new platform.
  - If the platform is Docker-backed and `cleanup.docker_manage_platforms` is true, validate managed-start eligibility and start its compose stack before reachability probing.
  - If the platform is Docker-backed and `cleanup.docker_manage_platforms` is false, keep current externally managed skip/probe behavior and record Docker cleanup as disabled, not active.
  - Run all benchmarks/scales for that platform sequentially as today.
  - Continue running existing reuse-aware `benchmark_runs/databases` cleanup at safe mid-platform and platform-completion boundaries.
  - In a `finally` block around the whole platform block, call Docker teardown according to `cleanup.docker_platform_switch` before moving to the next platform, but only for a stack UAT actually started.
Teardown must run after passed, failed, timed-out, ladder-pruned, and skipped-unreachable outcomes for the platform when UAT-managed startup occurred.
Teardown must also run when the runner raises an exception or a `KeyboardInterrupt`/TERM path unwinds through Python.
Do not tear down per cell; that would destroy same-platform reuse and add timing noise.
Do not include Docker startup/teardown time inside `CellResult.elapsed_s` because benchmark cell timing should remain scoped to `benchbox run`.
If startup fails after creating partial assets, still attempt the configured teardown in `finally`.

work.notes:
Root cause was query 10_v8 ("EXISTS pattern"), NOT a slow run: its
EXISTS subquery used unqualified columns (l2.l_orderkey = l_orderkey)
that silently bound to the inner alias l2, degenerating the correlated
semi-join into an uncorrelated full scan that DuckDB's planner blew up
at SF1 (>180s, uninterruptible in-engine; EXPLAIN showed a
self-equality filter l_orderkey=l_orderkey). Fixed by qualifying the
correlation to the outer table (l2.l_orderkey = lineitem.l_orderkey),
which DuckDB decorrelates into a RIGHT_SEMI hash join.
Evidence (2026-05-29, DuckDB 1.3.2 / tpchavoc_sf1):
  - before: query 10_v8 hung >180s; tpchavoc@1.0 exit 124.
  - after:  10_v8 EXPLAIN shows SEMI join, executes in 0.1s; full
            tpchavoc@1.0 load,power = 880/880 executions, 100%, PASSED.
Timeout was NOT raised (anti-pattern: cell was hung, not slow).
