description:
Four inconsistencies in the abort/advance decision matrix, verified on
develop @ fc31f3604:

1. REPORT WITHOUT EXECUTE SILENTLY SUCCEEDS: validate and package abort
   when execute has not run (orchestrator.py:369-372, :408-411) but
   report proceeds with empty rows (`cells = ... if execute_outcome else
   []`, orchestrator.py:460) and exits 0 -- an empty report reads as a
   clean sweep.

2. EXPLORER SMOKE IS BOTH TOO LOUD AND TOO QUIET: empty/malformed corpus
   raises uncaught RuntimeError (phases/explorer_smoke.py:305, :343; no
   try in run_sweep's branch, orchestrator.py:447-457) -- a crash with no
   abort artifacts. Meanwhile a missing `node` binary returns
   skipped-with-exit-0 (explorer_smoke.py:160-169) -- a sweep on a
   machine without Node silently drops all browser coverage. Both ends
   need structured results: corpus problems become a structured phase
   failure (abort artifacts emitted); node-missing becomes a recorded
   skip that downstream accounting can see (explorer_smoke_status in the
   sidecar) instead of an invisible exit 0.

3. STARTUP-FAILED INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM UNREACHABLE: managed compose-up
   failure routes cells into skipped_unreachable (execute.py:176-186) --
   correct advance semantics (#700), but accounting cannot distinguish
   "stack failed to start" from "TCP probe found nothing listening"; the
   distinction survives only in uat_lifecycle.log. Add a separate
   startup_failed count to ExecuteOutcome and the accounting sidecar.

4. BROKEN STACK DEFEATS ITS OWN ADVANCE: after startup-failed,
   started=True is set unconditionally (execute.py:315-320) so the
   finally teardown runs; if `compose down` on that same broken stack
   also fails, teardown_abort_reason becomes a GLOBAL abort
   (execute.py:236-241) -- the advance-past-broken-stack intent
   (comment at execute.py:176-185) is defeated by the same broken
   stack's teardown. Policy fix: teardown failure aborts only for stacks
   that STARTED successfully (a healthy stack we cannot tear down is a
   real resource-leak emergency); teardown failure after startup-failed
   records a lifecycle event and advances.
preserves: #699 semantics: dask cluster death stays FAIL-and-advance.
#700 semantics: compose-up failure never aborts the whole sweep.
Healthy-stack teardown failure remains a global abort (resource-leak emergency).
Standalone make uat-report over an existing cells.jsonl keeps working without an execute phase in the same process.

(explorer_smoke_status=skipped_no_node)` line to stderr regardless of whether a sidecar existed to patch. `update_accounting_sidecar` returns False (no-op, no fabricated sidecar) when no sidecar exists yet -- documented in its docstring per the TODO's "else document" fallback for the case where explorer_smoke runs in a `phases:` list that never ran `execute`. work.notes: Added `ExecuteOutcome.startup_failed: tuple[Cell, ...]`; the docker_startup_failed branch in execute.py's `run_execute` now extends `startup_failed` instead of `skipped_unreachable` for a platform whose managed compose-up failed (the #700 path). `cells_io.write_cells_jsonl` gained `startup_failed_count` (additive sidecar field, alongside a new shared `_read_accounting_payload` helper and `read_startup_failed_sidecar`, mirroring `read_skipped_unreachable_sidecar`). `report.write_report` gained `startup_failed_count` (default 0): it feeds `total_defined_count = attempted + skipped + unreachable + startup_failed`, a `startup_failed=N` token in both the per-line and release_accounting footer comments, a `# STARTUP_FAILED_CELLS=N release_gate_attention=required` marker line (only emitted when nonzero, mirroring UNREACHABLE_CELLS), and `ReportSummary.exit_code()` now treats `startup_failed_count > 0` as uncleared (nonzero exit), same tier as fail/timeout/unreachable. orchestrator.py threads `startup_failed_count` through every write_cells_jsonl/write_report call site (execute-phase success, `_emit_abort_artifacts`, the DiskFloorAbort synthesized outcome via `exc.startup_failed_count` annotated by `_annotate_disk_floor_abort`, and the report phase). `_cli.py`'s `_handle_report`/`_handle_execute` also thread/print the new field. Updated the #700 regression tests (test_execute_docker_startup_failure_records_and_advances_to_next_platform, test_execute_outcome_exit_code_nonzero_when_every_compose_up_fails) to assert cells land in `startup_failed`, not `skipped_unreachable` -- the TODO's explicit intent, not a preservation violation. test_report_accounting.py's identity assertion updated to `attempted + skipped + unreachable + startup_failed == total_defined`. New tests cover write_report threading/exit-code, the CLI sidecar round-trip, and a bare exit-code-clean-when-zero case.

work.notes: `_teardown_docker_platform_if_needed` (execute.py) now captures `stack_started_successfully = docker_state.cleanup_status == "started"` before running `_run_docker_teardown` (the incoming cleanup_status is "startup-failed" for a stack whose own compose-up already failed -- set in `_start_docker_platform_if_needed`). On a teardown failure: if the stack started successfully, behavior is unchanged (global abort, `abort_kind="docker_teardown"`). If the stack never started, the teardown failure is recorded as an extra `DockerLifecycleEvent(action="down-policy", status="advance-after-startup-failed", message=...)` (the raw `down status=failed` event from `_run_docker_teardown` is still recorded too) and execution falls through to the existing free-space check + normal advance, instead of returning an abort reason/kind. The pre-existing test_execute_docker_teardown_failure_aborts_before_next_platform continues to pass unchanged.
work.summary: Teardown-failure policy: global abort only when the stack had started successfully; startup-failed stacks record the teardown failure as a lifecycle event and advance; tests for both directions

description:
Closes the simplification + de-duplication findings surfaced by the
principal-engineer review of PR #205 (UAT framework W2-W11) on
2026-05-05. The review delivered 16 simplification findings + 3
de-duplication candidates; this TODO addresses every one.

## Posture: forward-fix, no backward-compat surface

Per explicit user direction at TODO-creation time: this work does NOT
preserve old surfaces. We do not deprecate, we delete; we do not
thin-delegate, we cut over; we do not hedge schemas, we flatten. Each
work unit removes the prior surface in the same change that lands the
replacement. There is no "Tier 2" cleanup TODO behind this one.

Concrete consequences:
  - `scripts/local_stress_test.sh` is deleted (not thin-delegated).
  - `tests/uat/test_matrix.py::test_bash_parity_*` is deleted (no
    surface to be parity-tested against).
  - `tests/fixtures/published_results_validator.py` is deleted in
    favour of a proper `benchbox/validation/bundle.py` library.
  - `config.raw: dict[str, Any]` and `apply_stress_overrides` are
    deleted in favour of typed dataclasses + `dataclasses.replace`.
  - `cleanup.SOURCE_REUSE_GRAPH`, `KNOWN_SQL_ONLY_BENCHMARKS`,
    `enumerate` phase, `.frozen-hashes.json`, the `# FROZEN` ceremony,
    `apply_stress_overrides`, and confirmed-unused YAML fields all leave
    the tree.
  - The `benchbox/cli/` surface constraint gains a real test guard
    with an explicit exception for the internal submit-validator wiring
    moved by W4.

## Evidence base

Review output (in conversation transcript 2026-05-05). Sweep this
file alongside the four blind-spot captures:
  - `_project/blind-spots/2026-05-05-154305-uat-orphan-yaml-fields.md`
  - `_project/blind-spots/2026-05-05-154306-uat-noisy-neighbor-invocation-divergence.md`
  - `_project/blind-spots/2026-05-05-154307-uat-tpcds-obt-reuse-graph-asymmetry.md`
  - `_project/blind-spots/2026-05-05-154308-uat-cli-surface-constraint-no-enforcement.md`
And the two pre-existing UAT blind-spots that this TODO also resolves:
  - `_project/blind-spots/2026-05-05-080138-uat-bash-parity-structural-only.md`
    (resolved by deleting the bash + parity test in W3)
  - `_project/blind-spots/2026-05-05-080138-uat-frozen-config-replay-not-runnable.md`
    (resolved by W6's frozen-ceremony retirement)

Current-state note (2026-05-21): this TODO was created against PR #205
review evidence, but the branch has since gained Docker lifecycle cleanup
fields and additional UAT configs. W0 must revalidate every path/reader
claim against the implementation branch before code edits. Do not carry
forward deletion claims just because they were true on 2026-05-05.

## Decisions this TODO commits to (no further user gates required)

  1. **Bash retirement direction.** The framework owns matrix
     iteration. `scripts/local_stress_test.sh` is deleted. The
     2026-05-02 adoption criterion ("two-plus subsequent UATs") is
     superseded — adoption is now mandatory, not measured.
  2. **Frozen-config ceremony retirement.** The freeze + hash JSON +
     three-test guard buys nothing once the structural-parity replay
     (W4 of the parent TODO) is corrected to actually replay. Demote
     to a plain `# HISTORICAL` comment.
  3. **Validator library extraction.** `benchbox/validation/bundle.py`
     becomes the single source of truth. Both
     `scripts/validate_submission.py` and the published-results-branch
     copy become thin entrypoints (~30 lines).
  4. **Schema is fully typed.** No `raw: dict[str, Any]` passthrough,
     no W3/W4 staging artifact, no scattered defaults.

## What this TODO does NOT do

        def test_uat_did_not_modify_benchbox_cli_surface():
            base = os.environ.get("BENCHBOX_BASE_REF",
                                   "origin/develop")
            changed = subprocess.check_output(
                ["git", "diff", "--name-only", base, "--",
                 "benchbox/cli/"],
                cwd=REPO_ROOT, text=True
            ).splitlines()
            allowed_internal = {"benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py"}
            unexpected = set(changed) - allowed_internal

            diff = subprocess.check_output(
                ["git", "diff", "--unified=0", base, "--",
                 "benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py"],
                cwd=REPO_ROOT, text=True
            )
            changed_lines = [
                line for line in diff.splitlines()
                if line.startswith(("+", "-"))
                and not line.startswith(("+++", "---"))
            ]
            assert not any("@click.option" in line for line in changed_lines)
            assert not any("@click.command" in line for line in changed_lines)
            assert not any(
                line[1:].lstrip().startswith("def submit(")
                for line in changed_lines
            )

description:
Closes the **script/driver-drift** gap that
`_project/specs/uat-methodology-blind-spot-remediation.md` deliberately
scoped out. The methodology spec resolved three blind-spot findings
about *how UAT TODOs are authored and reviewed*; this TODO resolves
a different gap about *how UAT machinery is built and reused*.

## The gap

Today there are two parallel surfaces for matrix-shape execution:

  1. `scripts/local_stress_test.sh` -- 600-line bash. Single scale per
     benchmark, no cleanup, no validation, no scale-ladder. Purpose:
     verify "does it run?" across the (platform, benchmark) matrix.

  2. The 2026-05-02 UAT driver -- bespoke, hand-rolled, lives only as
     `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_20260502/` artifacts plus
     the retrospective. Re-invented timeout-wrapper (the script
     already had one), scale-ladder, reuse-aware cleanup, matrix
     summary TSV, submission packaging, validator subset filtering,
     explorer build, Playwright smoke. Not reusable; the next sweep
     will reinvent again.

Recorded:
`_project/blind-spots/2026-05-03-130000-stress-script-uat-driver-drift.md`.

## What this TODO does

Builds a single Python framework under `tests/uat/` (tracked, not in
`_project/`), exposed via `make uat-*` operator targets (no
`benchbox` user-CLI surface change). Composable phases driven by
YAML configs under `tests/uat/configs/`:

  - preflight (disk, docker, noisy-neighbor scan)
  - enumerate (registry-driven matrix with min/max scale enforcement)
  - execute (scale-ladder + early-stop + reuse-aware cleanup)
  - validate (calls `scripts/uat_validator_rollup.py` from
    `uat-template-validator-clean-rate-runner`)
  - package (uses `submit_terminal_state` vocab from
    `uat-template-success-metric-terminal-state-and-gating`)
  - explorer-smoke (build + Playwright; optional)
  - report (TSV roll-up + cross-scale coverage assertion)

Stress testing is the degenerate config (one scale, one platform
group, no validate/package/explorer phases).

## Adversarial framing -- strongest case for not doing this

Per the methodology-spec author's recommendation: "convention plus a
small wrap-script is sufficient; framework adds engineering cost
without proportional benefit." Counter: the stress script IS the
framework that already exists; it just lacks half the phases. Either
we evolve it (this TODO) or accept that the next UAT reinvents the
same machinery a third time. The bash script's readability argument
weakened post-2026-05-02 because the sweep author had to read the
script for knowledge anyway, and still re-invented its timeout
wrapper.

Per blind-spot finding `2026-05-03-084354-stress-test-self-bias`:
this section may itself be proposer-biased. Independent review at
W1 (spec) is the mitigation; the spec is the explicit user-approval
gate before any code lands.

## What this TODO does NOT do

  - Methodology / TODO-template work -- owned by the two
    `uat-template-*` deps. This TODO consumes their outputs.
  - Cloud-platform UAT -- deferred (separate TODO if needed).
  - Throughput-phase coverage -- deferred (separate sweep).
  - Removing `scripts/local_stress_test.sh` -- W11 documents the
    migration path but does not delete; deprecation is a separate
    decision after adoption proves out.
  - `benchbox uat` CLI subcommand -- explicitly out of scope; UAT
    is a project-developer concern, `benchbox` is a project-user
    concern.
preserves: Sequential platform execution discipline -- because UAT W3 line 222 explicitly forbids parallel platforms (timing contamination); code comments must reference this
_project/TODO_SCHEMA.yaml and _project/TODO_ENTRY_TEMPLATE.yaml unchanged -- because schema/template work is owned by uat-template-success-metric-terminal-state-and-gating
benchbox user-facing CLI surface unchanged -- because UAT is dev tooling, not user surface; no benchbox uat subcommand, no new top-level commands
results-data/ and origin/published-results corpus untouched -- because the framework dispatches submission, it does not curate corpus content

scripts/local_stress_test.sh continues to work as today's stress entrypoint until W11 explicitly migrates it -- because muscle memory is widespread and breaking this surface mid-framework-build invalidates the no-disruption promise
scripts/uat_validator_rollup.py public CLI unchanged once it lands -- because that helper is owned by uat-template-validator-clean-rate-runner; the framework is a consumer
scripts/validate_submission.py contract and exit codes unchanged -- because the validator is the source of truth; the framework wraps via uat_validator_rollup.py only

cells on read-only engines (datafusion, clickhouse-local) were ATTEMPTED
and FAILED rather than compatibility-pruned, inflating the failure count
with cells that policy should never have run. Examples from resume.json:
datafusion|write_primitives|*, datafusion|transaction_primitives|*,
datafusion|vector_search|*, clickhouse-local|write_primitives|*,
clickhouse-local|transaction_primitives|* — all "failed". The dataframe
sweep had the same shape (e.g. transaction_primitives NO_JSON across
pandas/polars/pyspark; polars tpcdi correctly self-reported "requires
transactional maintenance capabilities").

Correctness note from code reading: the pruning *machinery* already works
for every mode — tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py emits compatibility_pruned
rows from rules in tests/uat/compatibility.py. The reason native/dataframe
runs produced no native/dataframe prunes is that compatibility.py only
carries rules for docker platforms (pg-duckdb, pg-mooncake, timescaledb,
lakesail, questdb) plus one generic dataframe rule. The gap is MISSING
RULES, not missing emission. Do not rebuild emission.

one generic dataframe rule" is confirmed against commit da6a33c14
(`grep -oE 'uat\.compat\.[a-z0-9-]+' tests/uat/compatibility.py | sort -u`).

PRUNED (status compatibility-pruned, with rule_id + reason + evidence),
not counted as FAIL.

CRITICAL distinction (this is the adversarial trap): prune only what is
genuinely unsupported by the engine's model (e.g. row-level DML /
transactions on a read-only OLAP engine). DO NOT prune cells that failed
because of a BenchBox defect — those belong in the defect TODOs
(uat-cross-engine-dataframe-defects, uat-duckdb-reference-triage), where
they get fixed, not hidden. A prune rule must cite engine-model evidence,
not "it errored last run".

description:
Bus-factor findings from the review (develop @ fc31f3604): a competent
second operator on a fresh machine cannot run the release-gate sweep
from the docs alone. Ordered by how badly each strands them:

1. VENV PROVISIONING GAP: cells run `uv run --no-sync`
   (matrix.py:353-363); PLATFORM_UV_EXTRA covers only clickhouse-local,
   clickhouse-server, lakesail, singlestore, influxdb (matrix.py:36-43).
   The default dev dependency-group ([dependency-groups] dev,
   pyproject.toml:425+) covers most drivers but NOT modin[ray] and NOT
   databend-driver -- both appear only under
   [project.optional-dependencies] extras (modin at :149 in the all-style
   extra and :241 in the modin extra; databend-driver at :207-209), which
   a plain `uv sync` does not install -- and modin-df is in
   release-gate stage 1, databend in stage 3. A second operator gets
   ModuleNotFoundError cells recorded as FAILED, breaching the 1.0
   clean-rate floor with no doc pointing at the cause. Fix in code:
   extend PLATFORM_UV_EXTRA for modin and databend (the mechanism
   exists); document the provisioning contract (which extras each
   release-gate stage needs) in uat-local-provisioning.md.

2. OUTPUT-ROOT CONTRACT CONTRADICTION: uat-framework.md:391-392 and
   AGENTS.md:121 say to set BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR for sweeps, but sweeps
   read the root ONLY from YAML output.* templates (execute.py:766-771,
   config.py:53-56 defaults); the env var affects only bare uat-cell
   defaults (runner.py:326-342) and uat_bring_up. Fix in code (preferred
   over doc-only): when the YAML uses the DEFAULT templates, honor
   BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR as the base root; explicit YAML templates always
   win. Then the docs become true.

3. PHANTOM BENCHBOX_SEED: uat-framework.md:393 tells operators to record
   BENCHBOX_SEED; nothing reads it (grep verified: only the doc and a
   YAML comment). Remove from docs, or wire it through if seeds are
   meant to be controllable -- removing is correct: execute.official/
   seed is the real mechanism (config.py:47-49).

4. UNDOCUMENTED PHYSICAL PREREQS: Docker VM memory (velox's 11.7 GB
   ceiling lives in a code comment, matrix.py:29-34), doris
   vm.max_map_count (documented only outside UAT docs), first-run
   multi-GB image pulls/builds silently eating docker_start_timeout_s
   300 (LakeSail admits it in release-gate-02:55 comment), node +
   Playwright browser install for explorer smoke. Add a "fresh machine
   checklist" section to uat-local-provisioning.md; add a pre-pull/
   pre-build helper (make uat-prepull PLATFORM=... wrapping compose pull
   --ignore-buildable + compose build) so first-run timeouts stop
   presenting as skipped-unreachable mysteries.

5. ENGINE REQUIREMENT: after uat-container-engine-routing, document the
   resolved-engine contract (mocker on macOS, docker elsewhere,
   BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI override) in uat-local-provisioning.md.

description: Two Windows nightly failures are a genuine lifecycle-accounting bug, NOT the path-separator family they currently sit inside: tests/uat/test_orchestrator.py::test_disk_floor_abort_carries_startup_failed_count and ::test_disk_floor_abort_threads_startup_failed_count_into_sidecar_and_partial_report both fail 'assert 0 == 1' - the disk-floor abort path reports startup_failed_count as 0 when one platform already failed to start, so the count is dropped on the way into the sidecar and the partial report. description:
The native SQL sweep (uat_complete_native_20260528_20260528) aborted
mid-execute when /tmp fell below the 4.0 GiB floor:
resume.json abort_reason = "free space 3.6 GiB < cutoff 4.0 GiB at /tmp".
uat_lifecycle.log shows free space drifting down (18.63 -> 11.01 -> 7.36
-> 4.86 GiB) across platforms with docker_cleanup_status=not-run until the
floor tripped. The existing preflight.free_space_min_gib cutoff is a single
static floor; it does not relate available headroom to the workload the
config actually demands, and it watches a limited set of paths.

Make preflight (a) report free space at every relevant root and (b) gate
the sweep against the largest configured scale's expected peak from the
disk-budget table, so a sweep does not start only to abort halfway.

free_space_min_gib remains a valid explicit override; the new gate must be overridable for operators who know the run fits.

description:
DECISION (user, 2026-07-11): UAT becomes a REAL gate. Today it is
advisory by documented design -- docs/operations/release-guide.md:71-73
says "long-running UAT remain[s] advisory"; release-finalize gates on
exactly RELEASE_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS := validate-base release-required-result
(Makefile:1054) and scripts/release_readiness_check.py reads only
release-canary evidence. No workflow, script, or target consumes any UAT
artifact; the APPROVE/HOLD checklist (docs/operations/uat-framework.md
:418-434) is manual and unreferenced from the release runbook. Verified
on develop @ fc31f3604.

MECHANISM (mirrors the proven release-canary pattern -- readiness check
queries canary summary artifact, fails on missing/red/stale/non-ancestor,
release-guide.md:47-57):

1. GATE SUMMARY ARTIFACT: at sweep completion the orchestrator writes
   uat_gate_summary.json (versioned schema): config name,
   source_commit_sha + source_dirty (already computed for the TSV,
   report.py SourceInfo), container engine (from
   uat-container-engine-routing), completed_at, per-phase exit codes,
   accounting counts (attempted/passed/failed/timeout/unreachable/
   startup_failed/skipped incl. pruned split), validator clean rate vs
   floor, cross-scale pairs vs floor, explorer_smoke_status,
   unreachable_is_estimated, and a single derived verdict green|red.

2. AGGREGATION + ORDERING: `make uat-gate-check` reads the three
   release-gate stage summaries, enforces the cross-stage Docker
   ordering invariant machine-readably (stage completed_at fields
   replace the manual copy-paste snippet at uat-framework.md:404-413 /
   report.py:release_gate_ordering_violations), enforces the
   mechanizable APPROVE checklist items (all stages green, sidecar not
   estimated, explorer smoke actually ran for stages that include it),
   and writes a combined release-evidence file to a TRACKED path
   (_project/release-evidence/uat-gate-summary.json) that the operator
   commits.

3. RELEASE WIRING: extend scripts/release_readiness_check.py to require
   the combined summary: verdict green, source_dirty false,
   source_commit_sha an ancestor of the release PR head, age <= 21 days
   (judgement call: releases are cut every few weeks and a full 3-stage
   sweep costs an operator-day; the canary's 48h window would force
   redundant sweeps -- document the rationale). Missing/red/stale/
   non-ancestor fails validate-base on the release PR. Reuse the
   existing RELEASE_READINESS_OVERRIDE_SHA/_REASON admin escape hatch
   (release-guide.md:75-79) so incidents have the same documented
   override as the canary.

4. TUNED FLOORS (user delegated the judgement): replace the placeholder
   cross_scale_coverage_min_pairs: 1 in all three release-gate configs
   (release-gate-01:60, -02:62, -03:53 -- "Tune to the approved pair
   count during bring-up" was never done). Derivation rule: at
   implementation time, compute eligible (platform, benchmark) pairs per
   stage via enumerate_cells_with_pruning (registry + compatibility
   truth), set floor = floor(0.8 * eligible_pairs) with absolute minimum
   8 / 4 / 2 for stages 1 / 2 / 3, and write the derivation (eligible
   count, formula, date) as a comment above the value in each config.
   0.8 absorbs legitimate environment variance (a down docker stack)
   while making mass-regression impossible to sign off.

5. DOCS: release-guide.md drops the "advisory" language for UAT,
   documents the required evidence flow (sweep x3 -> uat-gate-check ->
   commit evidence -> open release PR), and the release runbook gains
   the checklist step that was always missing.

description:
DECISION (user, 2026-07-11): delete the resume machinery and lean on
datagen-reuse making restarts cheap, rather than hardening it.

Why deletion is the right call -- the resume path was verified fragile in
four independent ways on develop @ fc31f3604:
(a) load_resume_attempts (tests/uat/orchestrator.py:70-81) checks neither
    manifest version nor config_name nor commit -- resuming with a
    different config or on different code silently replays stale records;
(b) replayed passed cells never verify result_path still exists;
(c) the manifest is written only for free-space aborts (orchestrator.py
    :263-272, :310-317, :346-354, all gated on the prose string
    `"free space" in abort_reason`) -- docker/validate/package aborts were
    never resumable anyway;
(d) `--resume` is unreachable from the documented make surface (no
    RESUME= passthrough at Makefile:2206/:2224).

Deletion scope: _write_resume_manifest, load_resume_attempts,
build_resume_runner, RESUME_MANIFEST_VERSION (orchestrator.py),
`--resume` flags on the sweep and execute subparsers (_cli.py:504, :566)
and their handler branches (_cli.py:78-79, :409-413), resume-manifest
sections in _project/specs/uat-framework.md (Section 3 "Resume manifest",
Section 9.4) and docs/operations/uat-framework.md, and the resume-runner
tests in test_orchestrator.py / test_runner.py.

KEPT AND HARDENED -- the abort-safe provenance artifacts (#691) stay; the
restart story becomes "rerun the config; datagen reuse + ladder pruning
make it cheap". Two durability defects in those artifacts get fixed here
because resume's deletion makes the artifacts the ONLY record:

1. SAME-DAY EVIDENCE DESTRUCTION: default log dirs are date-granular
   (`uat_{date}`, config.py:55, execute.py:758-763) and every durable
   artifact is opened mode "w" (cells.jsonl orchestrator.py:579, sidecar
   :576-578, compatibility_pruned.jsonl :609-625, matrix_summary TSV).
   A second same-day run of the same config silently overwrites the first
   run's evidence.

2. NO ATOMIC WRITES ANYWHERE: every artifact is written in place. A crash
   mid-write leaves torn JSON/TSV; the sidecar is written before
   cells.jsonl so a crash between the two leaves a fresh sidecar beside a
   stale cell stream, and `make uat-report` will combine them.
preserves: Abort paths still emit cells.jsonl + sidecar + compatibility_pruned.jsonl + partial TSV (the #691 abort-safe provenance contract).
Existing logs_dir_template values in checked-in configs keep working verbatim (only the DEFAULT template changes).
cells.jsonl + sidecar schema stays readable by _cli.py report (only write mechanics change, not content).
generated-rerun-shards/ configs remain untouched -- they are frozen evidence of past sweeps, not consumers of the deleted machinery.

description:
Outcome of a 4-round adversarial architecture review of the UAT layer
(tests/uat/). The review converged on a "boundary reset": UAT's chartered
scope IS evidence-producing release-gate orchestration over named artifacts
(_project/specs/uat-framework.md:31,35-38,268,688,693), but it should
consume canonical BenchBox surfaces rather than fork policy.

This item fixes the highest-risk fork: UAT re-implements the submit
*classification policy*.

- tests/uat/runner.py:60 (classify_for_submit) re-expresses the decision
  tree that maps result predicates -> terminal state (and which terminal
  states are refusals) that benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py:587-606 already
  owns. The two surfaces will drift: when submit policy changes, UAT silently
  reports a different submittability verdict than `benchbox submit` enforces.
- tests/uat/runner.py:27 locally redefines
  frozenset({"unofficial_nonstandard","unofficial_subscale"}) instead of
  importing CLI_REFUSED_COMPLIANCE_CLASSES from
  benchbox/validation/bundle.py:46 (verified identical literals). Add a third
  refused class upstream and UAT silently diverges.

NOTE (precision from the review): the leaf predicates are NOT duplicated.
runner.py:22-23 already correctly imports result_non_clean_reason and
result_failed_query_count from benchbox.core.results.status. Only the
classification *policy* + the copy-pasted frozenset are duplicated. Do not
"fix" the predicate imports.

Establishes the principle every other UAT finding is an instance of:
consume canonical surfaces, do not fork policy.

description:
Outcome of a 4-round adversarial architecture review of the UAT layer
(tests/uat/). UAT maintains its own connection-truth table that duplicates
facts already owned by compose files and platform adapters, and the copies
can disagree silently.

- tests/uat/matrix.py:19-95 hardcodes PLATFORM_PORTS, PLATFORM_EXTRA_OPTS,
  LOCAL_MANAGED_PLATFORM_EXTRA_OPTS, and credentials (e.g. password=benchbox).
- SingleStore alone shows why the model must distinguish endpoint roles:
    * UAT hardcodes local Docker host reachability at 13306 (matrix.py:22)
    * compose maps ${SINGLESTORE_HOST_PORT:-13306} on the host to container port 3306
    * adapter credentials default to the service/container port 3306 (benchbox/platforms/credentials/singlestore.py:30)
- tests/uat/docker_assets.py:75 is yet another separate registry from matrix.py.

Failure mode: set SINGLESTORE_HOST_PORT (or change a compose mapping) and UAT
silently probes the wrong host port even though the adapter's service-port
default remains valid. A skipped-because-wrong-host-port platform looks
identical to a genuinely-down platform, so divergence quietly erodes the exact
coverage UAT exists to prove. This is the load-bearing fact a "lightweight
user-exercising" layer actually needs, and the one most certain to rot.
preserves: Externally-managed-platform path (docker_manage_platforms: false) still resolves connection facts correctly
UAT continues to reach every platform it currently reaches (no new skips after the refactor)

description:
UAT records skipped and unreachable cells, but the release report's candidate
counts do not fully represent them - so a release can look more complete than it
is. When skipped/unreachable cells silently shrink the denominator, a "passed N
of N" summary reads as full coverage when some cells never actually ran. That is
a release-evidence integrity problem, not a cosmetic one: the report is the
artifact a release decision is made against.

Audit the UAT report/validate accounting so skipped and unreachable cells appear
as explicit, reconciling denominators (e.g. passed / attempted / total-defined,
with skipped and unreachable broken out), and a non-zero unreachable count is
surfaced loudly in the summary rather than quietly absorbed.
preserves: Existing UAT report consumers (TSV columns) keep working; add columns/lines rather than renaming existing ones unless necessary.
Pass/fail classification of cells is unchanged; only the denominator representation and visibility change.

description:
Four verified correctness defects in the UAT cell status taxonomy and exit
codes, plus one portability crash. All verified on develop @ fc31f3604
(2026-07-10); base 0db7299f3 has no tests/uat changes since.

1. TIMED-OUT OVERWRITTEN BY FAILED (tests/uat/runner.py:270-277): the
   official/throughput validation block sets `status = "failed"`
   unconditionally after `_classify()`, with no `if status == "passed"`
   guard (contrast the correctly-guarded submit downgrade at
   runner.py:258). A timed-out official cell that exported no result JSON
   ends with status="failed", exit_code=124 -- report counts it in
   fail_count not timeout_count (phases/report.py:212-213), cells.jsonl
   records `timed_out: false` (orchestrator.py:592), while
   terminal_state() still derives "timeout" from exit 124
   (phases/report.py:120). One cell, three artifacts, three verdicts.

2. ALL-UNREACHABLE EXECUTE EXITS 0 (tests/uat/phases/execute.py:64-67):
   `ExecuteOutcome.exit_code()` is `all(r.status == "passed" for r in
   self.results)` -- `all([])` is True. Every platform down (or every
   managed compose-up failing, which routes cells into skipped_unreachable
   by design, execute.py:176-186) means zero cells run and
   `make uat-execute` exits 0. Only configs that include the report phase
   catch it (ReportSummary.exit_code checks unreachable_count).

3. FAILED CELLS LABELED submittable (tests/uat/phases/report.py:128-129):
   terminal_state() falls through to `cell.submit_terminal_state` (default
   "submittable") for any failed cell with a resolved result_path.
   Operators triaging by terminal_state misread failures as
   submission-ready. Relatedly the package phase submits result JSONs from
   failed cells: orchestrator.py:422 filters only on result_path presence,
   and official cells resolve result paths regardless of exit code
   (runner.py:246-251 comment says so explicitly).

4. throughput_check NEVER PERSISTED: CellResult.throughput_check
   (runner.py:59-63) -- the one diagnostic the #1094 stream-count guard
   exists to surface -- is not serialized by _write_cells_jsonl
   (orchestrator.py:583-603), is not a REPORT_HEADER column
   (phases/report.py:53-58), and is produced after the cell log closes so
   the failure tail cannot contain it. A stream-count failure leaves
   durable artifacts saying only failed/exit 1.

5. WINDOWS TIMEOUT CRASH (tests/uat/timeouts.py:104): `os.killpg` does not
   exist on win32; spawn handles the platform (`preexec = os.setsid if
   sys.platform != "win32" else None`) but the kill path calls
   `os.killpg` unconditionally and AttributeError is not in the
   `(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError)` catch -- a per-cell timeout
   crashes the whole execute phase instead of classifying the cell
   timed-out. The covering test is skipif-win32 so nothing catches it.
preserves: Exit-code contract: 0 success, 1 cell failures, 2 aborted, 124 timeout at the cell level.
REPORT_HEADER column order changes only by appending; existing columns keep their positions (external TSV consumers parse positionally, spec Section 6).
The submit-classification downgrade semantics at runner.py:256-260 (passed -> failed on refusal) stay exactly as-is.
cells.jsonl remains line-delimited JSON readable by the existing _cli.py report path; new fields are additive.

description:
2026-07-21 adversarial UAT review finding (P2): cells.jsonl and the accounting sidecar are written only after the whole execute phase returns (tests/uat/orchestrator.py:272-280) and uat_gate_summary.json only at the very end (:504-518); only DiskFloorAbort is artifact-safe mid-sweep (:229-271). An uncaught exception or SIGKILL mid-execute loses every completed cell's durable record (raw logs survive but are unreportable via make uat-report). SIGTERM is worse: no signal handler exists anywhere in tests/uat (timeouts.py only manages the CELL subprocess group), so Python's default SIGTERM action skips the finally teardown at tests/uat/phases/execute.py:300-313 entirely - a plain `kill <pid>` leaves the Docker stack up AND loses the records, while Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt) tears down correctly. docker_cleanup.py:3-8 names hard-kill recovery as make uat-docker-cleanup's job, so the stack half is acknowledged-by-design - but kill-vs-Ctrl-C asymmetry is a footgun during multi-hour release-gate sweeps, and the durability half has no mitigation at all.

Work: append each cell's row incrementally (or flush per platform) with an explicit finalize marker so a partial file can never read as a complete sweep; SIGTERM->raise shim in the sweep process so kill == Ctrl-C; record sweep-level cancellation as a lifecycle event (today it is only inferable from a missing gate summary). Interacts with uat-evidence-provenance-binding: the finalize marker is also what the digest/gate side should require - coordinate row/marker shape, and land this SECOND if both are in flight.
preserves: DiskFloorAbort behavior and exit codes unchanged; sweep exit codes unchanged.
cells.jsonl ROW schema unchanged (report/gate consumers parse it); the finalize marker is a separate artifact or trailing sentinel, decided with the provenance item.
timeouts.py cell-subprocess process-group kill semantics untouched.

description:
Promoted from the deferred item in
[[nightly-throughput-gate-restoration]] (surfaced by the UAT-effort
assessment, 2026-07-16). Restoring the nightly throughput gate detects
breakage (a cell fails / stream count wrong) but NOT gradual slowdown: there
is no Throughput@Size floor per platform/scale that a green run must clear.
Without it, a platform can regress in performance run-over-run without the
gate noticing.

This item defines that floor policy. It is deliberately gated on the gate
itself being restored AND on baseline data existing, because the parent's
deferral reason is explicit: "Needs baseline data from several green nightly
runs before a floor is defensible; premature thresholds create flake." A
threshold set before there is a stable baseline manufactures false failures.
preserves: The existing stream-count hard gate stays independent — a throughput-floor failure must not mask or replace a stream-count failure.

work.notes:
Decision unit. Prefer a relative floor (e.g. fail if Throughput@Size drops
more than X% below a rolling median of the last N green runs) over a
hardcoded absolute number, so the floor tracks hardware/runner drift.
X and N are set from the w0 spread, not guessed. Needs sign-off — a
too-tight floor flakes the gate; a too-loose floor is decorative.
work.summary: Choose the threshold model (relative % floor vs absolute floor vs rolling baseline)

description:
The official/throughput cell path resolves its result JSON by
filename-glob + mtime instead of the stdout contract every other cell
uses (because `run-official` has no --quiet; documented at
tests/uat/throughput.py:13-16). The resolver has two real weaknesses,
verified on develop @ fc31f3604:

1. SUBSTRING PLATFORM MATCH (tests/uat/throughput.py:60-66): the glob
   `f"{benchmark_token}_*{platform_token}*.json"` with platform="duckdb"
   matches `tpch_sf1_pg_duckdb_sql_20260709.json`. The existing

   entirely unfiltered.

2. ARBITRARY TIE-BREAK + WIDE CI WINDOW: max-mtime tie-break
   (throughput.py:70) is arbitrary within filesystem mtime granularity.
   Mitigated in production by sequential execution and per-cell

description:
Implement a unified `run_benchmark()` interface across SQL and DataFrame adapters,
eliminating the design defect identified in code review where DataFrame adapters
lack the same interface as SQL adapters.

The current architecture violates the Adapter pattern:

| Aspect | SQL Adapters | DataFrame Adapters |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| Has `run_benchmark()` | YES | NO |
| Entry point | `adapter.run_benchmark()` | `run_dataframe_benchmark()` function |
| Caller branching | None (polymorphic) | Required (orchestrator:287, MCP:175) |

**Design Violations:**
- Liskov Substitution Principle (adapters not interchangeable)
- Open/Closed Principle (new modes require caller changes)
- Adapter Pattern (no unified interface)

**Goal:** All adapters (SQL and DataFrame) should implement the same `run_benchmark()`
method, allowing callers to use adapters polymorphically without type-checking or
branching logic.
title: Unify SQL and DataFrame Adapter Execution Interfaces

description:
Architecture review (Work Area E, structural remediation) found that
`benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py:19-23`'s module docstring
self-admits a fragile design: DataFusion support "includes experimental
AST parsing for handling aggregate arithmetic expressions... tested with
DataFusion 43.0.0 and may not work with other versions if the error
message format changes."

The actual mechanism, `_get_datafusion_ast_string()`
(unified_frame.py:2313 onward), deliberately calls
`expr.rex_call_operator()` expecting it to THROW, then parses the AST
representation back out of the exception's string text (comment at
line ~2334: "the error message contains the AST like: 'Catch all
triggered in get_operator_name: Alias(BinaryExpr...)'"). It does a basic
sanity check (`"Alias" in error_str or "BinaryExpr" in error_str or
"AggregateFunction" in error_str`) before trusting the parsed text, and
falls back to passing expressions through unchanged if extraction fails
(per the module docstring) - which can then surface as a downstream
DataFusion error for unsupported aggregate-arithmetic patterns rather than
a clear, attributable failure at the point where the format assumption
broke.

This is a genuine upstream-coupling risk: a DataFusion release that
changes `rex_call_operator()`'s error text format would silently degrade
aggregate-arithmetic support without a clear signal pointing at this file.
preserves: Aggregate-arithmetic expressions that currently work correctly against the pinned DataFusion version continue to produce identical results after the hardening change.

The fallback-to-unchanged-expression behavior for genuinely unsupported patterns (not a format-parsing failure) is preserved for cases where DataFusion itself does not support the pattern - only the format-mismatch case should now raise loudly, not every extraction miss.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py:_get_datafusion_ast_string (2313) and its existing basic sanity check ('Alias'/'BinaryExpr'/'AggregateFunction' in error_str) - reuse and tighten this existing check into a hard assertion rather than adding a parallel validation path.

datafusion-tbl-trailing-delimiter-load.yaml - a prior TODO in this same platform area that replaced ad hoc/fragile per-caller logic with a shared, version-aware helper; follow its pattern of pinning behavior to a documented, tested version and adding a regression test for the failure mode.

description:

- SQL: `./benchmark_runs/datagen/{benchmark}_{sf}` (project-local, CWD-relative)
- DataFrame: `~/.benchbox/dataframe-data/{benchmark}/sf_{N}/{format}/` (user home, global)

format conversions cache globally. Both should default to project-local under

    DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path.home() / ".benchbox" / "dataframe-data"

    DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path.cwd() / "benchmark_runs" / "dataframe-data"

Resolve the architectural code smell of having two parallel platform registration systems
that can drift apart. Currently, new platforms must be registered in BOTH:

1. `get_platform_adapter()` in `benchbox/platforms/__init__.py` (hardcoded dict, 22 entries)
2. `PlatformRegistry.auto_register_platforms()` in `benchbox/core/platform_registry.py` (18 entries)

The systems serve different purposes:
- `get_platform_adapter()`: CLI routing + adapter instantiation (with alias support)
- `PlatformRegistry`: Metadata + discovery + availability (no alias support)

This has caused bugs where platforms were added to one system but not the other.
title: Unify Platform Registration Systems

description:
OBSOLETED on 2026-04-26: superseded by the single-repo migration plan
(_project/TODO/main/planning/single-repo-migration-phase-*.yaml). The
is_public_path predicate exists to maintain a curated public mirror of
a private repo; the migration deletes the curation apparatus entirely.
Phase 6 of that migration explicitly removes this work item's target
code (workflow.py).

Original description below preserved for historical context.

---

Today, "what goes into the public repo" is decided in two structurally different
code paths:

1. `benchbox/release/workflow.py::get_syncable_files` (filesystem walk +
   `_should_exclude_file`) - used by `compare_repos`, which `benchbox-sync`
   calls for status/push/pull operations.
2. `benchbox/release/workflow.py::prepare_public_release` (whitelist iteration
   via `_copy_root_files` + `_copy_sources_selective`) - used by
   `scripts/prepare_release.py`, which `automate_release.py` calls during a
   release.

Both consult the same constants (`HOLD_BACK_PATHS`, `ALLOWED_ROOT_FILES`,
`_SOURCES_INCLUDE_PATHS`, `DOCS_DIR_EXCLUDES`, `TESTS_DIR_EXCLUDES`,
`GLOBAL_EXCLUDES`, `FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS`, `ALLOWED_DATA_PATHS`) but combine them
through different control flow. If they ever drift, a release can ship a file
that `benchbox-sync status` reports as in-sync, or vice versa.

Goal: extract a single `is_public_path(rel_path: Path) -> bool` predicate as
the source of truth for inclusion. Both code paths consult it. The predicate
is orthogonal to `should_transform` (content rewrites) and `CLEANUP_PATTERNS`
(post-copy cleanup) - those remain separate concerns.

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/make-a-detailed-and-dynamic-bentley.md
(Phase A).
preserves: Existing tests in `tests/unit/release/test_release_sync_unit.py` and `tests/unit/test_release_exclusion_invariants.py` pass without modification.
Sync subcommand behaviour - `benchbox-sync status`, `push`, `pull` produce identical output before and after the refactor for a given source/target pair.
The `CLEANUP_PATTERNS` post-copy cleanup behaviour is unchanged. Files like .venv, .ruff_cache, node_modules continue to be stripped after copy.

The existing public-vs-private file boundary - no file currently shipped to public should be added to or removed from the public tree by this refactor. The tree-diff regression check (w5) is the load-bearing assertion.

The functions `should_transform` and `apply_transform` remain orthogonal to inclusion. Files that get transformed today must still get transformed (e.g., pyproject.toml, .gitignore, benchbox/cli/commands/__init__.py, .github/workflows/test.yml, pytest.ini, pytest-ci.ini).

description:
pandas 3.0.2 is available on PyPI but cannot be safely bumped yet.
A compatibility evaluation (2026-04-22) found two hard blockers that must
clear before the actual lock bump begins, plus two targeted code fixes needed before
the lock bump lands.

── HARD BLOCKERS (do not proceed until both are resolved) ──────────────────

1. modin 0.37.1 requires `pandas<2.4,>=2.2`.
   `uv lock --upgrade-package pandas` fails to resolve because modin's upper
   bound (`<2.4`) and pandas 3.x are mutually exclusive. No modin release
   beyond 0.37.1 exists as of 2026-04-22 that relaxes this cap. Modin is a
   first-class BenchBox platform (benchbox/platforms/dataframe/modin_df.py,
   extras modin / dataframe-pandas-family / all) - silently excluding it
   from the resolved environment is not acceptable.
   Watch: https://github.com/modin-project/modin/releases

2. pandas 3.0 requires Python ≥ 3.11.
   BenchBox declares `requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.15"`. Bumping pandas
   would silently break Python 3.10 users. Either (a) raise the project
   minimum to 3.11 (requires a separate decision and full CI matrix change)
   or (b) confirm that pandas can remain at 2.x for Python 3.10 via
   environment markers - and verify uv resolves that correctly.

── PRE-FLIGHT CODE FIXES (required before lock bump, no behaviour change) ──

3. pandas_df.py:145-155 - `pd.options.mode.copy_on_write` assignment.
   In pandas 3.0 this option is deprecated and a no-op. The current code
   sets it unconditionally (guarded only by `pandas_version >= (2, 0)`).
   Fix: add an upper guard `pandas_version < (3, 0)` so the assignment is
   skipped on 3.x where CoW is always active.

4. TPC-DI ingest datetime resolution.
   pandas 3.0 defaults to microsecond resolution for datetime parsing
   (vs. nanoseconds in 2.x). Any remaining code in `tpcdi/benchmark.py` that
   reads or normalizes date/time values via pd.read_csv / pd.read_fwf /
   pd.read_json / pd.to_datetime and then converts to int64 or compares
   values numerically can produce 1000× different results under 3.x. Audit and add
   explicit `dtype_backend`, `parse_dates=False`, or explicit resolution
   normalization where the downstream code is resolution-sensitive. (CoW
   in-place mutation audit was clean - no fixes needed there.)

── EVALUATION SUMMARY ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Evaluated 2026-04-22. pandas 3.x breaking changes cross-referenced against
BenchBox codebase:
- DataFrame.swapaxes / append / Index.format() - not used, no impact.
- groupby/resample keyword changes - not used in DataFrame platform layer.
- datetime-unit changes in read/normalize paths - affects the remaining
  TPC-DI benchmark ingest path only (item 4).
- CoW mandatory - in-place mutation audit clean; only item 3 needs a guard.
Estimated effort once gates clear: 1-2 days.
preserves: Fast test suite baseline: currently 19 pre-existing failures - bump must not add new failures
Python 3.10 users either still supported (via marker) or explicitly told the minimum raised
TPC-DI date/time correctness - no silent 1000x resolution change in datetime → int conversions
modin platform fully functional after bump (benchbox run --platform modin-df --benchmark tpch works)

anti_patterns.instead: use filename-based ABI check which costs < 1ms
anti_patterns.why: DuckDB import takes 50-200ms and discovery may scan many candidates

approach:
Minimal-surface fix inside discover_isolated_runtime() in runtime_env.py.

The cheapest reliable check for ABI compatibility is inspecting the filenames of
compiled extensions in site-packages. Python C extensions follow a naming convention:
`module.cpython-3XX-<platform>.so` (or `.pyd` on Windows). The current interpreter's
expected suffix is available from `sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')` or
`importlib.machinery.EXTENSION_SUFFIXES`.

Strategy:
1. After metadata version match (line 151), scan the package directory under
   site-packages for .so/.pyd files.
2. If extension files exist, check if any match the current Python's ABI tag.
3. If none match → skip this candidate (log warning, continue loop).
4. If no extension files exist → pure Python package, accept it.
5. This avoids the cost of a full import for the common case.

Use `importlib.machinery.EXTENSION_SUFFIXES` which gives the list of valid extension
suffixes for the running interpreter (e.g., ['.cpython-310-darwin.so', '.abi3.so', '.so']).

deferrals.reason: Destructive file operations on user's disk should require explicit opt-in. Warning + skip + fallthrough to auto-install is the safe default. Can revisit with a --force-rebuild flag if users want automatic cleanup.

deferrals.reason: ABI mismatch is the dominant failure mode. Full integrity checking adds complexity for a less common scenario. Can add later if needed.

description:
Bug discovered on 2026-02-24: `driver_auto_install=true` silently fails when a
corrupted isolated runtime exists on disk. The root cause is a two-layer failure:

Layer 1 - Discovery short-circuits auto-install:
In runtime_env.py lines 340-355, `discover_isolated_runtime()` runs before any
auto-install logic. If it finds a metadata match, it returns immediately and
auto-install is never reached. A broken isolated runtime at
`benchmark_runs/duckdb_version_envs/duckdb-1.2.2/` was discovered via
`importlib.metadata` (which only reads `.dist-info/METADATA` files - no actual
module import), so the metadata check passed and the corrupted runtime was returned.

Layer 2 - Python ABI mismatch makes the runtime unusable:
The DuckDB 1.2.2 C extension was installed under Python 3.12
(`duckdb.cpython-312-darwin.so`) but BenchBox was running under Python 3.10.
Python 3.10 cannot load a 3.12 C extension, causing
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'duckdb.duckdb'` at import time.

The downstream `load_driver_module()` (line 184) does perform an actual import and
path validation, but by the time it runs the damage is done: `ensure_driver_version()`
already returned a resolution claiming the runtime is valid, and the error surfaces
as an opaque import failure rather than a clear "stale/incompatible runtime" message
with recovery guidance.

The fix: `discover_isolated_runtime()` must validate that a candidate runtime is
actually importable (not just metadata-present) before treating it as a cache hit.
When validation fails, the candidate should be skipped (allowing auto-install to
proceed) and a warning should be logged.
preserves: Default runs without explicit requested version continue working unchanged
Existing test_discover_isolated_runtime_finds_matching_version and test_ensure_driver_version_prefers_isolated_runtime continue to pass
discover_isolated_runtime() returns immediately for valid runtimes with no measurable performance regression (< 5ms overhead per candidate)
ensure_driver_version() auto-install path still works when no isolated runtime exists
load_driver_module() import validation and _module_is_from_runtime() check remain unchanged as a second safety layer
title: Validate isolated runtime importability before treating as cache hit

and benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py are CODEOWNERS-covered;

The comparator behind the cross-surface gates reports only the FIRST
positional mismatch per row: both "Value mismatch at row {i}, column {j}"
emit sites in benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py (:454 and :674) break
out after the first differing column. PR #952's waiver-tightening work
(read-primitives-waivers-classified-divergence) made every waiver a
column-pinned predicate and, in doing so, documented the residual limit
honestly (cross_surface.py, min_by_complex waiver comment): if an ACCEPTED
column (e.g. the ARG_MIN tie-broken cheapest_part_name, column 1) differs
on the same row where a NON-waived column (min_price, column 3) is ALSO
wrong, only the accepted column-1 mismatch is visible, the predicate
accepts it, and the real regression rides through classified-green. The
h2odb Q9 waiver carries the same shape ("validator-imposed" blind spot).
Column-pinning minimized but structurally cannot close this; the fix is in
the validator's reporting, not in more predicate work.

that row (bounded output — indices always, per-column values capped) and
surface them in the divergence detail. Then tighten the waiver contract:
a ClassifiedDivergence predicate accepts only if EVERY mismatched column
on the row is within its accepted set, so "waived column diverged AND
unwaived column diverged" is unclassified (gate failure) instead of
invisibly green.

description:
SOUNDNESS-CRITICAL COMPARATOR SURFACE: this TODO's work is in
benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py, covered by .github/CODEOWNERS
(`benchbox/core/**/validation.py @joeharris76`). Its PR will require
code-owner review before merge regardless of CI status.

Verified by reading benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py on this branch:
`calculate_checksum` (lines 20-48) builds its digest input by, for each row
(sorted via the None-safe `_row_sort_key`), joining cells with `"|"` and then
joining rows with `"\n"`, over `str(val) if val is not None else "NULL"`
(line 45: `row_str = "|".join(str(val) if val is not None else "NULL" for val in row)`,
line 46: `result_str += row_str + "\n"`). This is a plain string-concatenation
digest with no escaping of the separator characters themselves, and no
type tag on each rendered cell.

Three collisions, each empirically verified by construction (the join/render
logic is inspectable directly - these are not hypothetical):
  1. Separator collision across cells: `[("a|b", "c")]` and `[("a", "b|c")]`
     both render to the row string `"a|b|c"` (the first as `"a|b" + "|" + "c"`,
     the second as `"a" + "|" + "b|c"`), so `calculate_checksum` returns the
     SAME digest for two DIFFERENT 2-column, 1-row result sets.
  2. Separator collision across rows: `[("a\nb",)]` (one row, one cell
     containing a literal newline) and `[("a",), ("b",)]` (two rows) both
     render to `"a\nb\n"`, so a single-row result with an embedded newline
     collides with a genuinely different two-row result.
  3. Type collision: `[("1",)]` (a string cell) and `[(1,)]` (an int cell)
     both render via `str(val)` to `"1"`, so a dtype REGRESSION (e.g. a column
     that should be INTEGER silently becoming VARCHAR after a schema/loader
     change) is INVISIBLE to this digest - the checksum is identical whether
     the cell is the string `"1"` or the int `1`.

The codebase has already accepted one collision in this same family as a
documented, pinned property rather than a bug: the NULL-vs-string-"NULL"
collision, at
tests/unit/core/tpchavoc/test_tpchavoc_validation_coverage.py:133-141
(`test_calculate_checksum_collides_null_with_string_null`, verified present
on this branch: `assert calculate_checksum([(None,)]) == calculate_checksum([("NULL",)])`,
with a docstring calling it "the one ambiguity of the str-rendering primitive
... accepted property ... pinned so a future change is a conscious one"). This
TODO extends that same discipline to the three collisions above, which the
NULL-vs-"NULL" test did not cover.

This digest is used by BOTH `ResultValidator.validate_results_checksum` (the
TPC-Havoc comparator) AND the bounded correctness gate's value-digest oracle
(per the module docstring at validation.py:23-28: "backs both the TPC-Havoc
equivalence comparators ... and the bounded correctness gate's value-digest
oracle, so SQL results and the gate share exactly one digest definition"),
and the committed reference file
benchbox/core/expected_results/reference_digests/tpch_value_digests_sf1.json
is generated FROM this function via `make correctness-gate-digests-regen`
(Makefile:159-160, confirmed present). Any separator change to
`calculate_checksum` therefore invalidates that committed reference and
requires regeneration through the make target - never a hand-edit.
preserves: The existing NULL-vs-string-'NULL' pin (test_calculate_checksum_collides_null_with_string_null) continues to pass unless w1 explicitly decides to fix that collision too (out of scope here - only the three NEW collisions this review found are in scope, though noting the parallel is fine).

calculate_checksum's ORDER-NORMALIZATION behavior (rows sorted via _row_sort_key before hashing) and its None-safe sort surrogate are unchanged unless w1 explicitly decides to touch them - this TODO is about the join/render separator and type-rendering, not the sort key.
tph_value_digests_sf1.json is only ever regenerated via `make correctness-gate-digests-regen`, never hand-edited.

default for this batch, applied here after independently confirming it is

full - do not change calculate_checksum's join/render logic. Rationale,
including the w1 open_question's caller audit:
  - Callers audited: `ResultValidator.validate_results_checksum`'s only
    caller is `TPCHavocBenchmark.validate_variant_equivalence`
    (benchbox/core/tpchavoc/benchmark.py:282); the correctness-gate
    value-digest oracle path is `compute_result_digest` ->
    `calculate_checksum` via `benchbox/core/results/result_digest.py`.
    Neither path, nor anything else found searching the repo, independently
    verifies cell DTYPE on the paths this digest guards - a str-vs-int
    dtype regression is a real, currently-uncaught blind spot from this
    digest ALONE.
  - However, `result_digest._normalize_cell` already documents (and pins
    in tests/unit/test_correctness_gate_value_oracle.py::
    test_digest_couples_value_with_numeric_type) a closely analogous
    accepted asymmetry: an int and a float/Decimal of the SAME numeric
    value render DIFFERENTLY (int exact vs. float to N sig figs) purely
    because the oracle is DuckDB-pinned and single-engine by design (see
    _project/analysis/value-digest-cross-engine-independence-decision.md).
    The str-vs-int collision here is the SAME class of accepted risk for
    the SAME underlying reason (a single-engine, DuckDB-pinned regression
    snapshot, not an independent correctness oracle) - fixing it would
    require a type-tagged/escaped re-render of every cell, which changes
    the digest for every existing row and forces a regeneration of
    tpch_value_digests_sf1.json. That regeneration is real, auditable work
    (must re-run the full SF=1 gate via `make correctness-gate-digests-regen`
    and re-verify two-run determinism) that is out of safe scope for a
    pin-only batch item - it is exactly the kind of change the TODO's own
    anti_patterns flag as needing to land in the SAME reviewed change as
    the render fix, not bundled opportunistically here.
  - The two separator collisions (cross-cell `|`, cross-row `\n`) are
    cosmetic string-join artifacts with no analogous type-fidelity
    argument for fixing now; pinning them matches the existing
    NULL-vs-"NULL" precedent exactly.
Net: all three pinned as accepted properties this batch; the type
collision is flagged above as the one worth a FUTURE follow-up TODO if a
real dtype-regression incident on this digest's guarded paths is ever
observed (deferred, not silently dropped).

anti_patterns.instead: direct macOS/Windows developers to the Docker workflow in docker/velox/ instead.
anti_patterns.why: upstream does not support or test this path (see apache/incubator-gluten #5006, #5491) and any local success would diverge from published benchmark numbers

anti_patterns.dont: auto-download the Gluten bundle jar inside the adapter
anti_patterns.instead: require the user to supply `gluten_jar_path` (or pre-stage via an explicit, documented CLI command).
anti_patterns.why: silent network fetches during benchmark runs are a supply-chain and reproducibility hazard

anti_patterns.dont: edit benchbox/platforms/lakesail.py or benchbox/platforms/spark.py
anti_patterns.instead: all new code lives in velox.py and the small registration deltas in __init__.py / dependencies.py.
anti_patterns.why: Velox is additive and those adapters must remain byte-identical to avoid regressing existing benchmarks

anti_patterns.dont: have the adapter call out to `docker` / manage container lifecycle
anti_patterns.instead: treat Docker as user-operated infrastructure (like a Spark cluster), documented in docker/velox/README .md, and have the adapter speak only to an already-running endpoint or in-process SparkSession.
anti_patterns.why: coupling benchmark runs to an implicit Docker daemon hides failure modes and confuses CI

anti_patterns.dont: pin pyspark to a version outside the Gluten-supported set (3.2.2 / 3.3.1 / 3.4.4 / 3.5.5 as of 1.4.x)
anti_patterns.instead: expose `gluten_version` and validate pyspark version matches on session creation.
anti_patterns.why: the native bundle is ABI-coupled to the Spark minor version

anti_patterns.dont: require Velox jar for unit tests
anti_patterns.instead: mock SparkSession and gate live integration tests behind the `live_integration` + Linux markers.
anti_patterns.why: CI runners don't have the ~150MB native bundle and may not be Linux

anti_patterns.dont: run the Docker image under Rosetta or qemu emulation when the host arch differs from the image arch
anti_patterns.instead: ship multi-arch images (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) via docker buildx and fail fast with a clear warning if the adapter detects emulation at session startup.
anti_patterns.why: emulated SIMD / off-heap allocation destroys timing fidelity (this is the whole point of Velox)

anti_patterns.dont: silently omit spark.shuffle.manager=ColumnarShuffleManager
anti_patterns.instead: fail fast with a clear error if the user overrides it to a non-columnar value while deployment=local.
anti_patterns.why: forgetting it forfeits most of the Velox shuffle speedup and produces misleading benchmark numbers

anti_patterns.dont: subclass LakeSailAdapter or SparkAdapter
anti_patterns.instead: create a new VeloxAdapter that reuses the Spark mixins directly, following the LakeSail file as a structural template.
anti_patterns.why: Velox is a distinct deployment shape with required conf that would leak into those adapters if inherited

approach:
Follow the LakeSail adapter as the structural template, and the
Apache Spark adapter for local-mode session construction. Concretely:

  1. New file benchbox/platforms/velox.py defines VeloxAdapter
     inheriting (SparkDataLoadMixin, SparkQueryExecutionMixin,
     PlatformAdapter), mirroring LakeSail's class layout.

  2. Two deployment modes via a `deployment` config field:
       - "local":   builds a SparkSession (classic or Spark-Connect via
                    pysail-style in-process server is NOT applicable
                    here; use pyspark.sql.SparkSession.builder.master
                    'local[*]'). Adds Gluten jar to spark.jars and
                    classpath, sets plugin + off-heap + columnar shuffle.
       - "remote":  treats the endpoint as a pre-configured Spark-Connect
                    server (mirror LakeSail _parse_endpoint / _is_server
                    _reachable). Does NOT auto-start a server.

  3. Config knobs (CLI + --platform-option):
       deployment        = local | remote          (default local)
       endpoint          = sc://host:port          (remote only)
       gluten_jar_path   = /abs/path/to/bundle.jar (local only; required)
       gluten_version    = 1.4.0                    (informational; surfaced in platform_info)
       offheap_size      = 8g                       (default conservative)
       shuffle_partitions, adaptive_enabled, driver_memory, app_name,
       table_format, spark_config, disable_cache     (identical to LakeSail)

  4. `_get_spark_conf()` merges LakeSail-style base conf with Gluten-
     mandatory keys; in remote mode the conf is advisory (the server
     already has it - send only what Spark-Connect respects).

  5. `_create_spark_session()`:
       - local:  SparkSession.builder.master('local[*]')
                   .config('spark.plugins', 'org.apache.gluten.GlutenPlugin')
                   .config('spark.jars', gluten_jar_path)
                   .config('spark.driver.extraClassPath', gluten_jar_path)
                   .config('spark.executor.extraClassPath', gluten_jar_path)
                   .config('spark.memory.offHeap.enabled', 'true')
                   .config('spark.memory.offHeap.size', offheap_size)
                   .config('spark.shuffle.manager',
                           'org.apache.spark.shuffle.sort.ColumnarShuffleManager')
                   .getOrCreate()
       - remote: SparkSession.builder.remote(endpoint) + conf overlay.

  6. `get_platform_info()` reports: deployment mode, gluten_version,
     gluten_jar_path (redacted), offheap_size, Spark version, PySpark
     version, and (best-effort) backend fingerprint:
       - EXPLAIN a trivial query, look for 'VeloxColumnar' nodes to
         confirm Velox is actually active; store `velox_active: bool`.

  7. Query plan capture (`get_query_plan`) uses EXPLAIN EXTENDED (as
     LakeSail does) and additionally greps for Velox columnar nodes so
     the get_query_plan MCP tool can show native-vs-fallback.

  8. Fallback telemetry (stretch, in w-series): hook into Spark logs
     or Gluten metrics (SparkListener) to count JVM-fallback
     operators per query and attach to BenchmarkResults query metadata.

  9. Dependency + registry wiring (four touchpoints, mirroring LakeSail):
       - pyproject.toml extra "velox" pins pyspark==3.5.x (matching the
         bundle jar); the jar itself is NOT packaged.
       - utils/dependencies.py adds DependencyInfo("velox", ...) with
         packages=["pyspark"] and an extra `external_artifacts` note
         pointing to docs/platforms/velox_jar_setup.md.
       - platforms/__init__.py: register "VeloxAdapter" in the lazy
         adapter map (mirroring the "LakeSailAdapter" entry at line 89),
         add "velox" (and optional "gluten-velox") to the platform-name
         lookup, add availability constant entry for
         list_available_platforms().
       - platforms/adapter_factory.py: register the Velox dispatch entry
         so get_platform_adapter("velox", **config) resolves.
       - At the bottom of velox.py, define `_build_velox_config` and
         call PlatformHookRegistry.register_config_builder("velox", ...)
         exactly as LakeSail does (credential loading, driver_package
         = "pyspark", platform_fields listing Velox-specific knobs).

 10. Jar provisioning helper (small utility in benchbox/platforms/velox
     or a scripts/ helper): given gluten_version + spark_version + arch,
     prints the canonical jar URL (Apache dist mirror) and checksum.
     Do NOT auto-download during benchmark runs (supply-chain risk);
     provide an opt-in `benchbox fetch-velox-jar` CLI later if demanded.

 11. Docker-based local dev + CI path (primary workflow on macOS/Windows,
     recommended on Linux):

       docker/velox/Dockerfile
         FROM apache/spark:3.5.2-scala2.12-java17-python3-ubuntu
         ARG GLUTEN_VERSION=1.4.0
         ARG TARGETARCH        # amd64 | arm64 (inferred by buildx)
         RUN curl -fsSL ${APACHE_MIRROR}/gluten/${GLUTEN_VERSION}/\
             gluten-velox-bundle-spark3.5_2.12-linux_${TARGETARCH}-${GLUTEN_VERSION}.jar \
             -o /opt/gluten.jar
         COPY --chown=spark:spark . /opt/benchbox
         RUN pip install -e /opt/benchbox[velox]
         COPY docker/velox/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
         ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]

       docker/velox/docker-compose.yml defines two services:
         - 'velox-connect': starts Spark-Connect server on :50051 with
           Gluten conf, for adapter-only dev from the host.
         - 'velox-runner':  runs `benchbox run --platform velox …`
           end-to-end inside the container, for one-shot benchmarks
           and CI.

       Build and publish multi-arch images via `docker buildx build
       --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` so Apple Silicon and Intel
       developers get native execution.

       The adapter code DOES NOT manage Docker lifecycle - that is the
       user's responsibility via `docker compose up`. The adapter only
       needs to (a) accept a `sc://localhost:50051` endpoint, and
       (b) document the Docker path prominently.

 12. Validation strategy for first PR: run TPC-H Q1, Q6, Q3, Q9 at
     SF 0.01 under local mode *inside* the Docker image on both
     linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 runners (matrix), assert
     'VeloxColumnar' nodes appear in EXPLAIN for at least Q1/Q6.
     This becomes the single live_integration test; all other tests
     use mocked pyspark like existing LakeSail tests.

description:
Add a BenchBox platform adapter for Apache Gluten with the Velox backend -
a plugin to Apache Spark that offloads physical operators to a highly
optimized native C++ engine (Velox) while preserving Spark's fault
tolerance, distributed scheduling, and DataFrame/SQL APIs.

Unlike LakeSail (a standalone Rust/DataFusion Spark-Connect server),
Gluten+Velox runs *inside* Apache Spark via jar + plugin configuration.
From a client perspective, a Gluten-accelerated Spark cluster still speaks
standard Spark (Connect or classic) - the acceleration is invisible to the
application. The adapter's job is therefore primarily to:

  1. Own the lifecycle of a Gluten-enabled SparkSession / Spark-Connect
     server (jars on the classpath, required conf set, off-heap memory).
  2. Expose Gluten/Velox-specific configuration knobs as CLI options.
  3. Capture native-execution metadata (backend = Velox vs. JVM fallback)
     in platform info and query plans.
  4. Reuse all Spark load/query/tuning plumbing already proven on
     LakeSail and Apache Spark adapters.

Reference performance: TPC-H ~3.3x overall / up to ~23x on individual
queries, TPC-DS ~3x overall / up to ~13.7x on individual queries (Gluten
community numbers, March 2024). This makes Velox a natural fit next to
LakeSail, Photon-backed Databricks, and Fabric native acceleration in
BenchBox's "accelerated Spark" tier.

Upstream references:
  - https://gluten.apache.org/
  - https://github.com/apache/gluten (ASF Top-Level Project since Feb 2026)
  - https://velox-lib.io/
  - https://apache.github.io/incubator-gluten/get-started/Velox.html

`results-explorer/src/lib/duckdbBundles.ts` imports the worker and WASM
assets directly from the installed npm package via Vite `?url` imports,

loads and the browser-functional harness without introducing a separate
committed vendor directory. Because the browser now imports assets from
the installed package at build time, there is no duplicated byte copy to
desync from `package-lock.json`.

approach:
This is a CI-governance change, not application code. Add one step to
validate-submission.yml (the published-results submission gate): compute the
base...HEAD diff filtered to results-data/bundles/vendor/, and if non-empty AND
github.event.pull_request.author_association is not OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR,
emit ::error:: and exit 1. author_association is set by GitHub from the actor's
relationship to the repo and is not controllable by PR content; fork PRs (how
community contributors submit) run the base-branch workflow copy, so the gate
cannot be edited away in the same PR. Add a lightweight test asserting the step
is present. The workflow reaches published-results via the existing mirror.
description:
The vendor-supplied trust label is RANKING-ELIGIBLE (D2) and is derived purely
from a bundle living under the top-level `results-data/bundles/vendor/` subtree
(generate_corpus_inventory.py::_is_vendor_subtree and
explorer_pipeline/pipeline.py::_is_vendor_subtree). The submission validator
only rejects a bundle that self-asserts result_source=vendor OUTSIDE that path;
it does NOT stop a contributor who simply drops a file INTO vendor/. So the only
real control is a review gate on WHO may add under vendor/.

Branch reframing (2026-07-07): community/vendor submissions PR to
`published-results` (submit.py:82, contributing-results.md:79), validated by
.github/workflows/validate-submission.yml. The develop-only
SOUNDNESS_PREFIXES/auto-merge-on-open machinery does NOT govern that branch, so
the original "add vendor/ to SOUNDNESS_PREFIXES + develop CODEOWNERS" idea gates
the WRONG branch (it would only cover maintainer-added bundles on develop, the
low-risk actor). The gate belongs on published-results, on the submission-PR
path itself.

deferrals.reason: Sweep result with lint --include-done across 1626 items: exactly 2 unsatisfiable rungs remain -- results-explorer-qa-pass2-fixes seq 8 ('Page renders the NotFound component, not DOES-NOT-EXIST Results' with command 'open http://...', which always exits 0) and timing-policy-check-misreports-pytest-failure-as-violation seq 1 (expects output while the correct behaviour is a non-zero exit). BOTH are on state=done items. They cannot be fixed: verifications are create-time-only in this wrapper, the update verb is standalone-only (todo-db >= 0.3, see adopt-todo-db-standalone-cli-for-amendable-items), and amending a finished item is refused by design anyway -- a done record is history. So the sweep's repair half is not actionable until the adoption item lands, and even then amending done items is a separate policy question. Also correcting the record: PR #1311's body claimed this rule flags '8 of 2958 (0.27%)'. That figure came from a DRAFT regex in my calibration script, not from the rule that shipped. The shipped _EXPECTED_NEGATES_OUTPUT_RE binds 'must not' to an output verb (print|contain|report|emit|include|output|show) and has no 'rather than'/'instead of' alternations, so it flags 2, not 8. The narrower rule is the correct one -- 'must not fail with X' and 'instead of failing setup' ARE expressible by exit code, so the extra 6 were false positives -- but the published number was measured against code that was never merged.
deferrals.resolved_reason: Recorded as the sweep's finding rather than as further work. The 2 remaining rungs are on done items, which are immutable by design ('a finished item is history'), so there is nothing to schedule: repair depends entirely on adopt-todo-db-standalone-cli-for-amendable-items, which is already tracked, plus a separate policy call on whether done items may ever be amended. The corrected flag count (2, not the 8 published in PR #1311) is captured here and in this item's PR body so the number is not left wrong in the record.
deferrals.summary: The 2 rungs the sweep found sit on done items and cannot be repaired by any current mechanism

description: Two confirmed instances of the same defect: a verification command that can never pass regardless of implementation. (1) medium-test-timeout-headroom rung 1: 'grep -A1 medium-test .github/workflows/pr.yml | grep timeout-minutes' -- timeout-minutes sits 5+ lines below the match so -A1 never reaches it; verified failing against the ORIGINAL unmodified file by git-stashing all changes. It is also self-contradictory, since its expectation demands an inline comment and adding one pushes the value further from the match. (2) timing-policy-check-misreports-pytest-failure-as-violation rung 1: expects output ('reports a tooling/environment error') but todo verify grades only on exit code (todo_db.py:1809), and the correct behaviour there is a NON-ZERO exit. Root cause is shared with todo-verify-grades-only-on-exit-code: nothing checks that a rung's command actually encodes its expectation, and verifications are create-time-only so a bad rung can never be repaired. Sweep the corpus (2968 verifications across 1587 items) for rungs whose command is a bare grep/invocation while the expectation is negative or output-shaped, and fix the authoring guidance so commands are self-asserting (exit 0 iff satisfied).
